## 1. Game loop architecture

*Source: [game-loop-architecture.md](game-loop-architecture.md). The overall flow of the game. Short, and reworked if the loop changes (not expected).*

Solid Carbide is played in 8-minute runs. The player only drives: drifting earns XP, each level-up brings a weapon choice, weapons fire on their own at the enemies swarming in, and enemies drop coins. At 7 minutes the kaiju arrives, and the player has the last 60 seconds to defeat it; it can be damaged at any time. Between runs, the player is back at the main menu, where the Garage spends coins on permanent car upgrades, and Start begins the next run.

### Decisions

- A run lasts 8 minutes.
- The player only drives. The car's weapons fire automatically.
- Enemies come in from the edges of the screen, in numbers that grow over the run (how they scale: Enemies, Decisions).
- XP comes only from driving, never from kills. In the MVP it comes from drifting only, since challenges are left out of the MVP (Level design, Decisions); if they come back, completed challenges give XP too.
- **Combo:** tricks (Drifting, Decisions) raise a combo multiplier, and the multiplier multiplies all XP gained (from challenges and from drifting). Each trick adds to the multiplier: extended drifts a little, a 360 more, an alternate drift the most. Colliding with anything, enemies included, cuts the combo by 50%. If no trick follows within 2 seconds, the combo drains away quickly. The Game Data Agent proposes the numbers; the board judges them in playtests. The XP from drifting seconds stays as it is, alongside the extended-drift trick. Part of the MVP.
- The higher the combo, the more enemies spawn (how: Enemies, Decisions). The board will judge in playtests whether to keep this.
- A drift that lasts longer than 1 second gives XP for every second it lasts, the first second included (a 3-second drift gives 3 seconds' worth).
- Each second of drifting gives a fixed amount of XP: 10% of the XP bar at level 1. The amount does not grow with the bar, so at higher levels it is a smaller share of the bar and drifting gives only a little XP.
- **Likes drain:** when the player isn't doing tricks, the likes bar empties, but never below the start of the current level, so the player never loses a level. It starts once the combo has fully drained, and any trick stops it. The speed is the board's playtest value, 8% of the current level's bar a second (four times the first proposal; the number: [game/data/run.json](../game/data/run.json)). Part of the MVP.
- "Drifting", for XP, uses the Unity prototype's definition: any moment W or S is held together with A or D (Unity prototype report, section 3).
- After the MVP, if challenges come back (2026-10-11): at level 1, completing one challenge fills the XP bar: the player reaches level 2 and gets the weapon choice.
- How much XP challenges and drifting give at each level, and how much XP each level needs, is worked out by the Game Data Agent as sensible XP scaling, within the decisions here.
- The weapon choice opens only when the XP bar fills and the player levels up (how many weapons are offered: Weapons, Decisions). The weapons chosen reset at the start of every run.
- **Gift pack drop** (board, 2026-10-16; tasks T-144 to T-146): the level-up screen no longer just appears. When the player levels up, a helicopter sent by Greenbull (first Redgull) flies over the screen and drops a package carrying Greenbull's brand (the gift pack). When the player drives over the package, the level-up screen (the gift pack screen) opens. The look of the helicopter and the package: Visual style, Decisions. The run keeps going while the helicopter comes and the package waits; it pauses only when the screen opens. The package lands a short way ahead of the car, on open road, and stays until picked up. One package per level-up, each opening its own screen. When a landed package is off screen, an arrow at the screen edge points to it.
- **A falling gift pack shows its shadow** (board, 2026-10-30): while the gift pack falls, a shadow on the ground (or the platform) where it will land shows the player where it is coming down, the same shadow the car casts when it is in the air. (T-407)
- After the MVP, if challenges come back (2026-10-11): completing a challenge flashes a score, the likes it gave, and gives XP.
- Enemies drop coins. The coins collected in a run are kept whether the run is won or lost.
- At the 7-minute mark the kaiju spawns. It moves slowly toward the player, deals contact damage, and can be damaged at any time (Enemies, Decisions).
- Win: defeat the kaiju within the final 60 seconds. Loss: the car's HP reaches 0 at any point, or the kaiju survives the timer.
- Between runs, coins are spent in the Garage on permanent car upgrades that improve the car in the next run (which upgrades: Garage design, Decisions).
- The game opens on a main menu with three buttons: Start (begins a run), Garage, and Exit. When a run ends, win or loss, the player returns to the main menu (through the recap screen, below).
- The final release adds a recap screen right after a run ends, win or loss: how many of each enemy type the player killed, and other stats the board will choose (task T-017). In the MVP there is no recap: the run ends at the main menu.
- The final release adds local co-op for 2 players (screen split in halves) and 4 players (screen split in quarters). The MVP is single-player.
- **Music** (board, 2026-10-20): the board's own two tracks, "DEMO BEAT 1 (ANDY GAME)" and "DEMO BEAT 2 (ANDY GAME)" (made by the board; the music is human-made), play through the whole game, menus and runs alike, without stopping between screens: one track, then the other, alternating and looping. Its volume is the pause screen's music volume slider (HUD and menus, Decisions). Built in T-209: one music player, a child of the game flow, so the screens changing never restarts it; it plays on its own "Music" bus, and the setting is `music_volume` in `game_settings.gd` (0 to 100, saved with the SFX volume, starting at 40 as a proposal for the playtest). (tasks T-209, T-210)
- **Pickup magnet** (board, 2026-10-21): coins, level-up gift packs and health drops are pulled towards the car once they are within a radius of 1 car length, so they are easier to pick up. The radius is a garage upgrade (Garage design, Decisions). Built in T-222: the radius is 3 units (the car is drawn 3 units long, Drifting, Decisions), read from `run.json`'s `pickup_magnet`, and pickups fly to the car at 30 units per second (proposals for the playtest: the pull speed, and the reach measured on the flat map); since T-402 it pulls only pickups on the level the car is on (the ground under the car), so nothing is pulled up or down a rooftop's wall, and a pulled pickup is drawn at the height of the ground it crosses (proposal for the playtest); `game/docs/game-loop/gift-pack-and-pickups.md`, "The pickup magnet (T-222)". (T-222)
- **An arrow for every gift pack on the map** (board, 2026-10-28): every gift pack on the map gets its own arrow, the same arrow that today points at a landed package off screen, so several arrows show when several packages are out. (T-314)
- **A crash pays the trick in progress** (board, 2026-10-28): when a crash breaks the combo, the player still gets the trick they were doing up to that moment (a drift pays for the time it lasted), instead of losing it. (T-315)
- **Time's up screen** (board, 2026-10-28): when the 8-minute timer runs out (the kaiju survived it, a loss), a 3-second animated failure screen plays before the run ends. Its text: HUD and menus, Content (T-316). (T-317)
- **Recap screen in the MVP** (board, 2026-10-28; replaces "In the MVP there is no recap" above): after a run ends, the player sees a recap of the run: the enemies slain, the tricks completed, the highest combo multiplier reached and the weapons used, each shown with pictures where it can be (the enemies' and weapons' own art). Its text: HUD and menus, Content (T-318). (T-319, T-320)
- **Wrecked: the stream keeps rolling** (board, 2026-10-29; replaces the time's up screen's proposal that losing all health ends the run as before): when the car loses its last heart, the run doesn't end at once. The controls go dead, the car keeps whatever movement it had and slides or rolls to a stop, and it sits there crashed, smoking and burning (pixel art smoke and flames), for **3 seconds**, with the stream (the HUD, the live viewers) still on screen. It is like the end of a stream that doesn't cut away. Then the recap screen shows. No text. (T-360, T-361)
- **A health pickup revives a wrecked car** (board, 2026-10-30): while the car is wrecked and still sliding, if it comes within a health pickup's pickup range (its magnet), it picks it up and comes back with **1 heart**: the controls return, the smoke and flames stop and the run goes on; the recap does not show. Whether the usual 1-second invulnerability follows, and what happens to the combo and the live viewers, are proposals for the playtest. (T-406)
- **The recap always closes a run** (board, 2026-10-29): every run ends on the recap screen (a win, the time's up screen, the wreck), and the player leaves it with a Continue button or an X at the top right, both to the main menu. (T-320)
- **The runs list** (board, 2026-10-29): each run's recap stats are saved on this computer, and a new button on the main menu opens a list of the player's past runs. Its text: HUD and menus, Content (T-362). (T-363, T-364)
- **More gift packs, earlier** (board, 2026-10-28): the early levels need fewer likes, so the first gift packs come more often at the start of a run. The new curve is the Game Data Agent's proposal for the playtest, built in T-328: 30, 45, 65, 95, 140, 200, 290, 400, 560, 745 and 931 likes for levels 2 to 12 (total 3,501, was 4,255); the table and reasons are in Content, "Likes and levels". (T-328)
- **A crash cuts the combo by 50%** (board, 2026-10-28; replaces the 80% in "Combo" above): a collision or any damage to the car cuts the part of the multiplier above "no combo" by 50% instead of 80%, so the player keeps half of their combo bonus (x4 becomes x2.5). (T-329)
- **A bigger gift pack helicopter** (board, 2026-10-28): the helicopter that drops each gift pack is drawn 30% larger on screen than today (about 125 x 104 drawn pixels instead of 96 x 80), with the same art. The package still hangs clear of its belly. (T-330)
- **The combo shows as live viewers** (board, 2026-10-28): the combo multiplier keeps working exactly as it does (tricks raise it, crashes cut it, it drains, it multiplies what drifting earns), but the player sees it as the stream's live viewers instead of "Combo x2.00": about 20,000 at x2 and 1,000,000 at x6 (the board's anchors), on a smooth curve between them (and below x2, a proposal). The number behaves like a real stream's: it counts towards its value and keeps moving a little. The higher it is, the hotter it looks, and over a million it is on fire. (T-332, T-336)
- **Subs instead of likes** (board, 2026-10-28): what the player earns toward the next gift pack is **subs** (the stream's subscribers), not likes: drifting brings subs, the viewers multiply them, each full **sub goal** sends a gift pack, and the drain is people unsubscribing when the stream gets dull. Only the name and the look change; the numbers and rules of the likes stay (the likes bar becomes the sub goal: HUD and menus, Decisions). Extended narrative, Decisions, "Subs". (T-331, T-337)
- **Hearts instead of health points** (board, 2026-10-28): the car has **5 hearts**. A minion's hit and a meteor take 1 heart, the kaiju's 2. After any hit the car is invulnerable for **1 second**, blinking, so the player can escape a swarm; hits during that second do nothing and don't cut the combo. A health pickup heals 1 heart, and drops at half today's chance (15%, Enemies). The garage's car health upgrade adds 1 heart per level (Garage design). (T-333, T-334, T-338) Numbers (T-333, `game/data/run.json` `car`): `starting_hearts` 5, `invulnerability_seconds` 1.0, `blink_interval_seconds` 0.1 (a proposal: each on or off phase of the blink). The old `starting_health` 100 is gone. Built in T-334 ([game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md](../game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md), "Hearts and the invulnerability (T-334)"); proposals for the playtest: a hit during the second also gives **no knockback** (so the car drives out of the swarm), a hit ignored during it does not restart the second, and the blink starts with the car hidden, so the hit shows at once.
- **The tutorial slides come between Start and the run** (board, 2026-10-29; the slides, their text and the "Don't show again" checkbox: HUD and menus, Decisions, "Tutorial slides before the first run"): the main menu's Start shows the tutorial slides first, and the run begins (its clock starts at 8:00) only when the slides' own Start is pressed. If "Don't show again" was ticked then, that is saved, and every later Start, also after restarting the game, goes straight into the run. The pause screen's Restart starts a fresh run directly, without the slides. (T-382, T-387)
- **A red flash when the car takes damage** (board, 2026-10-30): when the car loses a heart, it flashes red, so the hit reads at once. How it fits with the invulnerability blink, its length and its shade of red are proposals for the playtest. The same red flash shows on enemies when they take damage (Enemies, Decisions). (T-403) Built in T-403 ([game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md](../game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md), "The red hit flash (T-403)"); proposals for the playtest (`game/data/run.json` `hit_flash`): `seconds` 0.4 and `color` [1.0, 0.25, 0.25] (a multiply tint). The car is hidden for the first 0.1 s of the blink, so the flash shows as red on the next two visible phases (0.1 to 0.2 s and 0.3 to 0.4 s), then the plain blink goes on; a hit ignored during the invulnerability does not flash.
- **The wreck decides the loss at its end** (board, 2026-10-30, audit; replaces "The loss is decided at once" and "a kaiju kill can no longer turn it into a win" in Content, "Wrecked"): the run is lost only when the wreck's 3 seconds end and the recap shows. Until then a health pickup revives the car (T-406): the clock runs again, the controls return and the loss is undone; a trick in progress at the wreck is dropped, not paid. A kaiju kill during the wreck wins the run. Coins and health pickups are pulled in and count as usual. Restart or Exit from the pause screen during the wreck cancels the run: no coins kept, no runs-list entry. Which weapons keep working during the wreck: Weapons, Decisions.
- **A tie goes to the player** (board, 2026-10-30, audit): if the kaiju dies on the same step the clock reaches 0:00, the run is won.
- **A health pickup at full hearts stays** (board, 2026-10-30, audit): with full hearts the car doesn't pick a health pickup up, and the magnet doesn't pull it. Built in T-415 (`health_pickup.gd` `wants_health()`, `pickup_magnet.gd`): a health pickup is taken only below full hearts, or during the wreck (it revives the car); it waits where it lies, and is taken once the car is hurt.
- **Hits close together cut the combo once** (board, 2026-10-30, audit): a collision within 0.5 seconds of the one that cut the combo doesn't cut it again (0.5 s is a proposal for the playtest). Built in T-415 (`combo.json` `collision_window_seconds` 0.5, `run_state.gd` `_cut_combo()`, on the run's clock); a new run clears it. Proposals for the playtest (T-415, not the board's yet): the window starts only when a collision really cut the combo, a collision inside it does not start a new one, and the crash still pays its trick in progress (`crashed`) as before.
- **The garage adds to run.json's base** (board, 2026-10-30, audit; T-415): the run's starting hearts and the magnet's radius are stored in `run.json` only (`car.starting_hearts`, `pickup_magnet.radius_units`). `garage.json` stores for those two upgrades only each level's `bonus` (no `base_value`, no absolute `value`); `RunState.start_run()` adds the bonus to `run.json`'s base, and `GarageData.value()` (the garage screen) is that same sum. Changing the base in `run.json` changes both the run and the garage screen.
- **Closing the game mid-run** (board, 2026-10-30, audit): ~~closing the window during a run ends it as a loss: its coins are kept and it goes in the runs list~~ (replaced the same day by "Restart, Exit or closing cancels the run", below). Switching to another window pauses the game. How it works (T-416): losing focus opens the pause screen, except during the level-up choice and the time's up screen, where pause is already blocked, and outside a run (proposal for the playtest: no auto-resume when focus returns, the player resumes with Escape).
- **Restart, Exit or closing cancels the run** (board, 2026-10-30, after playing build I: "I told you to CANCEL the run, NOT SAVE it if it gets restarted or quit"; "coins are lost too, nothing saved"): Restart or Exit on the pause screen, and closing the game window, at any point of a run (the wreck included), cancel it: the coins picked up in it are lost, nothing goes into the run history, and no recap shows. Replaces the coins kept by Restart and Exit (Content, "Restart and Exit on the pause screen", T-327), and the loss with coins kept on closing (above). (T-416)
- **Mission packs** (board, 2026-10-31): besides the subs (which give weapons through the level-up gift pack), a run has **missions**, shown one at a time on the **left side** of the screen as a pixel-art **notebook page**. A mission is one or more **mission goals** (for example "thread the needle 3 times"); each goal has a checkbox, a quantity goal shows its progress (for example "2/4 Alt drifts"), a duration or other goal shows none, and a goal is crossed off when completed. When every goal of a mission is done, the mission is completed and the next one appears. Missions are for **one run only**: they start over from the first mission every run. There are **30 missions** a run. The **first 5 are always the same**, in this order: (1) drift for 2 seconds continuously (the board, 2026-11-01; was 4); (2) perform 10 alt drifts; (3) get 3 seconds of airtime; (4) perform 3 air 180s; (5) perform an air 360. **Missions 6 to 30 are generated at random each run** from combinations of the tricks and their amounts; the generator's rules (which tricks, how amounts grow, how many goals per mission) are the agents' proposal for the board's review. Airtime from the Jump power-up counts towards the airtime and air-trick goals (board, 2026-10-31). A completed mission gives a **driving power-up gift** instead of a weapon: like the level-up gift pack, it pauses the run and offers **2 choices** (a new power-up or the next tier of one the car has), on an overlay similar to the weapons' gift menu but clearly distinct, to show these are driving power-ups, not weapons. The power-ups: Drifting, Decisions, "Driving power-ups". (goal G-009)

### Content

#### One run

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    launch([Game launches]) --> menu
    start([Run starts: 8:00 on the clock]) --> drive[Drive and drift]
    drive --> drift{Drift longer than 1 s?}
    drift -- yes --> dxp[XP per second, times the combo] --> lvl{XP bar full?}
    lvl -- yes --> heli[Level up: a helicopter drops the gift pack ahead of the car] --> drive
    drive --> pack{Drive over a gift pack?}
    pack -- yes --> choice[Level-up screen: weapon choice, run paused] --> drive
    lvl -- no --> drive
    drive --> enemies[Enemies swarm in; weapons fire automatically; enemies drop coins] --> drive
    drive --> boss{7:00 reached?}
    boss -- yes --> kaiju[Kaiju spawns: weapons can damage it at any time]
    kaiju --> win{Kaiju defeated before 8:00?}
    win -- yes --> won([Win])
    win -- no --> lost([Loss])
    drive -- Last heart gone --> wreck[Wrecked: controls dead, the car slides on, smoking and burning, 3 s] --> lost
    won --> recap[Recap screen: the run's stats with pictures; Continue or X]
    lost --> recap
    recap --> menu[Main menu: Start, Garage, Exit]
    menu -- Garage --> garage[Garage: spend coins on permanent car upgrades] --> menu
    menu -- Start --> hidden{Tutorial hidden?}
    hidden -- yes --> start
    hidden -- no --> slides[Tutorial slides: controls, tricks, goal; no run yet]
    slides -- "Slides' Start (Don't show again saved if ticked)" --> start
```

#### The run scene

The run is one Godot scene (task T-036; how to use it: [game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md](../game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md), section "The run"). It loads the run's map and puts the drift car (Drifting) on it, at the centre of the map, in the gravel square, with the camera following the car in the isometric view, as in the drift prototype.

The run's map (task T-206; Level design, Decisions, "The elevation sample map becomes the run's map") is the elevation sample map's layout with its rooftops and ramps (Level design, Content, "Elevation sample map", "The run on this map"): the car has its height there, and everything else in the run (enemies, weapons, pickups, coins, the HUD, the pause screen) works on it as on the MVP map. The MVP map (Level design, Content, "MVP map") stays in the project; one constant in the run switches back to it ([game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md](../game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md), "The run").

The run owns its state: the clock (8:00 counting down, stopping while the game is paused), the car's health in hearts (starting at the value in [game/data/run.json](../game/data/run.json), plus the garage upgrade's hearts; Decisions, "Hearts instead of health points"), and the coins collected in the run. Other parts of the game plug into it:

- At 1:00 left the run sends "boss time"; the kaiju spawns on it (Enemies).
- Enemies damage the car and add coins through the run; the kaiju's death ends the run as a win.
- The car reaching 0 hearts, or the clock reaching 0:00, ends the run as a loss. At 0 hearts the car is wrecked first, for 3 seconds (Wrecked, below).
- Either way, the run sends one "run ended" signal with the result and the coins collected, which are saved (Garage design).
- The HUD reads the time left, the health and the coins from the run (HUD and menus).

#### Likes and levels

The run also owns the likes (XP) and the level (task T-037; how to use it: [game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md](../game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md), section "The run"; the numbers: [game/data/run.json](../game/data/run.json)):

- Every completed challenge, preset or the kaiju's meteor challenges, gives the current level's challenge XP, and the run sends a "score" signal with it for the challenge popup.
- The run follows the car's drift state step by step: once an unbroken drift reaches 1 second it gives the drift XP for that second, then for each further full second.
- When XP reaches the level's threshold the level goes up (leftover XP carries over, so one gain can give several level-ups), and the run sends "level up" with the new level. At the top level the bar stops.
- On every level-up the run plays the level-up effect: a burst of pixel particles from the car, following it while it plays (task T-112; the look: Visual style, Decisions, "Level-up effect"). Several level-ups in the same moment show as one burst, and the burst keeps playing while the run is paused for the weapon choice.
- The HUD reads the XP, the level's threshold and the level, with a signal whenever they change.
- A level-up does not pause the run by itself: it sends the gift pack (below, task T-144). The run pauses (clock and car) when the car drives over the gift pack's package and the level-up screen opens (task T-052), until the weapon choice is made, one choice after another when several packages are picked up at once.
- **Likes drain** (task T-115; the speed: [game/data/run.json](../game/data/run.json), `likes_drain`, task T-114): once the combo has fully drained back to "no combo", the XP in the current level goes down, stopping at the start of the level, so the level never goes down. Any trick raises the combo and stops it; it starts again once the combo has drained again. It stops while the run is paused (pause screen, level-up screen) and after the run ends. At the top level there is nothing to drain. The HUD's likes bar follows it, so the bar visibly empties.
- **The curve (T-328, proposal for the playtest; the numbers: `levels` in [game/data/run.json](../game/data/run.json)):** the early levels need far fewer likes so the first gift packs come quickly, and the last two levels are unchanged. One drift second is 10 likes at x1, so the seconds below are drift seconds at that combo (a drift pays whole seconds only):

  | Level up to | Likes needed | Seconds at x1 | at x2 | at x4 | Likes in total |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 2 | 30 (was 100) | 3.0 | 1.5 | 0.75 | 30 |
  | 3 | 45 (was 125) | 4.5 | 2.25 | 1.1 | 75 |
  | 4 | 65 (was 156) | 6.5 | 3.25 | 1.6 | 140 |
  | 5 | 95 (was 195) | 9.5 | 4.75 | 2.4 | 235 |
  | 6 | 140 (was 244) | 14 | 7 | 3.5 | 375 |
  | 7 | 200 (was 305) | 20 | 10 | 5 | 575 |
  | 8 | 290 (was 381) | 29 | 14.5 | 7.3 | 865 |
  | 9 | 400 (was 477) | 40 | 20 | 10 | 1,265 |
  | 10 | 560 (was 596) | 56 | 28 | 14 | 1,825 |
  | 11 | 745 (same) | 74.5 | 37 | 18.6 | 2,570 |
  | 12 | 931 (same) | 93 | 47 | 23 | 3,501 |

  The total for all 11 level-ups is 3,501 likes, 18% under today's 4,255; the level cap stays 12. Reasons for the shape: each level needs about 1.4 to 1.5 times the one before at the start (the old curve's 1.25 from a much higher start), easing to 1.25 at the end, so the first gift pack comes after about 3 seconds of drifting (the board's "a few seconds") and the first four within about 10 seconds of drift at x2 (140 likes), against about 38 s at x1 before; the gaps then stretch so the middle and late run keep the old pace, and levels 10 and 11 are exactly today's. Time to each gift pack in a typical run, my estimate from the formula only (not a scripted run): drifting about half the time at an average x2 earns about 10 likes a second, so levels 2 to 5 arrive at about 3, 7, 14 and 24 s, level 8 at about 87 s and level 12 at about 350 s of an 8-minute run (480 s); the old curve reached level 5 at about 70 s and level 12 at about 430 s. The board judges it in the playtest. The likes drain is a share of the level's bar (8% a second), so a full bar still empties in 12.5 s at every level: 2.4 likes a second at level 2's 30-like bar, against 10 likes earned for each drifted second, so it only eats the progress made inside the level. The challenge XP of the old MVP map keeps its share of the level's bar (30, 40, 50, 65, 84, 106, 135, 164, 201, then the old 236, 259, 285), so one challenge never skips levels it did not skip before.
- A new run starts back at level 1 with no XP.

#### The gift pack drop

How the level-up screen is reached (task T-144; how to use it: [game/docs/game-loop/gift-pack-and-pickups.md](../game/docs/game-loop/gift-pack-and-pickups.md), section "The gift pack drop"; the numbers: [game/data/gift_pack.json](../game/data/gift_pack.json)):

- On every level-up the run sends a helicopter. It flies across the screen from beyond one edge to beyond the other, carrying the package, and drops it over the landing spot; the package falls and lands. Built with placeholder art for now (the final art: tasks T-145 and T-146).
- The helicopter is drawn 30% bigger than its first size (T-330): scale 0.65 on its 192 x 160 sheet frames, about 125 x 104 drawn pixels, set as `helicopter.draw_scale` in `gift_pack.json`. The package hangs `hang_below_px` 88 (was 80) under its centre, so it still hangs clear of the bigger belly; the top margin and the off-screen margin are read from the drawn size and did not change.
- The landing spot is a short way ahead of the car, along the way it is moving, on open road: never in a building, a boulder or past the map's edge. If straight ahead is blocked, the nearest open spot around it is used.
- On a map with rooftops (T-402; Level design, Decisions, "A gift pack that falls on a platform shows on it"; proposal for the playtest): the landing spot is on the street whenever one is open within the search. Only when none is (the car well inside a large rooftop) does the package land on open, flat ground of the rooftop the car is on, away from its edges, ramps and any higher rooftop on it. Wherever it lands it is drawn at the height of that ground and in the depth order the car has there, so it is never drawn below a rooftop; the pickup magnet moves it with the ground's height. The car picks it up only from that height or above (a car on the street beside the rooftop does not; a car jumping over a package still does).
- The falling shadow (T-407; board, 2026-10-30): from the moment the helicopter drops the package until it lands, the car's air shadow (`game/scripts/driving/car_shadow.gd`, no new art; since T-454 it is small while the package is high and grows to the package's size as it comes down: Visual style, Content, "Shadows that shrink with height") lies at the landing spot, at the height of the ground it lands on (the street or the rooftop), in the car's shadow depth order there. It is gone the moment the package lands (and on pickup or a new run). Not shown while the helicopter still carries it.
- Every pickup at its height (board, 2026-10-30, widening T-402: "when I go to pick up the gift on a platform, its hitbox is in the wrong place"): gift packages, coins and health pickups are drawn and picked up at the height of the ground they lie on. On a rooftop the car picks them up there, never from the street below; one rule for all of them (`game/scripts/run/pickup_height.gd`: the car's height at least the pickup's less 0.5 units).
- The run keeps going the whole time (the clock, enemies, likes and the likes drain). The level-up moment itself (the "level up" signal, the level-up effect, the likes bar) is unchanged.
- One package per level-up. Packages stay on the ground until picked up; a new run clears them.
- Loaded with the run (T-482; the board's recording of 2026-11-01 showed a 97 ms hitch at the first pickup): the level-up screen builds every possible card once while the run is set up (`LevelUpScreen.prewarm()`, called by `setup()`), hidden, and clears them, so the card and highlight frames, every weapon's picture and the cards' text shaping are loaded before the first gift pack pickup. Nothing the player sees changes.
- Driving over a landed package removes it and opens the level-up screen for that level, with the same weapon choices as before; the run pauses until the choice is made. Two packages picked up together give two screens, one after the other.
- Every package on the map gets its own arrow (board, 2026-10-28; T-314): while a package that has been dropped, falling or landed, is off screen, an arrow at the screen's edge points to it, one per package, kept clear of the HUD, so several arrows show when several packages are out. The package still carried by the helicopter has none yet. Arrows that would overlap are slid apart along the edge (proposal for the playtest). Proposal for the playtest: arrows only for packages off screen, none for a package on screen (the board asked for "the same one that appears today at the edge of the screen").

#### The combo

The run also owns the combo (task T-081; how to use it: [game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md](../game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md), section "The run"; the numbers: [game/data/combo.json](../game/data/combo.json)):

- Each trick the car does raises the combo multiplier by that trick's amount, up to a cap. The run sends a signal with the trick, the amount added and the new multiplier, for the trick popups.
- The tricks: the extended drift (paid once per drift, by its length), the 360, the alternate drift (Drifting, Decisions), the air 180 and air 360 (Drifting, Decisions, "Aerial tricks"), the airtime trick (Drifting, Decisions, "Airtime trick"), and **thread the needle** (task T-272; Level design, Decisions, "Thread the needle"): on a level made in the creator, driving through the gap between two obstacles the board paired, without touching either. When each fires is in `game/docs/driving/tricks.md`, "Tricks" (thread the needle: "Level creator", "Thread the needle (T-272)"); what each adds is in `combo.json`.
- The multiplier multiplies all XP gained: each completed challenge's XP (the "score" signal carries the multiplied amount) and each drift second's XP.
- Hitting a wall, a building, the map edge or a boulder cuts the combo by 50%, and so does any damage to the car (enemies, meteors). The cut applies to the part of the multiplier above "no combo".
- A crash pays the trick in progress first (task T-315; Decisions, "A crash pays the trick in progress"): a drift under way pays its extended drift for the time it lasted until the crash, and in the air the spins and the airtime so far pay too; then the combo is cut, so the trick's popup shows just before COMBO BROKEN!. Which tricks count and why: Drifting, Content, "A crash pays the trick in progress". The order is a switch in `combo.json` (`crash_pays_trick_first`).
- When no trick has come for 2 seconds, the combo drains, down to "no combo". A trick restarts the wait.
- **Live viewers (T-332):** the player sees the multiplier as viewers. The curve, heat steps (20,000, 84,736 and 236,026, then fire from 1,000,000), the counting speed, the wobble and the number format are in [game/data/viewers.json](../game/data/viewers.json), read through `ViewersData` (`viewers_for`, `step_for_viewers`, `count_toward`, `with_wobble`, `trick_gain`, `crash_loss`, `format`). x1 = 2,500, x2 = 20,000, x6 = 1,000,000. The HUD counter is T-336.
- The HUD and enemy spawning read the multiplier, with a signal whenever it changes. It stops while the run is paused and resets with every new run.

Starting a new run resets the map, the car and the state. The run's camera zoom can be changed from the pause screen.

#### The run's stats for the recap

The run keeps the stats the recap screen shows (task T-319; Decisions, "Recap screen in the MVP"; how to read them: [game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md](../game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md), "The run's recap summary"). One read-only summary, a plain dictionary that also serialises to JSON (so the runs list, T-363, can save it), is cleared when a new run starts and stays readable after the run ends:

- **enemies_slain:** kills per enemy type ("minion", "kaiju"), counted when the car's weapons kill one.
- **tricks:** how many times each trick was completed, by the id the combo uses (the drifts, 360s, alternate drifts, air tricks, airtime, thread the needle).
- **highest_combo:** the highest multiplier reached.
- **peak_viewers:** the live viewers counter's highest number in the run (T-320, the board's quick tuning of 2026-10-29: the recap's "Peak engagement" shows viewers, not a multiplier): the viewers for the highest combo on the viewers curve (Decisions, "The combo shows as live viewers"), the number the counter counts up to, without its small wobble. Saved with the run history like the rest.
- **weapons:** every weapon the car owned at the end, with the tier it ended on and the kills it made (the kills are a proposal, since they were cheap to count).
- **Also kept, for the recap and the runs list:** the result (win or loss), why a loss happened (the clock ran out, or health), the time survived, the coins, the likes gained in total and the level reached.

Nothing in this changes what the player sees.

#### Wrecked

When the car loses its last heart (Decisions, "Wrecked: the stream keeps rolling"; task T-360; how it is built: [game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md](../game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md), "Wrecked (T-360)"):

- **The loss is decided at the wreck's end** (Decisions, "The wreck decides the loss at its end"; task T-413). The last heart starts the wreck but sets no result: the run is lost (on health, which the recap keeps as the reason) only when the **3 seconds** are over (the board's number, in [game/data/run.json](../game/data/run.json), `wreck.seconds`), with the same "run ended" as before, so the next screen follows as for any other end. During the 3 seconds no damage, likes, gift packs or tricks count; the trick in progress at the last heart's hit is dropped, not paid. Proposals for the playtest (T-413, not the board's yet): the car makes no tricks while wrecked; kills during the wreck count in the recap; the level creator's Play follows the same pause rule. Coins count, coins and health pickups are pulled in by the magnet as usual (the gift packs stand still), a health pickup revives the car (below), and a kaiju kill ends the run at once as a win, with the win recap. Restart or Exit on the pause screen during the wreck cancels the run: no coins are kept and nothing goes into the runs list. The time's up (the clock) has its own 3 seconds, its screen over the frozen run (T-317; HUD and menus, Content, "Time's up screen"), and a kaiju kill on the same step the clock reaches 0:00 still wins (Decisions, "A tie goes to the player").
- **The controls go dead.** No steering, throttle or brake reaches the car. It keeps the movement it had and slows to a stop with its normal physics: it can still slide, spin, bounce off walls or land a jump. The camera keeps following it. Its handling while alive is unchanged.
- **Smoke and flames** come out of the car for the 3 seconds: placeholders drawn in code (grey pixel puffs that rise, grow and shrink, left behind as the car slides, and flickering flames on the car in red, orange and a white-hot core, none of Greenbull's colours) until T-361's pixel art animations replace them.
- **Pause** still works: it freezes the wreck, and the 3 seconds carry on when the game resumes.
- **Proposals for the playtest** (the board's questions left open, settled by the Game Loop Agent; T-360): the **HUD stays on screen** as it was at the last heart (the hearts empty, the coins, the viewers counter and the sub goal) so the stream still feels live; the **clock stops** at the moment the last heart goes (that is the time survived the recap shows); the weapons, the kaiju's meteors and the gift pack helicopter stand still, as they do at any end of the run; the engine sound stops.
- **The enemies swarm the wreck** (board, quick tuning, 2026-10-29: "I don't want the monsters to stop moving when I die, when the car gets destroyed. I want them to keep coming and swarming the car. But with no like interaction or anything, they just come and swarm over the car."): during the 3 seconds the minions keep coming (they still spawn) and walk to the wrecked car as they normally would, and a kaiju already there keeps walking to it too, but nothing interacts: no damage or knockback to the car, and no likes. Once the run has ended they stand still. (Coins count during the wreck: "The wreck decides the loss at its end", T-413. Which weapons still hurt enemies during the wreck, so whether minions and the kaiju can die: Weapons, Decisions, "Weapons during the wreck", T-414.) (Replaces the first proposal, that they freeze.)
- **A health pickup revives the wreck** (board, 2026-10-30; task T-406; Decisions, "A health pickup revives a wrecked car"): during the 3 seconds a health pickup still flies to the sliding car inside its usual pickup range (the magnet) and is picked up as it touches it. The car comes back with **1 heart**: the controls return, the smoke and flames stop, the run goes on (no result was set, T-413; the recap does not show and `run_ended` is not sent), the clock runs on from where it stopped, and likes, tricks and damage count again. Proposals for the playtest: the usual **1-second invulnerability** follows the revive (with the blink), so the swarm round the wreck does not finish it at once; the **combo** stays cut as the fatal hit left it and the **live viewers** follow it as always (the recap's peak is kept). The **gift packs** stay still during the wreck; coins are pulled and count (T-413, replacing T-406's proposal that they stay still too). Without a pickup in reach, the wreck ends with the recap as before.

#### The run history

Every run's recap stats are kept on this computer (task T-363; Decisions, "The runs list"), for the runs list screen (T-364). When a run ends, win or loss, its final recap summary (the section above) is added to a history file, once, on `run_ended`; how the ending is reached (including the wreck's wait) makes no difference. Each entry is that summary plus the date and time the run ended (`ended_at`, local, and `ended_unix`). The result (win, loss by health, loss by time), the time survived, the coins and the likes are in it. The history keeps the newest 200 runs and drops older ones (a proposal; the board can change the cap). A missing or broken file is an empty history. The list is read newest first. Only the game's own runs are saved, not the level creator's Play. The file, fields and functions: [game/docs/data/game-data.md](../game/docs/data/game-data.md), "Run history". Nothing the player sees changes.

#### Missions: the generator's rules (task T-455, proposals)

The data is `game/data/missions.json` (read through `MissionData`; [game/docs/data/game-data.md](../game/docs/data/game-data.md)). `total` is 30. The 5 fixed missions are the board's (Decisions, "Mission packs"): drift 4 s unbroken (`extended_drift`, seconds), 10 alt drifts (`alternate_drift`), 3 s airtime (`airtime`, seconds), 3 air 180s (`air_one_eighty`), 1 air 360 (`air_three_sixty`). The ids are the ones the trick detector emits (`trick_detector.gd`); `thread_the_needle` comes from `thread_the_needle.gd`; `three_sixty` (a ground 360) is the seventh. The rules for missions 6 to 30 are **proposals for the board's playtest** (the driving numbers are the Driving & Drift Agent's call by the docs; Game Data wrote them on its behalf), each with a reason in the file:

- **Goals per mission:** 1 for missions 6 to 14, 2 for 15 to 24, 3 for 25 to 30, never the same trick twice in a mission. Reason: a new mission stays quick to read early; later ones take longer.
- **Amounts** grow in a straight line from mission 6 to a cap (`base + growth × (mission − 6)`, capped; seconds rounded to 0.5): drift 5 s (+0.2, cap 10); alt drifts 12 (+0.8, cap 32); ground 360s 2 (+0.2, cap 7); airtime 4 s (+0.25, cap 10); air 180s 4 (+0.3, cap 11); air 360s 2 (+0.12, cap 5); thread the needle 3 (+0.25, cap 9). Reason: each starts just above the fixed mission of its kind and ends at about 2.5 times, still doable inside a run; the hardest tricks have the lowest caps.

#### Missions in the run (task T-457)

The run keeps its missions and the car's driving power-ups (Decisions, "Mission packs"; how to use it: [game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md](../game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md), "Missions and the car's power-ups (T-457)"). Nothing in this shows on screen by itself: the notebook page and the power-up gift overlay (T-459) are separate tickets that read it.

- **A fresh set every run:** a new run (Start, or Restart from the pause screen) starts at mission 1 with 30 missions: the 5 fixed ones, then missions 6 to 30 generated from the rules above with a new random seed each run (a test can give the seed).
- **One mission at a time:** every goal of the current mission counts at once; when all are done the mission is completed and the next one is current.
- **What counts:** the car's tricks as the combo gets them (alt drifts, 360s, air 180s and 360s, thread the needle), every landing's airtime added up (also a hop too short to raise the combo), and, for the drift goal, **one unbroken drift**: it is ticked off the moment the drift reaches its seconds, and a drift that ends, by letting go or hitting something, starts over from 0. How tricks pay in the combo and likes does not change.
- **Signals** for the HUD page and the gift overlay: a goal's progress (done out of total), a goal completed, a mission completed, and a mission started.
- **The car's driving power-ups:** the run keeps which power-ups the car owns and at which tier (0 = not owned); a gift gives a new one at tier 1 or the next tier of one owned, never past its last tier; a signal fires when they change; a new run clears them.
- **The gift's pause (T-459):** a completed mission pauses the run for the driving power-up overlay, like the level-up's weapon choice, and taking a power-up resumes it. The two never show at once: whichever opens second waits for the first to close, and the run stays paused between them; a gift with nothing left to offer is skipped without a pause. The rules and the look: HUD and menus, Content, "Power-up overlay".
- **Proposals for the playtest** (T-457, not the board's yet): after mission 30 nothing more is offered; a trick that completes a mission does not count for the next one too; a new mission's drift goal counts only drifting done after it appeared.

#### Screen flow

One screen is on show at a time (task T-055; how to use it: [game/docs/game-loop/screen-flow.md](../game/docs/game-loop/screen-flow.md), section "Screen flow"):

- The game opens on the main menu (HUD and menus, Content).
- **Start** replaces the menu with the **tutorial slides** (task T-387; Decisions, "The tutorial slides come between Start and the run"; the slides: HUD and menus, Content, "Tutorial slides and trick list"). No run exists while they are up, so its clock has not started. The slides' own Start replaces them with a fresh run, after saving "Don't show again" when it is ticked. Once it has been saved, Start replaces the menu with a fresh run straight away. During the run, Escape pauses and resumes it (the pause screen, HUD and menus).
- When the run ends, win or loss (a loss on health after the wreck's 3 seconds, Wrecked, above), the run is removed and the **recap screen** shows its stats (task T-320; Decisions, "The recap always closes a run"; the look: HUD and menus, Content, "Recap screen"). Its Continue button and the X at its top right both bring the main menu back. Another Start begins a fresh run.
- **Garage** opens the garage, and leaving the garage goes back to the main menu (Garage design). Wired in task T-089: the garage's back button returns to the main menu.
- **Exit** closes the game.
- **Restart and Exit on the pause screen** (board, 2026-10-28; T-327; coins since 2026-10-30: Decisions, "Restart, Exit or closing cancels the run", T-416): the pause screen's **Restart** ~~keeps the coins collected so far (banked as on a loss)~~ cancels the run (its coins are lost, nothing saved), removes the run and starts a fresh one straight away, never showing the tutorial slides (T-387) (level 1, the same map, the garage upgrades applied). Its **Exit** ~~keeps the coins~~ cancels the run the same way, removes the run and shows the main menu (Exit on the main menu still closes the game). Neither shows a time's up screen or a recap, and neither goes through the run's `run_ended` signal; the recap (T-320) must skip them the same way. HUD and menus, Content, has the buttons' look and the proposals.

The drift prototype is not part of the flow; it stays as a tuning tool, opened on its own.

### References

- Final GDD (historical; superseded by the game area docs): [short-gdd/Solid_Carbide_-_Final_GDD.pdf](short-gdd/Solid_Carbide_-_Final_GDD.pdf), sections "Game Specificity" and "Player Experience".
- Unity prototype report: [drifting/unity-prototype-report.md](drifting/unity-prototype-report.md), for the definition of drifting used for XP.
- Run numbers (XP per challenge, XP per level, drift XP, car starting hearts, invulnerability, blink): [game/data/run.json](../game/data/run.json), read through `game/scripts/data/run_data.gd`.
- Combo numbers (what each trick adds, the cap, the collision cut, the drain, how the combo raises spawning): [game/data/combo.json](../game/data/combo.json), read through `game/scripts/data/combo_data.gd`.
- Gift pack numbers (the helicopter's speed, height and margin; the package's fall time, landing distance, clearance and pickup radius): [game/data/gift_pack.json](../game/data/gift_pack.json), read through `game/scripts/data/gift_pack_data.gd`.


## 2. Drifting

*Source: [drifting.md](drifting.md). How the car drives, drifts and reverses, the prototypes built so far, and the research and decisions behind them.*

Drifting is the one core skill of Solid Carbide. The car's driving and drifting copy the board's older Unity prototype, including its drift curve and its camera, with a higher top speed chosen after the board's playtest of the Godot version, and the car can also reverse. The player sets the camera zoom in the pause menu. The player drives with W to go forward, S to reverse, and A and D to steer and drift.

### Decisions

- The car's driving and drifting copy the board's Unity prototype (see Content, "Prototypes so far").
- The car can reverse with the S key, as in the Unity prototype. Controls: W to go forward, S to reverse, A and D to steer and drift.
- The drift curve is the one the Unity prototype uses. This replaces the earlier plan to choose between three candidate curves (square root, linear or exponential) by playtesting. Drift is not meant to be realistic.
- The camera behaves like the Unity prototype's camera by default (how it follows the car, its zoom and any look-ahead), unless the board decides otherwise later.
- The car is drawn 3 times as long as it is wide: 1 unit wide and 3 units long. This is the drawing only: the car's physics body stays a 1 by 1 unit square, as in the Unity prototype, so collisions behave the same. The drawing sticks out past the body at the front and back.
- The car bounces off walls slightly (buildings and the map's edges), and off boulders the same way.
- The car does not bounce off enemies: they only damage it.
- ~~The bounce off walls and boulders sends the car back at a quarter of the speed it hit with (bounce strength 0.25). While W is held the car stays pressed against the wall, and a knockback against the car's nose is cancelled, because W keeps snapping the car back to cruise speed; the board is fine with both. (2026-10-10)~~ Replaced by the next line.
- **The car bounces off walls** (board, 2026-10-30, after playing master: "the wall grabs me when I keep accelerating on it"; drifting into a wall with W held, the car stayed stuck on it and the drift kept climbing): the car really bounces off walls, buildings, raised areas' sides, the map's edges and boulders, even while W is held, instead of being pressed against them. The bounce grows with how hard the car hits, up to a maximum, so a very fast hit is not a comically big bounce. No throttle cut: the board rejected switching W off for a time after a hit. The scale and the maximum are proposals for the playtest. Replaces the 2026-10-10 line above. (T-435)
- **A wall hit ends the drift** (board, 2026-10-31, after playing T-435's wall bounce): when the car hits a wall, a building, a raised area's side, the map's edge or a boulder while drifting, the drift ends at the hit, as if the player had ended it: it pays once for the time it lasted up to the hit (Game loop architecture, Decisions, "A crash pays the trick in progress"), then the hit's combo cut applies as before. A new drift can start right after the bounce. (T-438)
- The MVP has three **tricks**, all done with the car's existing driving (what tricks are worth: Game loop architecture, Decisions):
  - **Extended drift:** every second of drifting counts as one low-value trick.
  - **360:** the car's heading turns a full 360 degrees in one direction during one unbroken drift; a mid-value trick. 720 degrees counts as two.
  - **Alternate drift:** drift forwards, release W while still steering, switch to S and drift backwards, then back to W, so the car draws semicircles. Each switch between a forward and a backward drift while keeping the same steering direction counts as one high-value trick. The Driving & Drift Agent proposes the timing limits; the board tunes them.
- **Aerial tricks** (board, 2026-10-21): two tricks in the air, from turning the car while it is airborne (off a ramp or a rooftop's edge): a **180** (the heading turns 180 degrees during one airtime) and a **360** (a full turn). Either direction counts the same: a left 180 and a right 180 are the same trick, and so for the 360. What they are worth, and whether a 360 also counts its 180, are the Driving & Drift Agent's proposals for the playtest (Game loop architecture, Decisions, for how tricks raise the combo). Their popup texts: HUD and menus, Content (T-218). (T-219) The car turns faster in the air than on the ground, so an air 360 fits in a jump off the tallest rooftop (board, 2026-10-21, after T-219 found the longest airtime, 1 second, too short for a 360 at the ground turn rate); how fast is the Driving & Drift Agent's proposal for the playtest. Each spin pays once (board, 2026-10-21): turning while airborne no longer counts towards the drift's 360, so an air spin pays only its aerial trick, not FULL 360! as well. No drifting in the air (board, 2026-10-21, after playing T-219): once the car leaves the ground it keeps the speed and direction it had at takeoff and its path can't be changed until it lands; W, S, A and D in the air only spin the car (its heading), they don't steer, speed up, slow down or drift it. Since the car isn't drifting in the air, airtime doesn't count as drift time for LONG DRIFT! either. **A little side slip out of a drift** (board, 2026-10-22; "insanely crucial to the fundamental feel"): when a drift ends, the car keeps a small amount of sideways slide for a moment, so the player has to steady it with a touch of counter-steer, as in Hotshot Racing and Mario Kart; getting that right should feel satisfying. Tiny, not a spin-out; how much and for how long are tuning values the board sets in a playtest of its own, separate from every other change (T-278). **Hype speed boost** (board, 2026-10-22): the higher the hype level (the combo heat steps x2, x3, x4 and up; HUD and menus, Decisions), the faster the car goes: its top speed (and how fast it gets there, the agent's call) rises with each step and falls back when the combo drops; how much per step is the Driving & Drift Agent's proposal for the playtest. (T-275) **Slower air turn, upgradable** (board, 2026-10-22): the car's turn rate in the air is halved (the multiplier over the ground rate from 2.5 to 1.25), and a new garage upgrade raises it (Garage design, Decisions, "Air turn upgrade"). (T-269, T-270)
- **Airtime trick** (board, 2026-10-21): every time the car is off the ground, its airtime is a trick of its own: on landing it pays a combo amount that scales with how long it was in the air (seconds and hundredths). Reasonable defaults for the scaling are the Driving & Drift Agent's proposal for the playtest. It counts alongside AIR 180! and AIR 360!. Its popup text: HUD and menus, Content (T-241). (T-242)
- **Drift pays once, at its end** (board, 2026-10-22, like the airtime trick): the extended drift no longer pays a small trick every second; a whole drift pays once when it ends, with a combo amount scaled by how long it lasted (seconds and hundredths). Its popup keeps the existing LONG DRIFT! text with its amount. The XP from drifting seconds stays as it is (Game loop architecture, Decisions). The scaling defaults are the Driving & Drift Agent's proposal for the playtest. (T-246)
- Settling the movement mechanics is one of the project's top priorities and the first thing to work on.
- When W makes the car jump instantly to cruise speed, a short "boost" effect plays to emphasise the jump. This comes after the MVP (tasks T-008 and T-009, final release). Its look: Visual style, Decisions.
- The reference feel is the Unity prototype on its Grass stage, the only stage the board played. Grass has no off-road slowdown, so the Isometric stage's off-road damping is not part of the reference.
- The camera zoom is a player setting: a slider in the pause menu (HUD and menus, Decisions), with the Unity prototype's range, 6 to 20, and its default, 14.4. As in the Unity prototype, the player's choice is saved between sessions.
- Two camera options to try, each a pause-screen checkbox, off by default and saved like the zoom (board, 2026-10-13): **camera smoothing** (the camera follows the car with a short smooth lag instead of sitting exactly on it), and the **dynamic camera** (the zoom follows the car's speed, from a min zoom at very low speed to a max zoom at the car's top forward speed, easing there with a short delay instead of jumping; while it is on it replaces the slider's fixed zoom). The board tunes the min and max in playtests with temporary pause-screen buttons. These are a change from the Unity prototype's camera, which stays the default.
- **The camera follows the car's height** (board, 2026-10-21, after playing the elevation map, where on a height-6 rooftop the car sat high on the screen and the view was hard to read): the camera follows the car as drawn, height included, so the car stays near the middle of the screen on rooftops, ramps and in the air; the height change is eased smoothly so jumps and landings don't jerk the view. (T-228)
- The car's top forward speed is **half** what it was: 16.5 units a second instead of 33 (the top-speed multiplier on the cruise speed goes from 3 to 1.5; the cruise speed of 11 is unchanged). Tried in the board's quick tuning on T-124 and kept.
- The Godot car runs its physics at 50 steps per second, like the Unity prototype, so the per-step values carry over exactly. If 50 turns out not to be possible, the values are converted for 60.
- The car's physics stays flat top-down, as in the Unity prototype, and the Godot version draws it isometrically.
- The board playtested the Godot drift prototype in the isometric view and is very happy with it. The game uses the isometric view and the Unity values, with two changes: the top speed is **3.0 times** cruise speed (Unity: 2.5), and **physics interpolation is on**, for smoother motion between physics steps. The jump to cruise speed stays at 11.

- **Arrow-key tricks, prototype** (board, 2026-10-16): a standalone trick prototype to playtest the idea of tricks done by chaining arrow keys while driving with W/A/S/D. One trick for now: Up, Right, Down, Left in a row makes the car do a **side flip to the right** (a full roll around its long axis) with the illusion of a small jump; the car's physics stays on the ground. A live HUD in the bottom-right corner shows the four arrow keys as they are pressed, and completing the sequence plays a comic-style confirmation animation. The roll is generated with PixelLab for one car direction first. Not part of the MVP; it tries out the far-future trick idea (Open questions). Tasks T-150 to T-153.

- **Trick prototype, round 2** (board, 2026-10-17, after playing it): during any trick's jump the car flies over obstacles and walls, and clearing one earns a jump-over bonus that counts as a trick. Two more arrow tricks: **Up, Left, Down, Right**, the side flip to the left (the mirror of the right one), and **Up, Down, Up, Up**, the nose launch: the car leans onto its nose, then springs forward into the air with its nose flipping up as it flies, and lands, like a toy car pressed down at the back and let go. The board's verdict on the first roll art: fine for a prototype, but it looks flat, like flipping a 2D image ("Paper Mario"), with no depth or sense of physics. Asked how to give the tricks real depth (a 3D car rendered as pixels, more PixelLab, or keep the code stand-in), the board first chose to keep the code stand-in, then the same day replaced that: the tricks get full generated art made with PixelLab's rotation tools (`/rotate` with its tilt, in-betweens from `/interpolation-v2`), not the code stand-in (board, 2026-10-17: "scratch the current way, i want to do it with the full art"). Sample first: one direction for the side roll and the nose pop, then all 16 directions after the board approves. Tasks T-154 to T-157.

- **Trick prototype, round 3** (board, 2026-10-17): while the car is on the ground, the last pressed arrow key that is still held tilts the car slightly toward that direction (relative to the car, matching the tricks), as live feedback. **Wall grinds:** landing from a trick close to the edge of a wall (walls, not boulders) locks the car into a grind, sitting across the wall nearly perpendicular but slightly diagonal, carrying on along the wall in the direction it was going and slowing as it burns speed, with discrete sparks; the grind counts as a trick. Space (a new jump key) or another arrow trick exits it, keeping the speed and direction along the wall. Tasks T-158 to T-160.

- **The trick prototype is a reference; tricks are rebuilt on real height** (board, 2026-10-19): building the trick prototype before an elevation system was a mistake, since its jumps only fake height. The tricks are rebuilt on the elevation system below, once the board trusts it. The prototype is not merged: its trick definitions, animations, numbers and art stay as a reference (Content, "Trick prototype (reference)"), its code on the branch `hold/trick-prototype`, and tasks T-151 to T-160 are cancelled.

- **Elevation** (board, 2026-10-17; go-ahead 2026-10-19): the car gets a real height above the ground, separate from where it is on the map, with gravity, a takeoff speed and a landing. It can drive up a ramp onto a raised area, drive along it, and jump off its edge or off a ramp. The illusion of height in this 2D game: the car's drawing lifts up the screen with its height while its round shadow stays on the ground under it (the car is always drawn at its normal size; the board tried drawing it bigger when high and removed it, task T-192). Built first in a test scene, the way the drift prototype was, not in the real map. The map side (raised areas and ramps) is in Level design. Later, on top of it: the car jumping on its own, grinds, and rotating the car in the air (the trick system, rebuilt from the reference); far later, maybe loops.

- **Elevation test scene, the board's playtest** (board, 2026-10-19): the board likes the physics: how the car drives, how it looks going up the ramp, and jumping over the platform ("amazing"). Three changes before it merges:
  - **See-through raised areas.** When the car is behind a raised area it must not disappear: the raised area turns see-through the way the map's buildings do (Level design, "When a building fades"), reusing the same logic. And driving into a raised area's side from behind (its top-right or top-left side on screen, where the car is hidden) must not make the car suddenly draw over the raised area.
  - **No "bigger when high" option.** The board tried drawing the car bigger with height and didn't like it: the option is removed, and the car is always drawn at its normal size.
  - **A round shadow.** The shadow is a circle right under the centre of the car, in the same colour and feel as now, instead of the rectangle, so the player sees where the car is on the ground when it is in the air.
- **No sprite shadow in the air** (board, 2026-10-20, from the elevation sample map's screenshots): the car's sprite has a drop shadow drawn into most of its 16 frames, which travels up with the car when it is in the air, beside the round shadow. In the air the car is drawn without it, so only the round shadow shows; on the ground it keeps the sprite's own shadow, as now. The shadowless frames are made by a free script, not PixelLab (Visual style, Decisions, "The car without its shadow").
- **No drift smoke or tyre marks in the air** (board, 2026-10-21, after playing the full game on the elevation map): while the car is airborne it leaves no drift smoke and no tyre marks, even if the drift keys are held; both come back when it lands (tyre marks: board, 2026-10-21, same day). (T-206)
- **Every ramp launches the car off its top** (board, 2026-10-30, audit): leaving a ramp through its top end launches the car, whether or not anything stands at the top, and the faster the car, the higher it flies, so a fast car reaches roofs it couldn't before. Leaving a ramp over its long side is still a fall. (T-411)
- **Driving power-ups** (board, 2026-10-31): the car can gain driving abilities during a run, as gifts for completed missions (Game loop architecture, Decisions, "Mission packs"). Each has an icon and an upgrade progression (tiers, like the weapons); the tiers and their numbers are the Driving & Drift Agent's proposals for the playtest. The four: **Rev Charge**: hold accelerate (W) and brake (S) at the same time to charge a powerful boost that fires when the brake is released, with a visible charging and boost effect. **Jump**: press Space to do a small hop (its airtime counts towards missions). **Bouncy Bumpers**: increase the bounce distance from crashing into obstacles (the wall bounce, T-435). **Rusty Overcoat**: the car deals damage to enemies on contact. (goal G-009)
- **The Jump clears obstacles** (board, 2026-11-01, after playing goal G-009): with the Jump power-up, Space hops the car over obstacles: it passes over an obstacle while it is higher than the obstacle's top, and meets it as a wall when it is lower. Taller buildings and the map's edge still block it. The car already takes no damage from enemies while it is above them (the board confirmed it in the playtest). Rusty Overcoat only adds damage to the enemies it touches: it never stops their hit on the car (the board found it made the car take no damage at all).

### Content

#### Prototypes so far

The board built two drift prototypes before this project:

- **The older prototype, in Unity: the board is very happy with it.** It is at `C:\Users\andre\drift-to-survive` on the board's machine (Unity 6000.3, project name DriftSurvivors). The reference is its current state. Its driving values come from the project files (the vehicle data asset); the board's earlier pause-menu tuning is no longer read by the current code, and only the camera zoom is still a saved pause-menu setting (in the Windows registry). Its driving and drifting are the reference for Solid Carbide. It also has reverse on the S key.
- **The newer prototype: the board is not happy with how it turned out.** It is not used as a reference and will not be analysed.

A report on how driving, drifting and reverse behave in the Unity prototype, with the preparations needed to reproduce them in Godot, is done (task T-006). See References.

#### Unity prototype summary

Facts from the report (Unity prototype report, sections 1 to 7). No new decisions.

- The car is a top-down 2D physics body. Every physics step (50 per second) the code sets its velocity directly, split into speed along the nose and speed across it. No forces.
- The handling values come from the car's data asset in the project files. The current code reads no driving value from the registry; the only saved setting that still matters is the camera zoom.
- W snaps the car to a cruise speed of 11 units per second (the Unity car is 1 unit long), then speed climbs in a straight line to a top speed of 27.5. Letting go coasts down in a straight line.
- S brakes in a straight line while moving forward, snaps to 11 backwards at zero, then climbs to 27.5 backwards. W always wins over S.
- A and D rotate the car at a fixed 191.9 degrees per second at every speed, including standing still.
- The drift comes from sideways speed being kept at 98% per physics step: held W + A or W + D builds a wide slide that levels off near a 75 degree drift angle at about 34 units per second.
- A coded "drift amount" ramps from 0 to 1 in 0.08 seconds and back in 0.33 seconds. With the current car values it does not change the handling; it drives the drift effects.
- The camera is orthographic, sits exactly on the car every frame, never rotates, and has no smoothing or look-ahead. Its zoom (default 14.4, half the visible height in world units) is a saved pause-menu setting.

#### Godot drift prototype

The Godot copy of the Unity car (task T-012), for the board's playtest.

- **Where:** the scene `game/scenes/drift_prototype/drift_prototype.tscn`, the project's main scene, with its code in `game/scripts/driving/`. How it is built, its keys and how to run it: `game/docs/driving/drift.md`, "Drift prototype".
- **How to run it:** open `game/` in Godot 4.6 and press F5, or run `"$GODOT_BIN" --path game` from the repo root.
- **Controls:** W, S, A and D as in the Unity prototype (Unity prototype report, section 2). Tab opens the tuning panel, V switches the view. No jump, arrow keys or gamepad.
- **Ground:** flat and empty, like the Unity Grass stage, with a grid (a thin line every unit, a stronger one every 5 units) and a marker at the start point.
- **Movement:** the Unity prototype report's section 4, step by step, at 50 physics steps per second, with the Unity values (report, section 5). The GUT tests check it against the report's numbers. One difference: the comparison that decides whether W snaps to cruise speed (and S to reverse cruise speed) ignores rounding errors below 0.000000001 units per second. Without it, at some headings the forward speed reads back a hair under cruise speed and W would snap to cruise speed on every step instead of climbing to top speed.
- **Boost signal:** the car signals each time W makes it jump up to cruise speed, with the speed before the jump and whether W was just pressed. During a held W + A or W + D drift the slide pulls the forward speed under cruise speed, so the jump happens on most steps of the drift too (with W not just pressed).
- **Scale and camera:** 16 pixels per unit, the scale of the placeholder car sheets. The camera sits exactly on the drawn car, never rotates and has no smoothing or look-ahead. Its zoom is Unity's orthographic size, half the visible height in units.
- **View switch:** the physics always runs in the flat top-down world. V, or the panel's "Isometric view" toggle, switches only the drawing: flat top-down with the flat placeholder sheet, or a standard 2:1 isometric projection (screen = (x - y, (x + y) / 2)) of the same world with the isometric sheet. It can be switched mid-drive; the car's position, speed and rotation do not change.
- **Collisions (task T-033):** the car's 1 by 1 unit body bounces off walls, buildings, the map's edge and boulders, and drives through enemies without bouncing. How hard it bounces is a tuning panel slider, "Wall bounce", in a "Collisions" group at the bottom of the panel: the share of its speed into the wall the car keeps, bouncing back (0 = no bounce, 1 = full bounce); the Unity prototype has no bounce. Since task T-435 (Decisions, "The car bounces off walls") the bounce wins over W: after a hit, W held with the nose towards the wall no longer snaps the car back to cruise speed (which kept it pressed against the wall) but speeds it up at a steady rate, so the car first bounces away, then W brings it back; turning away or letting go of W ends that at once, and W is never switched off. The bounce grows with the hit speed up to a cap. A wall hit also ends the drift in progress (Decisions, "A wall hit ends the drift", task T-438): `car.gd` clears the model's `is_drifting` on the hit step, so the trick detector pays the drift once, for the time up to the hit, and a player still holding the keys starts a new drift on the next step; in a run the crash pays it first, then the 50% combo cut, as for any crash. Proposals for the playtest, on the same panel group: "Wall bounce" 0.4 (was 0.25), "Wall bounce: hardest hit" 16.5 units/s (the top speed) and "Wall bounce: W pull-back" 12 units/s per second: a head-on hit at cruise speed bounces about 0.9 units away, at top speed or faster about 1.75. The prototype has a test room for trying it: a few walls and a boulder 3 units across. The car also signals each hit (for the combo) and can be knocked back by other code (minions, meteors). Details, the collision layers and the knockback function: `game/docs/driving/collisions.md`, "Car collisions".
- **Tricks (task T-079):** the car finds the three tricks (Decisions) in its own driving without changing how it drives, and signals each one with its id for the combo and the popups. "Drifting" is the Unity definition (W or S held together with A or D); any step without it is a break. An extended drift is one whole unbroken drift, paid once when it ends (since T-246; it paid every full second before). A 360 is each full turn of the heading in one direction during one unbroken drift; turning back the other way or a break starts the count again. An alternate drift is each switch between a forward drift (W) and a backward drift (S) with the same steering side, within limits the board tunes in the tuning panel's "Tricks" group: the switch from one drift to the other may take at most 0.5 seconds, both drifts must last at least 0.3 seconds (the trick counts when the new one reaches it), and A or D must stay held on the same side during the switch. These three values are proposals. The tuning panel's readout shows the last trick. The signal, the trick ids and the details: `game/docs/driving/tricks.md`, "Tricks".
- **Camera options (task T-123):** the two camera options (Decisions, 2026-10-13), both off by default; with both off the camera is exactly as above. They work the same in the drift prototype and in the run (also a run started from the main menu), and are saved with the zoom in the player's settings. **Camera smoothing:** each physics step the camera closes 1 - e^(-8 x step time) of its gap to the drawn car (rate 8 per second), so it trails a moving car by about its speed / 8 (about 4 units at the top speed of 33 units per second, under a third of the default half-height of 14.4) and catches up within about half a second once the car stops. **Dynamic camera:** the zoom's target is the min zoom at a standstill and the max zoom at the car's top forward speed, in a straight line in between (half speed: halfway), using the car's speed in any direction as a share of its top forward speed (capped at 1), so a fast slide or a fast reverse also zooms out. The zoom eases toward the target at a rate of 3 per second (about 63% of the way in a third of a second, 95% in one second), so it never jumps. While it is on it replaces the slider's zoom; moving the slider while it is on shows that zoom at once (so the board can see the value it is about to set as min or max), and the camera eases back to the speed's zoom once the car moves. Turning it off goes straight back to the slider's zoom. **Min and max:** proposed 11 (zoomed in at a standstill) and 17 (zoomed out at top speed), around the default 14.4 and within the slider's 6 to 20; the board sets them in playtests with the pause screen's buttons (task T-124), which take the slider's current zoom. The two rates are proposals in one place in the code. Settings keys, the API for the pause screen and where the saved min and max can be read: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/camera.md`, "Camera options".
- **Camera follows the car's height (task T-228; the decision is in Decisions, 2026-10-21):** the camera's position is the ground part plus a height part. The ground part follows the car's map position as before, with the camera options (smoothing, dynamic camera). The height part is the lift of the car's drawing (16 pixels per unit of height, straight up the screen) and **eases** toward it at a rate of 4 per second (a proposal, `HEIGHT_EASE_RATE` in `camera_follow.gd`): about 63% of a change in a quarter of a second and 95% in 0.75 s, so a jump, a landing or a ramp climb never jerks the view, and the car sits near the middle of the screen on a rooftop once it has settled (within 5 px of a height-6 rooftop's 96 px after 0.75 s). While the car rises or falls, it is off-centre by the part not yet eased (at most the full lift). A new run or a view switch snaps the camera straight onto the lifted car. At height 0 the lift is 0 and the camera is exactly as before, so the street is unchanged. It is used in the run on the elevation map, the drive-only elevation sample scene and the elevation test scene; the drift prototype has no heights.
- **Tuning panel (Tab):** one slider per setting in the report's section 8 list except off-road damping and the physics rate (cruise speed, top speed multiplier, time to top speed, coast slowdown, turn speed, steering sensitivity, base sideways grip, drift grip at low and high speed, drift speed reference, drift enter and exit rates), plus the camera zoom (6 to 20, starting at 14.4), and the side slip out of a drift's four sliders in their own group (task T-278; "Side slip out of a drift (task T-278)" below). Each slider applies live and has a tooltip showing the Unity value. The sliders start at the game's values (Decisions, 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-10), and one button resets everything to them. A "Physics interpolation" toggle (on, the game's value; Unity has it off) smooths the motion between physics steps. A readout shows speed, drift angle and drift amount. Nothing is saved between runs.

#### Elevation test scene

The test scene for the car's real height (Decisions, "Elevation"; tasks T-182 to T-187), built like the Godot drift prototype and kept apart from the real map. How it is built: `game/docs/level/elevation-test-scene.md`, "Elevation test scene".

- **Where:** `game/scenes/elevation_test/elevation_test.tscn`. It is not the project's main scene and no menu leads to it.
- **How to run it:** open the scene in the Godot editor and press F6 (Run Current Scene), or run `"$GODOT_BIN" --path game res://scenes/elevation_test/elevation_test.tscn` from the repo root. W, S, A and D drive as in the drift prototype; there is no tuning panel, view switch, pause screen or on-screen text. The car starts on the street east of the ramp's foot, facing it (a proposal), so W drives straight up the ramp.
- **What is in it:** the drift prototype's car (the same driving, at 50 physics steps per second, with physics interpolation on), its camera (the saved zoom and camera options) and its isometric view, on the street with its grid, plus one raised platform and one ramp up to it (Level design, "Elevation test scene").
- **What the car's height does** (tasks T-183 and T-184): the car has a height above the ground, separate from where it is on the map. On the ground and on the ramp it follows the ground. Leaving the ramp's top climbing at 4 units/s or more, it takes off with the ramp's slope; driving off a drop-off edge or a ramp's side, it falls. In the air, gravity of 12 units/s² pulls it down until it lands on whatever ground is under it, the platform's top or the street. In the air the car keeps its takeoff speed and direction and the keys only spin it (task T-219; Content, "Aerial tricks (task T-219)", "No drifting in the air"). From the street, a drop-off edge or a ramp's side higher than 0.1 units is a wall the car bounces off; lower steps are curbs it drives over. Details and the numbers: "Elevation: the platform's sides" below and `game/docs/level/elevation-test-scene.md`, "The car's height (T-183)".
- **The drawing (task T-185):** the car's drawing is lifted straight up the screen by its height, 16 pixels per unit (the drawing's scale), so on the platform it sits 48 pixels up. Its **shadow**, a dark opaque filled circle about 1 unit across (a proposal; task T-192), an ellipse twice as wide as tall on screen, not turning with the car, stays centred at the car's map position on the ground under it: on the platform's top or the ramp when over them, on the street otherwise. Its size doesn't change with height (a proposal; the car is always drawn at its normal size: the bigger-when-high option was removed).
