(Superseded by T-228, 2026-10-21: the camera now follows the car as drawn, height included, see "Camera follows the car's height" below.)
- **A round shadow, and no bigger-when-high (task T-192, board's playtest 2026-10-19):** the board tried drawing the car bigger when high (task T-187) and did not like it: the option is removed, the car is always drawn at its normal size. The shadow is now a filled circle on the ground right under the centre of the car's map position (the platform's top or the ramp when over them), about 1 unit across (a proposal, for the board's playtest), drawn in the isometric view as an ellipse twice as wide as it is tall. Same dark, opaque colour with hard pixel edges as before; it does not turn with the car and does not change with height (changed 2026-10-31, T-454: it now shrinks as the car rises, Visual style, Decisions, "Shadows shrink with height"). Where it sits, its depth order and the see-through stay as they were. See `game/docs/level/elevation-test-scene.md`, "The round shadow, and no bigger-when-high (T-192)".
- **The platform and ramp art (task T-186):** PixelLab art (`game/art/elevation/platform.png` and `ramp.png`) is drawn over the platform and the ramp, made from 3 generations and fitted to the sizes in the height data. How it is built: `game/docs/level/elevation-test-scene.md`, "The platform and ramp art (T-186)". Screenshots: [elevation-final-art](drifting/elevation-final-art.png), [elevation-final-art-platform](drifting/elevation-final-art-platform.png).
- **The script drawing (fallback):** the first version, still used if the art files are missing: flat-coloured top faces with a grid every unit, the east and south side faces the isometric view shows, and light edges. Grey-blue for the platform, a dull sand colour for the ramp's top (proposals), none of Greenbull's colours, no semi-transparent pixels. The five screenshots below show this version.
- **Depth order:** the car and its shadow are drawn under a raised area they are behind (their centre north or west of it on the map, not wholly east or south of it, and lower than its top), and over it when on it, above it or in front of it. Each is placed on its own: a car high above the street behind the platform is drawn over it while its shadow on the street is hidden under it. Behind is judged by the car's centre (task T-191): driving into the platform's back sides (top-left and top-right on screen), the car's centre stops at the side while its body reaches into it, and the old rule (the whole body north or west of it) drew the car over the platform for the moment of the hit. Now it stays under it through the hit.
- **See-through raised areas (task T-191):** when the car is behind the platform or the ramp and it covers the car on screen, the whole area fades like the map's buildings, with their numbers: to 15% visible over 0.15 seconds, and back over 0.15 seconds when it no longer covers the car (Level design, Content, "When a building fades"). The code is shared with the buildings rather than copied: the numbers are the map's (`mvp_map.gd`), the fade step is the buildings' (`map_building.gd`) and so is the car's on-screen shape. Where it lives: `game/docs/level/elevation-test-scene.md`, "See-through raised areas (T-191)". Screenshots: the car behind the see-through platform and at a wall hit on each back side, and the same hits with the fade off (the car hidden under the platform): `art-archive/T-191/screenshots/`.
- **The car's sheet in the air (task T-205; Decisions, "No sprite shadow in the air"):** while the car's height is above the ground under it, the isometric car is drawn from the shadowless sheet (`car_iso_noshadow.png`, same layout, same frame for the heading), so only the round shadow shows; on the ground, a rooftop or a ramp it is drawn from `car_iso.png` with its own shadow. The sheet switches on the physics step the car takes off and the step it lands. The run and the drift prototype have no ground heights, so their car never switches. Screenshots: `art-archive/T-205/screenshots/`.
- **Screenshots:** the car on the street, on the ramp, on the platform, in the air past the platform's south edge, and behind the platform (only its roof shows): [elevation-ground](drifting/elevation-ground.png), [elevation-ramp](drifting/elevation-ramp.png), [elevation-platform](drifting/elevation-platform.png), [elevation-air](drifting/elevation-air.png), [elevation-behind](drifting/elevation-behind.png).
- **Before T-191:** a car behind the platform was hidden by it (the last screenshot, taken before the see-through existed).

#### Elevation: the platform's sides (task T-184)

How the sides of a raised area and its ramp meet the car, in the elevation test scene (Decisions, "Elevation"; the ground: Level design, "Raised areas and ramps"). The docs left these open; each point below is a **proposal for the board's playtest**, built on the car's existing collisions (Godot drift prototype, "Collisions"). How it is built and its one number: `game/docs/level/elevation-test-scene.md`, "The platform's sides (T-184)".

- **A drop-off edge met from the ground below** (proposal): for a car lower than the platform's top, the edge is a wall. The car stops at it and bounces off it like off any wall, with the same "Wall bounce" share, and signals the hit like any wall hit. It stays on the ground. A car high enough to clear the edge (in the air, above the top) passes over it.
- **Landing** (proposal): a jump that ends over the platform's top lands on the top; one that ends beside it lands on the ground. A car in the air that would enter the platform's outline lower than its top meets its side as a wall (it bounces off and keeps falling beside it), so it never ends a physics step inside the platform.
- **The ramp's sides** (its two long sides, not its climbing end or its top; proposal): the same as a drop-off edge, a step of the ramp's height at that point. Driving off a side from on the ramp, the car leaves the ground at the ramp's height there and falls to the ground with gravity. From the ground beside the ramp, the side is a wall as high as the ramp at that point.
- **Curbs** (proposal): a step of the ground no higher than 0.1 units is driven over, not a wall or a drop; near the ramp's foot, where its sides are that low, the car drives onto the ramp from the side.

#### The car's footprint (task T-411)

How the car's drawn size meets the sides of raised areas (rooftops, ramps, T-405's platforms) (Decisions, "Elevation", and the drawn size, 2026-10-07). Before, only the car's centre met them: the drawn front half drove into a rooftop's or ramp's side before the car bounced, turning beside a side swept the nose into it, and tyre marks streaked down the wall at a roof edge. How it is built: `game/docs/level/elevation-test-scene.md`, "The car's footprint (T-411)".

- **The drawn car stops at a side** (proposal for the board's playtest; open question (b) below): the whole drawn outline, 1 wide and 3 long, meets the sides by the rule of "Elevation: the platform's sides" (above), so the bumper, a corner or a flank bounces off as soon as it touches, head-on, at an angle and while turning: a turn into a side stops like a drive into it. The ramp the car is on is never a wall for its own nose or tail, and touching platforms of the same height have no wall between them.
- **Unchanged:** the 1 by 1 physics body for buildings, boulders and the map's edge (Decisions, 2026-10-07); falling off a roof edge and landing, which still go by the centre (open question (a) below); the curb height. Near a ramp's foot, a side is a curb only where it is under 0.1 high under every point of the car, so the car can no longer slip on over the side with its centre at the lowest 0.4 units and its flank over a taller part.
- **Ramp tops** (Decisions, "Every ramp launches the car off its top"): already built by T-400; T-411 checks a free-standing ramp launches, higher at 16.5 units/s than at 11.
- **Tyre marks at a roof edge:** a rear tyre hanging over an edge (its ground more than 0.1 below the car) lays no mark and its mark ends; a new one starts when it is back on the ground, as after a jump (Decisions, "No drift smoke or tyre marks in the air").
- **Open questions for the board** (the T-411 assessment; today's choices kept): (a) when a car crawling off a roof edge tips off: when its middle passes the edge (today), when its front wheels leave, or as soon as the nose leaves; (b) whether the drawn body should bounce off a rooftop's or ramp's side as soon as the bumper touches (built, as a proposal); (c) whether a crawling car (under 4 units/s) launches off a ramp's top too, or whether there is a minimum speed (today: under 4 it rolls off and falls); (d) whether the nose may still enter skyscrapers by 1 unit (the 1 by 1 body, today).
- **Screenshots:** before and after, the car pressed against the platform's south, north and west sides and the ramp's side in the elevation test scene: `art-archive/T-411/screenshots/compare_before_after.png` (and the `before_*.png`, `after_*.png` frames).

#### Elevation: the three layers of the sample map (task T-195)

The car's height (above) checked on the elevation sample map's three layers, the street (0), the first-floor rooftops (3) and the second-floor rooftops (6) (Level design, "Elevation sample map"). It works there unchanged: the ramps whose foot is on a rooftop (3 to 6) need no special case, since the car's height always follows, leaves and lands on the ground under it, whatever that ground's height. The numbers (gravity, the takeoff speed and factor, the curb height) are unchanged. How it is tested and run: `game/docs/level/elevation-sample-map.md`, "The car's height on the three layers (T-195)".

- **What the tests show**, with the real car code, picking the ramps and rooftops from the map's file by their heights: up a 0-to-3 ramp and a 3-to-6 ramp the car follows the slope; off a 3-to-6 ramp's top at cruise speed it takes off along the slope, as at the test scene's ramp; driving off a height-6 rooftop's side it falls and lands on the height-3 rooftop under it, or on the street; on a height-3 rooftop, the side of a height-6 rooftop is a wall it bounces off. In the sample map scene, the MVP map's tall buildings and boulders block the car at every height it can reach: on the street, on 3, on 6 and in the air (they are walls in the flat world, so no jump clears them; a proposal kept from the MVP map).
- **The scripted drive** (`game/tools/drive_elevation_sample.sh`, or `.ps1`, from the repo root): drives the car, headless, from the street up a 0-to-3 ramp, up a 3-to-6 ramp and off a height-6 edge, the way a player would (W held, steering toward the route), and prints each layer reached, every jump, the maximum height and the airtime off the edge. With today's layout and numbers: height 3 at 1.8 s, height 6 at 5.3 s, a small hop off each ramp's top (up to 3.75 and 6.89), and 1.00 s in the air falling the 6 units off the edge onto the street. Plot of the height over time: [art-archive/T-195/screenshots/height-over-time.png](../art-archive/T-195/screenshots/height-over-time.png).

#### Aerial tricks (task T-219)

The air 180 and air 360 (Decisions, "Aerial tricks"), built in `game/scripts/driving/trick_detector.gd` from the car's heading and its airborne state; how it is built is in `game/docs/driving/tricks.md`, "Tricks". The detector only reads the driving. Two changes to the driving in the air come from the board (below): no drifting in the air, and faster turning in the air. Ground driving is unchanged. Every point below is a proposal for the board's playtest.

- **No drifting in the air** (Decisions, "Aerial tricks", board 2026-10-21, after playing T-219): from the first step that starts with the car in the air, the driving model keeps the car's velocity (speed and direction on the map) exactly as it was at takeoff. There is no speeding up, braking, steering of the path, grip or drift. W, S, A and D only spin the body: A and D at the air turn rate, and W and S alone do nothing. The car is not drifting in the air (its drift amount fades as whenever it stops drifting), so there is no drift smoke or tyre marks, no drift likes, no LONG DRIFT! and no drift sound, and the exhaust flamethrower, which fires while drifting, is off in the air too.
  - **Not changed:** the takeoff step is still a ground step. A wall or building side met in the air still bounces the car, and an enemy's knockback still pushes it, as before; neither is driving.
  - **Landing:** driving resumes on the step after the landing, from the heading the car landed with and the velocity it kept.
    - Landing straight on, it simply drives on.
    - Landing at an angle to its path, the part of its speed along the new nose becomes its forward speed. The part across the nose is a sideways slide that fades with the normal grip: 0.98 is kept per step when not drifting, so about a third of it is left after a second. In effect it lands into a drift-like slide.
    - With W held, a forward speed under cruise snaps up to cruise along the new nose, as W always does.
    - Landing backwards (more than 90 degrees off its path) with W held, the car snaps to cruise speed forward along its new nose, which is a sudden turnaround. Holding A or D with W or S on landing is a normal drift from that step.

- **What counts:** only heading turned on physics steps that end with the car in the air (from the takeoff step to the step before landing). Turning on the ground, before the takeoff or after the landing, counts nothing, and turns in two airtimes don't add up. The turn is counted in one direction; turning back starts a new count, and the airtime keeps its largest one, so a 180 followed by a small wiggle back still counts. Letting go of A or D in the air keeps the count. W makes no difference (steering turns the car with or without it).
- **Paid on landing:** the tricks are given on the step the car lands, not mid-air, so the turn must be finished before landing, and the popup shows as the car lands. A run that resets mid-air (a new car) forgets the airtime.
- **A 360 counts only the 360, not its 180 too.** The airtime's turn is paid in half turns: 180 gives AIR 180!, 360 gives AIR 360!, **540 gives AIR 360! and AIR 180!**, **720 gives two AIR 360!**.
- **Worth:** `air_one_eighty` adds 0.25 to the combo (as much as a drift 360) and `air_three_sixty` 0.5 (twice the turn, as much as an alternate drift, the hardest ground trick), in `game/data/combo.json`, `trick_add`.
- **A drift 360 that spans the jump: each spin pays once** (Decisions, "Aerial tricks", board 2026-10-21; this replaces the first build's independent counting). Turning on a step that ends in the air counts only for the aerial tricks and never towards the drift's FULL 360!, so an air spin with W held pays AIR 360! (or AIR 180!) and no FULL 360!.
  - **At takeoff**, since there is no drifting in the air, the airtime is a break in the drift. A drift 360 in progress starts again from zero, and a drift in progress ends there and pays (T-246). A drift segment ends too, for the alternate drift's switch timing. After landing, a drift starts counting from the landing. (Before "no drifting in the air", a drift 360 in progress was kept through the airtime.)
- **Faster turning in the air** (Decisions, "Aerial tricks"; the board chose this after the first build found the 360 out of reach): in the air the car turns `air_turn_multiplier` times faster than on the ground. This is a tuning value in `game/scripts/driving/car_tuning.gd`, with a slider in the drift prototype's tuning panel ("In the air"). **Halved in T-269** (Decisions, "Slower air turn, upgradable", board 2026-10-22): the base is now **1.25**, which is 239.9 degrees a second (4.8 per physics step) in the air; the first build had 2.5 (479.75). The ground rate stays 191.9. A garage bonus (T-270) is added to the multiplier at a run's start (`air_turn_bonus`, set by `apply_air_turn_bonus()`; 0 without the upgrade). At 1.25 an air 180 takes 38 steps (0.76 s) and is reachable off the tallest rooftop (a fall counts 49 steps, 0.98 s); an air 360 takes about 76 and is not. A 360 off that rooftop becomes reachable from a total of about **1.9** (1.85 is just short, 1.95 works; 2.0 has a margin), so the upgrade's top levels should reach about 2.0 or more. The faster rate applies on every step that starts with the car in the air, so the takeoff step still turns at the ground rate.
- **What it gives on today's map** (measured in the tests): the highest drop is a height-6 rooftop onto the street, 1.0 s, of which 49 steps count as in the air.
  - **A 360 takes 38 steps (0.76 s).** A player who steers the whole fall makes it with **about 0.2 s to spare**: starting the turn 10 steps (0.2 s) late still gives AIR 360!, while 12 steps late gives only AIR 180!.
  - **A 180 takes 19 steps (0.38 s)**, half of that, so it also fits a hop off a ramp's top (about 0.7 s).
  - The most a rooftop fall can turn is about 470 degrees, so a 540 can't be done on today's map.
  - **The board, 2026-11-01:** an AIR 360! is reachable on today's map at the base air-turn speed: with enough speed a ramp throws the car far across the map, much longer in the air than a rooftop fall. The rooftop-fall numbers above stand; they are not the longest airtime.
- **The recordings:**
  - [air_360_run_straight.gif](../art-archive/T-219/screenshots/air_360_run_straight.gif), the current build (no drifting in the air), in a run on the elevation map. The car drives off a height-6 rooftop's side with W and holds W and A for the whole fall. It keeps flying in its takeoff direction while it spins about 470 degrees: the camera follows the car, so the street and boulders scroll past steadily in one direction while the car turns on the spot over its shadow. It lands to AIR 360! +0.5 alone, with no LONG DRIFT! and no FULL 360!. Popup: [air_360_run_straight_popup.png](../art-archive/T-219/screenshots/air_360_run_straight_popup.png).
  - Kept from before "no drifting in the air": [air_360_run_pays_once.gif](../art-archive/T-219/screenshots/air_360_run_pays_once.gif), with the faster air turn and each spin paying once, in a run on the elevation map. The car drives off a height-6 rooftop's side with W and turns with A for the whole fall (about 470 degrees). Nothing pops mid-air. It lands to AIR 360! +0.5, with LONG DRIFT! +0.05 from the drift's seconds, and no FULL 360!. Popup: [air_360_run_pays_once_popup.png](../art-archive/T-219/screenshots/air_360_run_pays_once_popup.png).
  - Kept from before each spin paid once: [air_360_run.gif](../art-archive/T-219/screenshots/air_360_run.gif), with the faster air turn, in a run on the elevation map. The car drives off a height-6 rooftop's side with W and turns with A for the whole fall (50 steps, about 470 degrees). FULL 360! +0.25 pops mid-air, and the car lands to AIR 360! +0.5 (with LONG DRIFT! +0.05). Popup: [air_360_run_popup.png](../art-archive/T-219/screenshots/air_360_run_popup.png).
  - From the first build, at the ground turn rate (kept, not re-recorded): [air_180_run.gif](../art-archive/T-219/screenshots/air_180_run.gif), the same drive turning about 188 degrees in the air and landing to AIR 180! +0.25. Also [air_360_staged_drop.gif](../art-archive/T-219/screenshots/air_360_staged_drop.gif), a staged drop: the car is let go 22 units above the gravel square, zoomed out, and turns a full circle in 95 steps to AIR 360! +0.5. Popups: [air_180_popup.png](../art-archive/T-219/screenshots/air_180_popup.png), [air_360_popup.png](../art-archive/T-219/screenshots/air_360_popup.png).

#### Airtime trick (task T-242)

The board's airtime trick (Decisions, "Airtime trick", 2026-10-21): every airtime is a trick of its own, paid on landing by how long the car was in the air. Built in `game/scripts/driving/trick_detector.gd` (how: `game/docs/driving/effects.md`, "Airtime trick"); it reads the car's airborne state like the aerial tricks and changes no driving. Its popup is "HANG TIME!" with its amount (HUD and menus, Content, T-241). The live counter while airborne is T-243's. Every number below is a proposal for the board's playtest, in `game/data/combo.json`, `airtime`.

- **Seconds** are the sum of the physics steps that end in the air (0.02 s each), so a rooftop fall of 49 steps is 0.98 s.
- **Amount** = airtime (to hundredths) times `per_second`, nothing under `min_seconds`, held at `max_add`, rounded to hundredths. It adds to the combo like any trick (held at the combo's cap; at the cap only the name shows).
- **Proposed numbers and why:**
  - `min_seconds` **0.3**: a curb or a small hop stays under it, so only a real jump pays and the popup never fires for nothing. Ramp tops and rooftop falls (about 0.7 s to 1.0 s) are well over it.
  - `per_second` **0.2**: the rooftop fall (0.98 s) pays **0.20** and a 0.7 s ramp hop 0.14. That is less than an AIR 180! (0.25), since an airtime alone asks for no steering.
  - `max_add` **0.6**: reached at 3 s, a little above an AIR 360! (0.5), so a very long fall is worth about a spin and a bit, never much more than the hardest aerial trick. Today's highest drop is 1.0 s, so the cap is not reached on today's map.
- **Next to the aerial tricks:** it pays on the same landing step, after AIR 180! or AIR 360!, as its own popup. A spin does not replace it: a 360 off a height-6 rooftop pays AIR 360! +0.5 and HANG TIME! +0.2.
- **Recording:** [airtime_run.gif](../art-archive/T-242/screenshots/airtime_run.gif), a run on the elevation map: the car drives straight off a height-6 rooftop's side, flies 0.98 s over its shadow and lands to HANG TIME! +0.2 (combo x1.2). Popup: [airtime_popup.png](../art-archive/T-242/screenshots/airtime_popup.png).

#### Drift pays once, at its end (task T-246)

The Decision "Drift pays once, at its end" (board, 2026-10-22), built in `trick_detector.gd` and `combo.json`; how: `game/docs/driving/tricks.md`, "Tricks". Nothing pays while a drift lasts. When it ends (the keys let go, W alone, or a takeoff, "No drifting in the air") it pays one `extended_drift` trick, with the existing LONG DRIFT! popup and its amount (the amount is `+0.12` for a 2.37 s drift). FULL 360!, ALT DRIFT! and the XP from drifting seconds are unchanged. The numbers are in `game/data/combo.json`, `drift_pay`; every one is a proposal for the board's playtest:

- **per_second: 0.05.** The old build paid 0.05 for each full second, so a drift pays about what it did in total (a 4 s drift: 0.20, as 4 x 0.05 before), now with hundredths of a second counting.
- **min_seconds: 1.0.** The old build paid nothing before the first full second; a shorter drift still pays nothing.
- **max: 0.5.** The same as an ALT DRIFT!, reached at 10 s of drifting, so one very long drift cannot outrun the other tricks. The old build had no cap.

The popup stays the small size (a drift is a small trick). Screenshot and GIF: `art-archive/T-246/screenshots/`.

#### A crash pays the trick in progress (task T-315)

The Decision "A crash pays the trick in progress" (board, 2026-10-28) is in Game loop architecture, Decisions. Built in `trick_detector.gd` (`settle()`), `car.gd` (`settle_tricks()`) and `run_state.gd` (the `crashed` signal); how: `game/docs/driving/tricks.md`, "Tricks", "A crash pays the trick in progress (T-315)". A crash is anything that cuts the combo: hitting a wall, a building, a boulder, the map's edge or a side of the raised ground, or any damage to the car (minions, the kaiju, meteors).

- **The extended drift:** a drift under way when the car crashes pays its `extended_drift` at once, for the time it lasted until the crash, with its LONG DRIFT! popup and amount (`drift_pay`, as for a drift that ends normally). The keys are usually still held, so the car goes on drifting: the rest of the drift after the crash is a new drift, counted from zero, and pays when it ends (or at the next crash). Since T-438 a wall hit (not damage from enemies) also ends the drift itself, so the new drift starts on the step after the hit. A drift still shorter than `drift_pay.min_seconds` is left alone and goes on counting, as before. The XP from drifting seconds is unchanged: it is paid second by second while the drift lasts, not at its end.
- **The aerial tricks and the airtime trick:** a car in the air can crash into an obstacle or be hit by an enemy. The spins turned so far (AIR 180!, AIR 360!) and the airtime so far (HANG TIME!) pay at the crash, as if the car had landed; the rest of the airtime counts from the crash and pays on landing. An airtime still under `airtime.min_seconds` with no half turn yet is left alone.
- **Not changed, since nothing of them is in progress:** the drift 360 (FULL 360!) and the alternate drift (ALT DRIFT!) pay the moment they are complete, so a crash never cuts one that would have paid; a 360 under way is not a trick yet and keeps counting as before. Thread the needle pays a short moment after the gap is crossed; a touch of either obstacle voids the pass by its own rule (Level design, Decisions, "Thread the needle"), and other crashes don't touch it.
- **The order (proposal for the playtest, approved by the board):** the trick pays first, then the crash cuts the combo (by 50% since T-329; 80% before), so its popup shows just before COMBO BROKEN! (stacked under it). The cut then takes the same share of the trick too. The other order is a switch, `crash_pays_trick_first` in `game/data/combo.json`: `false` cuts first and then adds the trick to the cut combo, which keeps the whole trick (at the old 80% cut, a 1.7 s drift from x2.0: x1.22 paid first, x1.29 cut first) and shows COMBO BROKEN! first.
- **Feel (the agent's note for the playtest):** paying first reads as cause and effect (the drift is credited, then the crash), and both popups show at once, LONG DRIFT! under COMBO BROKEN!. The drift's amount is small (at most +0.5) and most of it is cut away, so the cost of a crash stays clear.

The HUD's drift counter (T-247) is not changed: it still shows the whole drift's seconds through a crash, while the paid part starts again from zero (a question for the playtest; HUD and menus owns it). GIF and screenshot: `art-archive/T-315/screenshots/`.

#### Hype speed boost (task T-275)

The decision is in Decisions ("Hype speed boost"). Proposals for the board's playtest, kept in `game/data/combo.json` (`hype_speed`):

| Combo heat step | Combo (ComboHeat.THRESHOLDS) | Top speed above the base | Top speed (base 16.5 units/s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | below x2 | +0% | 16.5 |
| 1 | from x2 | +8% | 17.8 |
| 2 | from x3 | +16% | 19.1 |
| 3 | from x4 up | +25% | 20.6 |

- **Why these amounts:** the first step has to be felt, and the last must not break the street's spacing. +8% (1.3 units/s) is just noticeable, +16% clearly quicker, and +25% (4.1 units/s) is the reward for holding x4 or more. The steps grow as the combo climbs, as the HUD's heat steps do.
- **Acceleration:** it rises with the top speed (my call). The ramp rate is top speed over the time to top speed, and that time (2.3 s, and the garage's acceleration upgrade) is untouched, so a hot car climbs to its higher top in the same time: about 25% quicker at x4. W's snap to cruise speed (11 units/s) is unchanged. Coasting loses a share of the top speed, so it scales the same way.
- **Easing:** the bonus moves towards the step's amount at 0.2 per second (`ease_per_second`): +8% takes 0.4 s, the full +25% 1.25 s, and it falls back at the same rate, so a combo cut by a crash slows the car over about a second, not at once.
- **What does not change:** turning, drift grip, and the drift prototype (no combo, so its top speed stays 16.5). The garage's speed upgrades multiply as before: the bonus multiplies the top speed as it stands.
- **Jumps:** a fall off the tallest rooftop (height 6) lasts 1.0 s (gravity 12) and the car keeps its takeoff speed in the air, so a jump off it carries about 16.5 units at the base top speed and about 20.6 units at the top step (4.1 units farther), if the car has reached top speed on the roof. Ramps launch farther the same way. Challenge distances (Level design) were made at the base speed, so a hot car only lands farther.
- Tests: `game/tests/unit/test_hype_speed.gd`.

#### Side slip out of a drift (task T-278)

The board's "little side slip out of a drift" (Decisions). The values are **proposals for the board's own playtest**, set with sliders in the drift prototype's tuning panel. How it is built: `game/docs/driving/drift.md`, "Side slip out of a drift (T-278)".

- **How a drift ended before:** the car already slides a lot. Its sideways speed fades by only 2% every physics step, drifting or not (the Unity values), so when a drift ends the car is still about 65 degrees sideways and straightens over a second or so as its path swings round onto its nose. What stopped dead was the car's **turn**: the moment A or D was let go, the body went from turning at 192 degrees a second to not turning at all, in one step. Nothing carried on that the player had to catch.
- **What it does now:** when a drift ends on the ground because A or D is let go, the car's tail keeps swinging out a little: the body keeps turning the drift's way for a moment, so the slide grows a touch before it settles. The extra turn starts at a share of the normal turn rate and fades to nothing on its own; a touch of the other key (D after a left drift, A after a right one) catches it four times faster, and the player then steers straight. Doing nothing, it settles by itself: the whole extra turn after a full drift is about 14 degrees, a little over half of one of the car sprite's 16 directions, so it is never a spin-out. Everything else (speed, grip, the drift amount behind the smoke and marks, the tricks and their payouts) is unchanged.
- **Only after a real slide:** the slip grows with how sideways the car was when the drift ended (with the square of the drift angle, full from 60 degrees), so a quick steering touch barely slips. It only carries on a turn that was swinging the tail out, never one that was already straightening the car. Letting go of W while still steering (as in the alternate drift) has no slip, since the car is still turning.
- **Not in the air:** a slip stops when the car leaves the ground, and a drift that ends in the air or on landing has none (Decisions, "No drifting in the air").
- **The four sliders and their defaults** (group "Out of a drift: side slip"; the Unity car has no slip):
  - **Strength**, 0.35 of the turn rate (67 degrees a second) for a full drift. Small enough to read as a wobble, not a second turn. 0 turns it off.
  - **Length**, 0.4 seconds to fade with no input. Long enough to notice and catch, short enough that a player who ignores it is straight again almost at once.
  - **Catch**, 4 times faster with counter-steer: caught within a tenth of a second, so a quick tap is enough and feels decisive.
  - **Full at drift angle**, 60 degrees: a held drift settles at about 68, so every proper drift gets the full slip and small corrections don't.
- **GIFs** (in `art-archive/T-278/screenshots/`): `drift_exit_slip_prototype.gif` (the drift prototype) and `drift_exit_slip_run.gif` (a run), each with a drift with the slip off, one left alone and one caught with counter-steer, with a caption showing the slip and the drift angle; stills `prototype_slip_off_released.png`, `prototype_slip_left_alone.png`, `run_slip_caught.png`.

#### Driving power-ups: the tiers (task T-455, proposals)

The data is `game/data/power_ups.json` (read through `PowerUpData`), four tiers each, every number a **proposal for the board's playtest** with its reason in the file (Game Data wrote them on the Driving & Drift Agent's behalf). Icons are fixed at `res://art/power_ups/<id>.png`; the files come with the art ticket.

- **Rev Charge:** charge time to full 1.6 / 1.3 / 1.0 / 0.7 s; boost speed ×1.5 / 1.6 / 1.75 / 1.9 for 0.8 / 1.0 / 1.2 / 1.5 s. Slow and short at first, so the idea shows; the top tier is cheap to use mid-drift.
- **Jump:** takeoff speed 5 / 6 / 7 / 8 (hop height, hence airtime) with a cooldown of 2.0 / 1.7 / 1.4 / 1.1 s. The first hop is enough for the airtime missions, the third for an air 180, the fourth for an air 360.
- **Bouncy Bumpers:** the T-435 wall bounce distance ×1.4 / 1.8 / 2.2 / 2.6.
- **Rusty Overcoat:** contact damage 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 (a minion has 4 health, T-408), a per-enemy repeat cooldown of 0.5 / 0.5 / 0.4 / 0.3 s, and the kaiju is hit only at tier 4. **Open questions for the board:** the repeat cooldown (so a crowd does not melt each frame) and whether the kaiju is hit.
- **When every power-up is at its last tier** (`offer_when_exhausted`): the mission gift is skipped, with no overlay and no pause, and the run goes on. Reason: an overlay with nothing to choose would only interrupt the run.

#### Rev Charge (task T-460)

The decision is in Decisions ("Driving power-ups"); the tier numbers are above. How it is built: `game/docs/driving/drift.md`, "Rev Charge (T-460)".

- **What it does:** with Rev Charge owned, holding W and S together charges a boost; releasing S fires it. The charge fills in the tier's charge time (1.6 / 1.3 / 1.0 / 0.7 s). The boost lifts the car at once to its top speed × the tier's multiplier (×1.5 / 1.6 / 1.75 / 1.9; from a top speed of 16.5 units/s that is 24.8 / 26.4 / 28.9 / 31.4) and holds it there for the tier's boost time (0.8 / 1.0 / 1.2 / 1.5 s); then the car slows back to its top speed on its own over a second or two. The top speed it multiplies includes the hype speed boost, so a hot car boosts harder.
- **Without it:** W+S drives exactly as before (W wins over S).
- **The proposals for the playtest** (Driving & Drift Agent's calls):
  - **While charging, the car slows to cruise speed** (brakes from top speed at the normal ramp rate, about 0.8 s, then holds cruise, 11 units/s) **and keeps driving**: steering and drifting work as with W alone. Reason: the car is never parked in the middle of a run full of enemies, and a charge can be built inside a drift (the tiers' reasons count on charging mid-drift); the slowdown is the price of the charge and makes the release feel like a kick.
  - **A partial charge fires a partial boost:** the boost's extra speed and its length both scale with how full the charge was. Below a quarter of a full charge nothing fires, so a brief W+S overlap while switching keys never boosts.
  - **Letting go of W first** (S still held) drops the charge with no boost: the car then brakes or reverses on S as usual.
  - **Drifting:** charging works mid-drift (above), and the boost holds its speed through a drift; it is the same forward push as W's, so the drift's grip and the tricks are unchanged.
  - **The air:** the charge does not grow in the air but is kept; releasing S in the air drops it (no boost: in the air the car keeps its takeoff speed, Decisions, "No drifting in the air"). A boost already running keeps its clock in the air and holds its speed again on landing if time is left.
  - **Walls:** a wall, building, boulder or ground-side hit ends a running boost (as it ends the drift since T-438); a charge in progress is kept.
  - **The wreck:** the controls go dead, so the charge and any running boost are dropped, with no boost.
- **The placeholder effect** (drawn in code until the art ticket replaces it): while charging, a round glow at the car's rear, in the heat yellows and oranges, that grows with the charge and pulses once it is full; while boosting, five light blue-grey speed lines streaming back from the rear, fading as the boost runs out. Both stop when the charge or boost ends; nothing shows without the power-up.
- Screenshots and GIF: `art-archive/T-460/screenshots/`.

#### Jump (task T-461)

The decision is in Decisions ("Driving power-ups"); the tier numbers are above. How it is built: `game/docs/driving/tricks.md`, "Jump (T-461)".

- **What it does:** with Jump owned, a press of Space on the ground makes a small hop. It is the car's own height (Elevation): the car leaves the ground straight up at the tier's takeoff speed (5 / 6 / 7 / 8 units/s), falls with the same gravity as off a rooftop (12 units/s²) and lands. Everything a fall off a rooftop does, the hop does: the car keeps its flat speed and heading in the air (no driving in the air) and spins faster there, it meets the sides of rooftops and ramps at its height and passes over what is lower than it, and its airtime and spins pay the airtime, AIR 180 and AIR 360 tricks, so they count for the missions' airtime and air-spin goals (board, 2026-10-31).
- **How high and how long** (from the tier numbers, flat ground): about 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 / 2.7 units high, 0.83 / 1.0 / 1.17 / 1.33 s in the air.
- **Without it:** Space does nothing while driving, as before.
- **The proposals for the playtest** (Driving & Drift Agent's calls):
  - **Only on the ground, no double jump:** a press in the air does nothing and is not kept for the landing. Reason: the hop is a small lift, not flying; a double jump would make the tallest tier reach rooftops.
  - **The cooldown counts from the takeoff** (the tier's 2.0 / 1.7 / 1.4 / 1.1 s), in the air too; a press while it runs does nothing and is not kept. So at tier 1 the next hop is ready about 1.2 s after landing, at tier 4 as soon as the car lands.
  - **One hop per press:** holding Space does not hop again on landing.
  - **From anywhere on the ground:** a street, a rooftop or a ramp; on a ramp it adds to nothing (straight up at the takeoff speed).
- **Note on the tier reasons (for Game Data and the board):** at the base air turn rate (240 degrees a second) the tier 1 hop already fits an air 180 (200 degrees), and the tier 4 hop (320 degrees) does not quite fit an air 360 without the garage's air turn upgrade. The tier numbers are unchanged; the playtest decides.
- Screenshots and GIF: `art-archive/T-461/screenshots/`.

#### The Jump clears obstacles (task T-478)

The decision is in Decisions ("The Jump clears obstacles"). How it is built: `game/scripts/level/mvp_map.gd` (`obstacle_heights`, `obstacle_floor`, `update_car_obstacles`) and `game/scripts/driving/car_height.gd` (`floor_height`).

- **The rule:** every boulder and prop has a bottom and a top (the ground it stands on, up to its height). The car passes over it while its height is at the top (within 0.05 units) or above, and meets it as a wall, with the bounce, when it is lower. Walls (skyscrapers) and the map's edge have no top: they block at any height. Short buildings are platforms of 3 units: a hop that stays below 3 meets their side as before.
- **Heights** (proposals for the playtest): a boulder (the map's and the meteors') is **0.8 units** high (width stays its 3-unit diameter). A prop's collision height is its `height_units` in `creator_assets.json` times 0.75 (`PROP_HEIGHT_SCALE`, so the street props are about as low as a boulder). The hop's peak: tier 1 1.04, tier 2 1.5, tier 3 2.04, tier 4 2.67.
- **What each tier clears** (collision heights): boulder 0.8, barrier 0.9, cones 0.68, broken cars 0.71: every tier. Parked cars 1.01 and a prop of 1.1 to 1.2 (AC unit, roof vent, after the scale): tier 2 and up. Crates 1.65: tier 3 and up. Roof sign and water tank 2.5: tier 4. The street lamp (4.0), the 3-unit platforms, the skyscrapers (30) and the map's edge: no tier.
- **Timing:** a car passes an obstacle once it is at its top (within 0.05), or while it is rising, its apex clears the obstacle's top and it is already 10% of the way up from the foot (`RISE_PASS_FRACTION`). So Space pressed when the car's drawn nose looks level with the obstacle (its body is 1 unit, its sprite 3, so contact comes about 1 unit, 0.06 s at full speed, later) clears it, and a Space about 0.04 s later than that still does; later, the car meets it as a wall. The board played the first version (a 0.8 clearance, pressed 6 to 7 units short) and could not do it.
- **Never landing inside** (proposal): the car lands on the obstacle it is over, at its top, and drives along it like on a low platform; off its edge it falls to the ground. It is never put inside an obstacle by a landing (a car falling through one it passes is put on its top).
- Screenshots and GIF: `art-archive/T-478/screenshots/`.

#### Bouncy Bumpers (task T-462)

The decision is in Decisions ("Driving power-ups"); the tier numbers (×1.4 / 1.8 / 2.2 / 2.6) are above. How it is built: `game/docs/driving/collisions.md`, "Bouncy Bumpers (T-462)".

- **What it does:** with Bouncy Bumpers owned, the wall bounce of "The car bounces off walls" (T-435: walls, buildings, raised sides, the map's edge, boulders) carries the car further, by the owned tier's factor. A head-on hit at cruise speed that travels about 0.9 units from the wall goes about 1.23 / 1.59 / 1.94 / 2.30 units at tiers 1 to 4 (measured, 0.87 without it; tests/unit/test_bouncy_bumpers.gd).
- **Without it:** the bounce is exactly the T-435 bounce.
- **The proposals for the playtest** (Driving & Drift Agent's calls):
  - **The factor multiplies the distance, not the speed:** a bounce's distance goes with its speed squared (W pulls the car back at a steady rate), so the bounce speed is scaled by the square root of the factor. Reason: the data calls it a distance multiplier and the screen text says "Bounce 1.4x farther".
  - **The bounce's maximum scales the same way:** a hit faster than the hardest-hit cap bounces like one at the cap, and that bounce is also times the factor, so the farthest bounce is the factor times today's (about 1.75 × 2.6 = 4.5 units at tier 4).
  - **Everything else is unchanged:** the drift still ends on a hit, the combo still cuts, W still pulls the car back at the same rate.
- Screenshots: `art-archive/T-462/screenshots/` (bounce distance per tier).

#### Trick prototype (reference)

What the trick prototype built (tasks T-151 to T-160, 2026-10-16 and 17), kept as the reference for rebuilding the tricks on real height (Decisions, 2026-10-19). Its code is on the branch `hold/trick-prototype` (the README sections named below are on that branch); its PixelLab art is in `art-archive/T-153/` and `art-archive/T-157/`. The card texts were approved in T-154 and T-158: RIGHT FLIP!, LEFT FLIP!, NOSE POP!, CLEARED IT!, GRIND!. All numbers were proposals for the board's playtest.

**Round 1 (task T-151).** A standalone scene to try the arrow-key tricks: the Godot drift prototype unchanged, driven with W/A/S/D, plus tricks on the arrow keys. Up, Right, Down, Left as consecutive presses, each within 0.6 seconds of the one before, makes a side flip to the right; a wrong key or a slow press starts the sequence again, and no new trick starts while a flip plays. The flip is drawing only: the car rises 16 pixels on an arc and lands after 0.6 seconds with a short squash, rolling a full turn on the way, while a dark shadow stays on the ground and shrinks and fades a little at the top. The car keeps driving and colliding as before. A HUD (T-152) in the bottom-right corner, 16 px from the edges, shows the label TRICK and four arrow keys in keyboard layout: a held key lights up white, a key already in the sequence gets a yellow ring, and a finished trick shows its name on a white rounded card with a black border in Bangers, popping in with an overshoot, holding and fading over 1 second, while the four keys flash yellow for 0.35 seconds.

**Round 2 (task T-155).**
- **Two more arrow tricks.** Up, Left, Down, Right is the side flip to the left: the same hop, rolling the other way (the roll frames played backwards). Up, Down, Up, Up is the nose launch: a 0.15 second nose dip on the ground (the drawing tips forward and squashes), then the launch, which adds 8 units/s to the car's speed along its nose (cruise is 11), a hop of 0.9 seconds and 28 pixels with the drawing pitching nose-up through one full backflip, and a deeper landing squash. All three start with Up and are told apart at the second key.
- **Jumping over obstacles.** While any trick is in the air, the car passes over obstacles and walls instead of hitting them. It never lands inside one: if the hop would end over an obstacle, it stays in the air, low (6 pixels up), until it is clear, then lands; while it waits, a car slower than 3 units/s is pushed gently along its nose. The car can still drive while in the air.
- **The jump-over bonus** counts as a trick of its own: one for each obstacle cleared, at the moment the car comes clear of it. It has its own card (T-156), which can show while a flip's card is showing; visible cards stack upward, 16 px apart, from 28% down the screen.
- **Known limits:** no depth order (the car was always drawn over obstacles), and a jump could carry the car out of the test room.

**Round 3 (task T-159).**
- **Live tilt.** On the ground, the last pressed arrow key that is still held tilts the car's drawing toward it, relative to the car: Up the nose down, Down the tail down, Left and Right onto that side. Releasing it falls back to the key pressed before it, if still held. Slight (25 degrees' worth of squash and a 2 pixel lean), easing in and out in 0.08 seconds; none during a trick or grind.
- **Wall grinds.** Landing from a trick with the car's side within 1.5 units of a wall's long edge, or on top of the wall, or up to a unit past its end (walls, not boulders), while moving along the wall at 1 unit/s or more (an angled landing counts its speed along the wall), locks the car into a grind. (Loosened after the board's playtest, "make grinding a little bit easier"; at first half a unit, beside the wall only, 2 units/s.) The car snaps onto the wall's edge and sits across it at 70 degrees to the wall, the nose leaning the way it travels, and carries on along the wall, slowing by 4 units/s every second. Yellow and orange pixel sparks fly back from the contact point, 5 per second for each unit/s of speed. The grind counts as a trick. When the wall runs out or the speed drops below 1.5 units/s, the car drops off onto the ground on the side it came from.
- **Leaving a grind.** Space (a jump key that only works on a wall) makes a small hop with no trick, landing beside the wall; any arrow trick also carries the car off. Either way the car keeps its speed and direction along the wall, its nose turned along the wall, and doesn't land back on the same wall or count it as a jump-over.
- **Known limits:** dropping off moved the car sideways in one step, and its nose turned along the wall at once.

**The art.** T-153 made the side-flip roll with PixelLab for one direction (the car's start direction, frame 12): one `/animate-with-text-v3` call, 8 frames, palette-matched by script. The board found it flat, like flipping a 2D image. T-157 then made a sample with real depth for the same direction: a script (`game/tools/render_trick_guides.py`) draws a simple 3D model of the car rolled or pitched by any angle, and each frame is one PixelLab `/rotate` call with the real car as the reference and the drawing as the pose (15 calls, starting-image strength 450); `game/tools/build_trick_frames.py` maps the colours and centres the frames. The result: the nose pop has real depth in most frames (the 135-degree one is weak); the roll is inconsistent in its middle frames. The board hadn't chosen the next step for the roll when the prototype was stopped (a free script fix was the Project Lead's pick).

## 3. Level design

*Source: [level-design.md](level-design.md). What the map looks like, plus the designs for the driving challenges. The board defines the challenges geometrically or visually at first, then agents build from that.*

The MVP has one map: a city laid out as a grid of building blocks, with roads of different widths running between them. Obstacles (crashed meteor boulders) stand on the roads in set patterns. Driving challenges, arrows painted on the ground around some of the patterns, are left out of the MVP; the board might bring them back later, and their design is kept here for that.

### Decisions

- **Challenges are left out of the MVP.** The MVP map has no challenge arrows and no challenges: the obstacle pattern copies stay on the roads as plain boulder obstacles. The board might bring challenges back after the MVP; the decisions below about challenges, arrows and corridors are kept for that and do not apply to the MVP.
- A challenge is defined as a curved corridor with a width, so there is room for tolerance.
- The car counts as in the challenge as long as any part of it is touching the corridor. "The car" here is the drawn car (1 by 3 units), not its smaller physics body.
- The MVP map is a city laid out as a grid: blocks of buildings, with roads running between the blocks. (How it looks: Visual style, Decisions.)
- Roads are 24 units wide, three times the first plan's 8, so the car drives through them easily (board, after playing the first map). A street never widens along its length.
- Map sizes are measured in units, where 1 unit is the drawn car's width (the smaller of its two dimensions; Drifting, Decisions). It is the same unit the driving values use.
- The MVP map is **240 by 240 units**: the first plan's 80 by 80 map with everything three times bigger (perimeter road, blocks, roads and the gravel centre). The boulders and the challenges stay sized to the car.
- A wide road, 24 units wide, runs around the whole edge of the map. The map ends in a hard stop at its edges.
- Inside the perimeter road, building blocks of 30 by 30 units are laid out in a 4 by 4 grid, separated by roads 24 units wide (3 roads in each direction).
- The centre of the map is an open square of 84 by 84 units with no blocks. Its ground is gravel, not road.
- Obstacles are placed on the roads. In the MVP the only obstacle is a crashed meteor boulder; more kinds come later.
- In the MVP, obstacles are circles, all 3 units across (one car length), so they never block a road. They stay this size on the bigger map.
- In the MVP, a challenge includes up to 2 obstacles.
- Each challenge's arrow path is shaped to its obstacles, using scripts from the Driving & Drift Agent that show what the car can actually drive and how it behaves.
- Some obstacles are on the map from the start; others appear during the run, dropped by the boss (Enemies, Decisions).
- The obstacles on the map from the start are placed in set patterns, called obstacle pattern groups. The board defines the patterns.
- The MVP has 2 obstacle patterns, each drawn by the board (Content, "MVP challenges"):
  - **Single Boulder:** 1 boulder, with 2 possible challenges: one loop clockwise and one counter-clockwise around it.
  - **Two Boulders:** 2 boulders, with 1 possible challenge: a figure-eight around both.
- A pattern can have several possible challenges: each challenge is a different arrow path around the same obstacles.
- For the MVP, the board does no level design itself. The Level/Challenge Design Agent makes the map once, following the rules in this document and the board's descriptions and drawings, and every run uses that same map.
- 30% of the obstacle pattern groups on the map become challenges. Each challenge gets an arrow that appears under it, animated as if painted on the ground, showing the player how to drive the challenge. The arrow's animation is designed in advance.
- Which pattern groups are challenges is set in advance, the same every run. The Level/Challenge Design Agent makes the first choice, and the board adjusts it if needed.
- The painted arrow marks the challenge's corridor (the corridor in the first Decision). The arrow is as wide as the car is long (3 units), so the player doesn't have to follow its centre line exactly: the car only has to touch the arrow. The Driving & Drift Agent's scripts make sure each path is drivable.
- The Level/Challenge Design Agent decides how many copies of each pattern are placed on the map, and where.
- A challenge is completed when the drawn car touches its corridor continuously from the arrow's start to its end, in the arrow's direction. Leaving the corridor midway means starting again from the start.
- When a challenge is completed, its arrow disappears and the player gets XP on the XP bar. The group's boulders stay on the map as plain obstacles for the rest of the run.
- When a pattern with several possible arrows becomes a challenge, the Level/Challenge Design Agent picks one of its arrows.
- The board draws each challenge as its own drawing in Crash City Grid (References): one drawing per arrow path, kept in a folder per obstacle pattern. Every drawing in a pattern's folder has the same boulders; only the arrow differs.
- The board's drawings are rough sketches of each challenge's general shape, not exact layouts. The Level/Challenge Design Agent makes them fit the map (for example the 8-unit roads), with whatever reasonable adjustments that needs (size, spacing, how tight the loops are), while keeping the shape: how many boulders, which way the arrow goes around each one, and the overall path (a loop, a figure-eight). The Driving & Drift Agent's check confirms the fitted versions can be driven.
- The kaiju's meteors leave plain boulders where they land, not challenges (Enemies, Decisions).
- After the MVP, if challenges come back (2026-10-11): a challenge the kaiju's meteors create never lands on another challenge: its boulders and its arrow corridor must not overlap any other challenge's arrow corridor, preset or meteor.
- **Raised areas and ramps** (board, 2026-10-17; go-ahead 2026-10-19): the map can have elevated areas, for example in the size of the current 2 by 2 grid of blocks. One side of a raised area is a ramp the car drives up; its other edges are drop-offs the car can jump off. How the car's height works: Drifting, Decisions, "Elevation". First built in a test scene with one raised platform, one ramp and one drop-off edge, not in the real map. The map's data format leaves room for heights and ramps from the start, for the level editor the board wants later.
- **Raised areas turn see-through like buildings** (board, 2026-10-19, after playing the elevation test scene): when a raised area (and its ramp) covers the car on screen, it fades the way buildings do ("When a building fades" below), with the same logic, so the car never vanishes behind it.
- **Elevation sample map** (board, 2026-10-19, after approving the elevation test scene): elevation goes into the game first, the tricks later. A drive-only sample map (no enemies, weapons or run timer; driving around freely, like the test scene but city-sized), made by the agents, with **three layers**: the street (height 0), a first floor (height 3) and a second floor (height 6), with ramps connecting the street to the first floor and the first floor to the second, so the car can jump from higher with more airtime. The raised areas are building rooftops and the ramps parking-garage-style ramps (look: Visual style, Decisions, "Elevation sample map art"). It uses the elevation system as approved (the car's height, edges, see-through, the round shadow) and the map's buildings, boulders and roads. Its map file holds the heights and ramps in the format a level editor would later edit. After the board's playtest: if the board is happy, maybe aerial tricks next (a 360 in the air, a combo from airtime); if not, a level editor so the board can make levels by hand and playtest them at once. The arrow-key tricks come after both. Full runs on elevated maps (enemies that handle heights) are a later step.
- **The elevation sample map becomes the run's map** (board, 2026-10-20, after playing it: "plays great"): a run started from the main menu now plays on the elevation sample map's layout, with its rooftops, ramps and the car's height, as the full game (enemies, weapons, timer, likes, levels, the kaiju), so the board can see how the enemies behave on it. The MVP map stays in the project and can be switched back to (tasks T-206, T-207). How enemies handle heights: Enemies, Decisions, "Enemies follow the car up the ramps" (board, 2026-10-21).
- **Level creator** (board, 2026-10-21): a separate app, opened like the game but never shipped with it, where the board makes levels by hand. It lists the levels made so far: pick one to play it as a full run (the same 8 minutes, enemies and kaiju as the game), or press a button to create a new one (the only option when there are none). Creating or editing a level is a scene with a side panel of every asset already in the game (ground tiles, roads, buildings, boulders, rooftops, ramps): pick one, place it, rotate it before placing (which means switching between the views the art exists in and mirroring them, since the art has only the angles that were generated), with rooftops and ramps at heights 3 and 6 as on today's map, and pieces snapping to the map's tile grid and to close neighbours so they align with little effort. Custom levels are played only from the creator; the game keeps its own map. Enemies find their way on whatever is built. Built by a goal run (G-005), first with today's art only.
- **Level creator piece set** (board, 2026-10-22, after playing G-005's creator; replaces "no new art is generated for it"): today's assets are not enough to build a full level, so the creator gets a comprehensive set of pieces generated with PixelLab, with no cap on generations (board, 2026-10-24: "we have all the budget available to us"; this replaces the first cap of 100). The aim is a functional, multi-layer world to drive around: rooftops and platforms that can be made smaller and bigger, ramps between the layers, and pieces in more rotations. What the set holds is the Project Lead's plan (the tickets list it); the board judges it in the playtest.
- **Asking for a new piece from the creator** (board, 2026-10-24): a "+" button in the creator's side panel opens a tab where the board picks a kind (building, obstacle or decoration), describes the piece in its own words and presses Send. Send is the board's go for that piece. The request reaches a Project Lead session through an inbox (T-284). The session writes an art ticket, and the Asset Generation Agent makes the piece from Visual style and the Extended narrative, in one generation round. Narrative Theme names it, a script adds it to the catalogue (T-285), and it appears in the panel while the creator is open (T-283; text T-282). The board's look in the creator is the review. QA checks the requested pieces together before they merge. The creator itself never calls PixelLab. Expected time from Send to the piece in the panel: about 5 to 10 minutes while a session is open (an estimate; the first request times it).
  - **Road pieces (T-252):** drawn by script from the existing road tiles (no PixelLab), at today's two-tile-wide roads' size so they join the straight roads the game's map and the creator already use: each piece is 2 x 2 tiles (4 x 4 units), placed with one click, and on every open side its lane (centre) line continues the straight tiles' line exactly. 4 corners, 4 T-junctions, a crossroads and 4 dead ends; a dead end closes the road with a white kerb line across it and gravel beyond. Each rotation is its own button under Roads, labelled from `creator_texts.json`, listed before the older road tiles. The older road tiles (centre-line halves, zebra crossings; x and y versions) stay as they were, so the game's own map is unchanged. Details: `game/docs/level/level-creator.md`, "Level creator (T-231)".
- **Small and long buildings** (T-254, part of the piece set above): two more short buildings for the creator, both with their roofs showing, solid, see-through when the car is behind them and pathed round by enemies like today's. The **small** one covers 6 x 6 units, the **long** one 12 x 6 (6 x 12 rotated, R). **Height (a proposal for the board): 4.3 units**, the same as today's short buildings. Placeholder look: a code-drawn box in the city's palette (pale lit windows on cool blue-grey walls); T-257 generates the final art. Their art per rotation and mirror is in `game/data/level/creator_buildings.json`. The game's own map is unchanged.
- **Level creator rework** (board, 2026-10-22, after playing the piece set; the plan the board read: https://claude.ai/artifact/2TXG35AkZFYXKvfNUUPfNN): the side panel is one button per kind of thing, in six groups from the ground up (Roads, Ground, Levels, Buildings, Obstacles, Decoration), with a piece's looks, turns, mirror and height chosen by keys and shown in a strip under the selected piece, instead of a button per rotation and variant. **Roads are painted with a brush**: drag to lay a road, which comes whole (a centre line in its middle, not two half tiles) and joins itself into corners, T-junctions, crossroads and dead ends; road kinds are plain, centre line, zebra crossing and cracked. **Ramps** are closed blocks with a wall at their tall end, and each ramp in each direction and height step can have its arrows pointing up or down the slope, the board's choice per ramp. **Platforms** (rooftops) have one-click sizes S 8 x 8, M 16 x 16 and L 32 x 32 units at heights 3 and 6, besides dragging any size. **Skyscraper banners** are on or off per building, off by default. No new generations.
- **The car's spawn point** (board, 2026-10-22): every level has a spawn point, where the car starts a run on it. It is visible in the editor from the moment a level opens and the board can move it anywhere the car can stand (dragging it, and turning it for the car's starting heading, a proposal). It can never be deleted: a level always has exactly one. A new level starts with it at the map's centre; a level saved before this has it there too. (T-279, T-280)
- **Thread the needle** (board, 2026-10-22): in the level creator the board can mark two obstacles (anything the car crashes into and that cuts the combo: boulders, barriers, cones, crates) as a pair. In a run on that level, driving through the gap between a marked pair is a trick, **thread the needle**, that raises the combo like the other tricks (Game loop architecture, Decisions, "The combo"). What it is worth, whether it pays again on the next pass, and how the pair shows in the editor and in the run are the agents' proposals for the playtest. Its popup text: HUD and menus, Content (T-271). (T-272)
- **Tutorial levels** (board, 2026-10-20, "not a request now"): short tutorial levels that show the player the tricks, one trick at a time. The board will describe them later; nothing is built until then (task T-211).
- **The board's own level becomes the game's map** (board, 2026-10-29): the board builds a level by hand in the level creator over several hours, then hands it over; that level becomes the map the game's Start plays, in place of the elevation sample map. The board handed over Kaiju City on 2026-10-30; the file the game plays: Content, "The game's map". (T-372)
- ~~**The kaiju alert signs move onto Kaiju City** (board, 2026-10-31): since Kaiju City became the game's map (T-372), the kaiju alert signs still sat at the old sample map's places and the hanging banners weren't drawn. All of them move onto Kaiju City: the hanging banners back on this map's skyscrapers and the standing signs on pavement beside its roads. The spots are the Level/Challenge Design Agent's proposal for the board's playtest. (T-439)~~ Replaced by the next line.
- **Kaiju alert signs are level creator pieces** (board, 2026-10-31, after T-439 placed them at fixed spots: "I want to be able to have the signs as components from the level creator. That way I can place them wherever I want, either on the ground or buildings"): two new pieces in the level creator, a standing alert sign placed on the ground or a rooftop and an alert banner hung on a skyscraper's wall, each in both designs (head and body), with the existing art. The fixed sign list (`kaiju_signs.json`) is retired: a map shows only the signs placed in its level, so Kaiju City has none until the board places them. T-439 is cancelled. (T-440, T-441)
- **Roads painted in the creator show in the run** (board, 2026-10-29; a bug, fixed at once): roads the board places on the ground in the level creator don't show up when the level is played. What is painted in the editor must be what the run draws. (T-391)
- **Obstacles and decorations respect the buildings' and rooftops' heights** (board, 2026-10-29; a bug, fixed at once): in the level creator, barriers placed by a building or a rooftop ignore its height (they draw over it as if it weren't there), and the board suspects other objects do the same. Every placed object must sit at the height of what it stands on and be drawn in front of or behind buildings and rooftops correctly, in the editor and in the run. (T-393)
- **A row of obstacles can be threaded gap after gap** (board, 2026-10-29): the board wants to thread the needle through every gap in a row of obstacles, one after another, but an obstacle can be in only one pair today (pairing it again unpairs it from the other). The board asked the Project Lead for an intuitive way that works both ways; the Project Lead's design: an obstacle can be in several pairs (pairing B with C keeps A with B), several obstacles can be picked in order and paired in one go as a chain (A with B, B with C, C with D), Unpair removes only the pair it is aimed at, and in the run each gap pays its own thread the needle, so a row threaded gap after gap pays each one. The board judges it in the playtest. (T-394)
- **Threading the needle flashes the pair** (board, 2026-10-31): when the car threads the needle, the two paired obstacles and the dashed line that connects them flash, so the player sees which gap paid. How long and in what colour are the agent's proposals for the playtest. (T-451)
- **Sidewalks and parked cars in the level creator** (board, 2026-10-30): new pieces for the creator, with art that fits the roads, the buildings and the other assets. **Sidewalks** are painted like roads; wherever a sidewalk meets a road the editor adds the curb edge itself. In the run the car drives up over the curb (it is a step under the 0.1-unit curb rule, Drifting, Decisions). The curb is drawn only, with no height step: the car feels no bump going onto a sidewalk (board, 2026-10-30, after playing T-398). **Parked cars**: a few normal, boring city cars and some broken (wrecked) ones, each at four facings (top right, bottom right, bottom left, top left). They are solid obstacles like boulders: the car crashes into them, and two of them can be paired for thread the needle. PixelLab up to 50 generations for the whole set, sample first (one sidewalk tile with its curb, one parked car facing) for the board's review. **Meteor craters** (board, 2026-10-30, the same day): holes the meteors left in the ground, placed in the creator as ground pieces, not obstacles: the car drives over them with no crash. A few looks, made inside the same 50-generation cap, one crater in the sample. This reopens the pavement question for the creator's levels only (Open questions); the game's own map is unchanged. (T-396 to T-399, T-401)
- **A gift pack that falls on a platform shows on it** (board, 2026-10-30; a bug, fixed at once): a gift pack dropped onto a platform (rooftop) is drawn below the platform, hidden under it. It must be drawn at the height of what it lands on. Whether a gift pack may land on a platform at all (today's rule, Content, "Elevation sample map": street-level spots only) or is drawn on the platform and picked up there is the agent's proposal, written with the root cause, for the board's playtest. (T-402)
- **Short buildings become platforms** (board, 2026-10-30): on platforms "a lot of stuff seems not to be working": a gift pack's pickup is in the wrong place, a low-rise under a platform is drawn correctly but its invisible body still stops the car, so it can't reach the platform's end, and nothing says what happens when the car jumps off a platform over a building. The board's decision: the low-rise, small and long buildings no longer exist as buildings; each is a **platform at height 3** with the same art (walls trimmed by script to height 3, no new generations), driven on like a rooftop and reached by today's 0-to-3 ramps. Placed side by side they **connect** into one larger platform (no walls or roof edges drawn between them). Only skyscrapers stay solid buildings. Every collider and pickup works at the height it is at (nothing below a platform stops the car on top of it; a pickup on a platform is picked up there), and the car that jumps off a platform falls to the ground or a lower platform; a skyscraper blocks it at any height. Levels saved before, and the game's own map, turn their short buildings into these platforms. (T-402, T-405)
- **A small jump ramp** (board, 2026-10-30): besides today's ramps (0 to 3, 3 to 6 and 0 to 6, each about three tiles long), a small ramp only one tile long that rises about 2 units from the ground it stands on, for small jumps: the car drives up it and flies off its top. It is placed, turned and raised like the other ramps (on the ground or on a rooftop). Its exact length, height and whether its tall end is open or closed are proposals for the playtest. (T-400)

### Content

#### The game's map

The map the main menu's Start plays (task T-372; Decisions, "The board's own level becomes the game's map") is the board's own level, **Kaiju City**, built by hand in the level creator and handed over on 2026-10-30. The game plays a copy of it in its own data, **`game/data/level/kaiju_city_map.json`**; the board's working file in the creator's levels folder (`game/data/levels/kaiju_city.json`) stays the board's, untouched and never committed. The copy is the board's file byte for byte; nothing in it was changed. The elevation sample map (`game/data/level/elevation_sample_map.json`, "Elevation sample map" below) stays in the project: the tests and the level creator use it, and a run with no map named still plays it. The creator's Play still plays the creator's own levels.

- **What it holds:** a 240 by 240 unit map with a hard stop at its edges, 42 buildings (skyscrapers, and short buildings that are platforms at height 3), 13 rooftops at heights 3 and 6, 28 ramps (among them T-400's small jump ramps), 82 props, 9 boulders, 10 meteor craters, 20 thread-the-needle pairs, sidewalks and painted roads, and its spawn point at (1, 1) on a road, heading 270 (up the screen's right, the run's usual start).
- **Checks:** `python game/tools/check_level.py` and `python game/tools/check_height_data.py` both print `OK` on it.
- **What the agents found in a scripted run, for the board's playtest** (T-372; the level is not changed): the rooftop roof-13 (height 6, west of the map's centre) has no ramp up to it (its four small ramps all climb from 6 to 8 on top of it), so it is reached only from the air, and minions can't follow the car onto it. When the car stands on a few rooftops in the north-west cluster and on roof-1 (west of the centre), the ring where minions spawn, just beyond the screen's edge, lies wholly on rooftops and buildings, so no new minions spawn until the car comes back near a street (minions spawn only on the street). The game's kaiju alert signs (task T-130) were placed for the elevation sample map's blocks: their two standing signs were drawn on this map at those same places, which belong to no block here. (Since T-441 that fixed list is retired: Kaiju City has no alert signs until the board places them in the level creator; Content, "Level creator: kaiju alert signs and banners".)

How the run loads it: `game/docs/level/game-map.md`.

The board's sketches of the 3 MVP challenges, one per arrow path. They show the general shape only; the fitted versions on the map are the Level/Challenge Design Agent's (Decisions). Each drawing's data (boulders and arrow points, in units from the sheet's centre) is in a `.json` file next to its picture. The pale band is the 3-unit corridor, the white dot is the start, and the arrowhead is the finish.

| Pattern | Challenge | How the arrow goes |

| Single Boulder | [arrow 2](level-design/single-boulder/arrow-2.svg) | One loop around the boulder, counter-clockwise |
| Two Boulders | [arrow 1](level-design/two-boulders/arrow-1.svg) | A figure-eight: clockwise around the top boulder, counter-clockwise around the bottom one |

#### Drivability check

The Driving & Drift Agent's drivability check (References) drove the board's sketches with the car's driving code (task T-021), both with the Unity prototype's top speed and with the board's top speed of 3.0 times cruise speed (Drifting, Decisions); the results were the same:

- Single Boulder, arrow 1: drivable: yes.
- Single Boulder, arrow 2: drivable: yes.
- Two Boulders, arrow 1: drivable: yes.

#### MVP map

The MVP map as built in Godot (task T-019; made bigger after Playtest 1 in task T-094, then rebuilt with everything three times bigger after the combined playtest in task T-096), in flat placeholder colours: dark grey roads, the tan gravel centre, purple buildings, and dark boulders with an orange rim. The art replaces the colours later. Since task T-103 the isometric view draws the ground art, and since task T-034 its buildings rise as boxes that turn see-through ("See-through buildings" below).

**No challenges in the MVP** (task T-097, as Decisions says). The map draws no challenge arrows and tracks no challenges, so it never sends a completed challenge and the run never flashes a score; likes come from drifting only. Every pattern copy below stays on the roads, its boulders exactly where they were, as plain obstacles the car bounces off. The challenges, the fitted versions, the completion rule, the arrows and the meteor challenges are kept in the code and the layout data, unused, so they can be switched back on in one place if the board brings them back (how: `game/docs/level/mvp-map.md`, "MVP map"). The parts of this section about challenges and arrows describe what comes back then.

![The MVP map, flat top-down](level-design/mvp-map.png)

![The MVP map, isometric](level-design/mvp-map-iso.png)

**Size.** The map is **240 by 240 units**, as Decisions says: across the map, the two 24-unit sides of the perimeter road, 4 blocks of 30 and the 3 roads of 24 between them (24 + 4 x 30 + 3 x 24 + 24 = 240). The gravel centre is the middle 2 by 2 blocks and the road between them, 84 by 84 units, which leaves 12 blocks.

**Coordinates.** Positions are in units from the map's centre, x to the right and y down, as in Crash City Grid, so the map runs from -120 to 120. The perimeter road runs from the edge to 96 units from the centre; the blocks start at -96, -42, 12 and 66 on each axis; the gravel centre runs from -42 to 42. The road centre lines are at -108 and 108 (the perimeter road) and -54, 0 and 54 (the roads between the blocks), and the middle of each block side is at -81, -27, 27 or 81. The car starts at 0, 0, in the gravel.

**Fitted patterns.** Each sketch has a fitted version next to it (`arrow-1.fitted.json` and `.svg`), made by a script from the sketch. The rule is the same as before: the sketch's boulders are kept, 3 units across and as far apart as drawn, and its arrow points are moved as little as possible until the arrow's centre line stays at least 2 units from each boulder's centre (the rock's radius plus half the car's width) and the 3-unit corridor stays at least 0.25 units from every building. On the 24-unit roads every sketch already keeps those distances, so no arrow point is moved: each fitted version is the board's sketch exactly, only shifted so its boulders sit on the crossing's centre or the road's centre line.

| Fitted version | Made to fit | Around each boulder |
|---|---|---|
| [Single Boulder, arrow 1](level-design/single-boulder/arrow-1.fitted.svg) | A crossing of two 24-unit roads, the boulder on its centre | Clockwise, 389 degrees, as in the sketch |
| [Single Boulder, arrow 2](level-design/single-boulder/arrow-2.fitted.svg) | A crossing of two 24-unit roads, the boulder on its centre | Counter-clockwise, 431 degrees, as in the sketch |
| [Two Boulders, arrow 1](level-design/two-boulders/arrow-1.fitted.svg) | A straight 24-unit road, the boulders on its centre line, 7 units apart | Clockwise 422 degrees, then counter-clockwise 332, as in the sketch |

The figure-eight is no longer squeezed across the road: its loops are as wide as the board drew them (about 8 units).

**Pattern copies.** 60 copies: 24 Single Boulder and 36 Two Boulders. None is in the gravel.

- A Single Boulder on the centre of every place where two road centre lines meet: the 8 crossings of the inner roads, the 12 junctions where they join the perimeter road, and its 4 corners.
- A Two Boulders on the middle of every stretch of road between those places (the middle of each block side), turned to run along the road.
- So along any road the next copy is 27 units away.

Every copy has room for any of its pattern's arrows, clear of buildings, the map's edge and the other copies, so which copies are challenges can change later without moving them.

**Challenges (off in the MVP, kept for later).** 30% of 60 is 18 challenges (rounded half up, as before): 6 Single Boulder (3 with arrow 1, 3 with arrow 2) and 12 Two Boulders. They are the same every run. They are chosen evenly through the copies in reading order (top to bottom, then left to right), which spreads them over the whole map; the Single Boulder ones take arrow 1 and arrow 2 in turn. The rotation turns the fitted version clockwise on screen (0: the Two Boulders runs along y).
