## 4. Enemies

*Source: [enemies.md](enemies.md). Which enemies exist, what they look like, how they move, deal damage and behave, including the boss.*

Each level ends with its own final boss; in the first level, Crash City, it is the kaiju. The MVP boss is a huge, slow sprite that walks toward the player and deals contact damage. Its one special move rains meteors that land as boulders, new obstacles on the roads. Weapons can damage it at any time.

### Decisions

- Each level ends with a different type of monster as its final boss. The kaiju is only the first level's boss.
- MVP boss: a sprite much bigger than the player, walking slowly toward the player, with contact damage.
- The boss has one special move. After a short animation, several meteors rain down at once. In 2D, each is a meteor sprite falling top to bottom, with an impact animation on landing.
- Before the meteors land, a danger warning area shows on the ground for 2 seconds. A meteor that lands on the player deals damage and knocks them back.
- Landed meteors become boulders, plain obstacles like the map's own, where they land. No challenge or arrow comes with them, since challenges are left out of the MVP (Level design, Decisions).
- A boulder left by a meteor stays for 10 seconds after it lands, then fades away and is gone.
- A meteor never lands on a boulder left by an earlier meteor that is still there (standing or fading); once that boulder is gone, its spot is free again.
- **The kaiju can be damaged at any time.** It has no shield and no vulnerability windows.
- Over a run, the number of enemies grows slightly. Enemies do not get tougher.
- The MVP minion walks on four legs towards the player (how it looks: Visual style, Decisions). Its health, contact damage and knockback are balancing numbers for the Game Data Agent; it does not copy a Unity prototype enemy.
- The Game Data Agent proposes the kaiju's health, together with the player's weapon damage; the board judges it in playtests.
- The Game Data Agent, with the Enemy Behavior Agent, works out the balancing numbers: how enemy numbers grow over the 7 minutes (within "slightly"), the coin drop chance and amounts, and how often the kaiju drops meteors and how many. The board judges them in playtests.
- When the kaiju is defeated it always drops a few coins (100% chance). Its death ends the run straight away, so its coins are added to the run's coins as the run ends, without being picked up.
- Where and how minions spawn, and how often their contact damage applies, are proposed by the Enemy Behavior Agent with the Game Data Agent; the board judges them in playtests.
- Killing the kaiju ends the run at once, as a win.
- The higher the player's combo (Game loop architecture, Decisions), the more minions spawn, on top of the slow growth over the run. It can be switched off, so the board can judge in playtests whether to keep it; the Game Data Agent proposes how strongly the combo raises spawning.
- **Minions spawn on a timer, and 30% slower** (board, 2026-10-31): minions no longer top up to a wanted number around the car (that rewarded not killing them: the fewer the player killed, the fewer came, so runs reached the end with few likes and weapons). Instead they spawn on a constant timer, coming in from the edges of the screen, however many are already around, and the timer speeds up as the run goes on, so more of them come later in the run. The combo still raises spawning on top of that (the decision above). Minions move 30% slower (move speed 6 becomes 4.2 units per second). With many more enemies on screen, the game is optimised so a crowd of minions doesn't slow it down much. The spawn rates at the start and the end of the run, and any safety ceiling on how many can be alive at once, are the Enemy Behavior Agent's proposals for the playtest. (T-443, T-444)
- Polish for the MVP, once the MVP is playable end to end: minions get a damage animation when hit, and when two minions bump into each other they fall down, get up again and carry on running at the car. How long they stay down is proposed by the Enemy Behavior Agent; the board judges it in playtests.
- The kaiju walks round buildings and boulders, like the minions, rather than through them.

- **Enemies follow the car up the ramps** (board, 2026-10-21, after playing the full game on the elevation map, where enemies ignored every raised surface): enemies treat rooftops as raised ground they can only reach by the ramps. To reach a car on a rooftop they find their way to a ramp, drive or walk up it and follow the car, with pathfinding over the map's streets, ramps and rooftops; a rooftop's edge blocks them like a wall from below. (T-207)
- **Enemies jump down off ledges** (board, 2026-10-21, after playing T-207): going down, enemies don't walk all the way round to a ramp: to chase a car below them they jump (drop) off a rooftop's edge. Going up still needs a ramp, and an edge still blocks them from below. A falling enemy plays a falling animation from the edge until it lands (board, 2026-10-21; placeholder T-226, art T-227). (T-226)

- **Health drops** (board, 2026-10-21): enemies also drop health pickups, at the same drop rate as the coins. Picking one up restores 30% of the car's health (never above its maximum). It looks like a red gas canister with a white cross on it (look: Visual style, Decisions). (T-220, art T-221) **Halved** (board, 2026-10-22): health drops now drop at half that rate (0.6 to 0.3), no longer the coins' rate; the coins are unchanged. (T-277)
- **Damage in hearts, fewer health drops, bolder outlines** (board, 2026-10-28): with hearts (Game loop architecture, Decisions, "Hearts instead of health points"), a minion's hit and a meteor take 1 heart and the kaiju's 2, once per hit, with the car's 1-second invulnerability after it instead of repeated contact hits. Health pickups drop at half today's chance (15% instead of 30%) and heal 1 heart. Every enemy's outline is a little bolder, so the player sees where they are and can steer round them. (T-333, T-334, T-340)
- **Health drops 1.5 times as often** (board, 2026-10-29): "increase the drop rate of health items by enemies by 1.5 times of what it is now": a killed minion drops a health pickup with a chance of 22.5% instead of 15%. The coins, the heal (1 heart) and the kaiju (none) are unchanged. (T-371)
- **Minions twice as big** (board, 2026-10-29, an MVP nice-to-have): the minions are drawn twice as big, and the size they hit and get hit with grows to match, so what the player sees is what touches the car. The kaiju stays as it is. **Built in T-379:** `size_scale` 2 in `game/data/enemies.json` (`minion`).
- **Minions don't get stuck on ramps** (board, 2026-10-29, an MVP nice-to-have; a bug): chasing the car, minions sometimes get stuck on walls as they try to go round a corner, mostly at the bottom end of a ramp. They should find their way round. **Built in T-380** (see Content, "Finding the way").
- **A red flash when an enemy takes damage** (board, 2026-10-30): every enemy (minions and the kaiju) flashes red when a weapon or the car hits it, the same red flash the car shows when it loses a heart (Game loop architecture, Decisions). Its length and shade match the car's; for the kaiju, whether it flashes on every hit or only in its vulnerable window is a proposal. Built in T-404 (see Content, "The red flash").
- **Meteors hit minions and push pickups aside** (board, 2026-10-30, audit): a meteor that lands on minions damages them; coins and health pickups where a boulder appears are pushed out of its way. A meteor misses a car more than 1 unit above it, the same rule as contact damage.
- **The kaiju only takes paths it fits through** (board, 2026-10-30, audit; a bug): the kaiju plans its way round buildings for its own size, so it never heads into a gap too narrow for it. It also keeps its body off rooftops', ramps' and the map's edges, and drops off a rooftop from a little way back from the edge (board, 2026-10-30, after playing build J: keep the edge rule; T-419).

### Content

#### The red flash (built in task T-404)

Every minion and the kaiju flash the car's red (Game loop architecture, Decisions) when a weapon or the car damages them and they survive: same colour and length, read from `hit_flash` in `game/data/run.json` (0.4 s, red [1, 0.25, 0.25], proposals). It replaces T-072's pale 0.12 s tint. Proposals: a hit that kills skips the flash (the enemy is gone at once); the kaiju flashes on every hit, not only in its vulnerable window; a new hit restarts the flash; the flamethrower's orange burn flash still wins over red. How: `game/docs/enemies/minions.md`.

#### The minion (built in task T-044)

What the game does now, with the numbers in `game/data/enemies.json` (see References). How it is built, and the damage function the weapons call: `game/docs/enemies/minions.md`, "Minions".

- **Look:** a placeholder for now: a light green four-legged lizard shape with a tail, drawn in code, facing the way it walks. Since T-379 the minions are drawn twice as big (`size_scale` 2, a whole number, so the pixel edges stay hard): about two units across, twice the car's width. The final minion art comes from a separate art task.
- **Spawning (T-443, on a timer):** minions come in one after another on a timer, however many are already around, each just beyond the edge of the visible screen (3 units out), at a random point on the street that is clear of buildings and boulders, so they walk in from the edges. The timer speeds up over the run: one every 1.2 seconds at the start, one every 0.3 seconds (4 a second) at the 7-minute mark (the kaiju's arrival), then held; in between the number per second grows in a straight line (one every 0.48 seconds at 3:30), about 870 minions over the 7 minutes. A safety ceiling of 100 minions alive at once stops the timer only while that many are alive, to protect the frame rate. All of these are proposals for the playtest (reasons: T-443's result notes; numbers in `game/data/enemies.json`, `spawning`). Minions the car has left a whole screen behind disappear, and the timer keeps bringing new ones in at the screen's edge. The higher the combo, the faster the timer (Decisions; see "The combo raises spawning" below).
- **Movement:** each minion walks straight towards the car at 4.2 units a second (30% slower than the old 6, T-443). Minions push a little apart from each other so they spread around the car. They do not walk through buildings, walls or boulders: they slide along them and walk round one that is in the way. They never block or push the car.
- **The combo raises spawning:** the spawn rate is multiplied by the combo's spawn multiplier, so the timer's interval is divided by it (T-443; up to 1.75 times as many, 0.3 s becoming about 0.17 s at the top) (Game loop architecture, The combo; numbers in the combo data), live as the combo changes: no combo, no extra minions; the higher the combo, the more, up to the data's maximum. A setting (`combo_raises_spawning`, on by default; how to flip it is in `game/docs/enemies/minions.md`, Minions) switches it off for playtests.
- **Contact damage:** while a minion touches the car's body, it hits the car: 1 heart off the car (which also cuts the combo, Game loop architecture) and a knockback away from the minion. Data (T-333): `contact_damage` 1; the old 0.5 s repeat (`contact_damage_interval`) is gone from the data, the car's 1 s invulnerability after a hit spaces the hits (built in T-334: while it lasts no enemy hits the car or knocks it back, a proposal for the playtest).
- **Health and death:** 4 health. The weapons damage it; at 0 it dies and disappears.
- **Knocked back by a weapon (built in task T-167):** a weapon can push a minion (the windshield wiper does; Weapons). The weapon gives a direction and a distance in units (the flat world's units, like every distance here); the minion is pushed that far in that direction over 0.15 seconds at an even speed, without walking, then walks towards the car again. It is stopped by buildings, walls and boulders just as its walking is (it slides along them and is never pushed into one). A second push during a push adds to what is left. Only minions can be pushed: the kaiju has no knockback and is never pushed. The 0.15 seconds is a proposed feel number in the code (`KNOCKBACK_SECONDS`); the distance is the weapon's number. How to call it: `game/docs/enemies/minions.md`, "Minions".
- **Coins:** a dying minion drops coins 60% of the time, 2 coins each time, around where it died: placeholder gold coins on the ground. Driving over a coin collects it and adds it to the run's coins. Coins stay on the ground until collected or the run ends.
- **Boulders fade:** a boulder a meteor left stays 10 seconds after it lands, fully visible and solid. Then it fades out over 2 seconds (still drawn and still solid while it fades) and is gone: it no longer blocks the car or anything else, and its spot is free again. The 10 seconds and the 2-second fade are in `meteor_attack` (`boulder_lifetime_seconds`, `boulder_fade_seconds`; the fade's length is a proposed number). The map's own boulders never fade. The flat view's placeholder circles vanish at the end without fading (only the boulder art is see-through).
- **Health pickups (built in T-220):** a dying minion also drops a health pickup where it died, at the ground height it stood on, rolled separately from the coins (so one kill can drop both) at 22.5% (`drop_chance` 0.225; was 15%, T-371; 30% before, T-333; 60% before that, T-277), 3/8 of the coins' rate. Driving over it restores 1 heart (`restore_hearts` 1; was `restore_fraction` 0.3), never above the maximum; a full-health car still uses it up (proposal). The kaiju drops none (proposal). Numbers: `health_drops` in `game/data/enemies.json`. The look is a placeholder drawn in code: a small orange-red canister with a white cross; final art T-221.
- **Pause and new runs:** minions, coins and health pickups stand still while the game is paused, and are all gone when a new run starts.
- **Draw order:** minions and coins are drawn in the buildings' depth order like the car: behind a building that covers them, in front of the rest. Buildings fade only for the car, so a minion behind an opaque skyscraper is hidden by it.

#### The kaiju (built in task T-045)

What the game does now, with the numbers in `game/data/enemies.json` (see References). How it is built, and how the weapons and the HUD reach it: `game/docs/enemies/kaiju.md`, "The kaiju". Its meteor attack: below.

- **Look:** a placeholder for now: a large dark slate green Godzilla-style shape drawn in code, seen from the side, with a lighter belly, pale cyan back plates and yellow eyes, facing left or right the way it walks and stomping as it walks. It stands on a ground circle 4 units across (four times the car's width) and is 7 units tall (over twice the car's length). The final kaiju art comes from a separate art task.
- **Arrival:** when the run reaches the boss time (7 minutes in, 1:00 left), the kaiju appears at a random point just beyond the edge of the visible screen, its whole drawing out of view, on the map and clear of buildings and boulders. One kaiju per run.
- **Movement:** it walks straight towards the car at 3 units a second, a little under three quarters of a minion's speed (4.2). Like the minions, it does not walk through buildings, walls or boulders: it slides along them and walks round one that is in the way (confirmed by the board, 2026-10-14). It never blocks or pushes the car.
- **Contact damage:** while it touches the car's body, it hits the car: 2 hearts off the car (which also cuts the combo; data `contact_damage` 2, the old 1 s repeat gone with the minion's) and a knockback of 16 units a second away from the kaiju.
- **Health and damage:** 500 health. Weapons damage it at any time, as soon as it has appeared, the same way they damage minions; there is no shield and no vulnerability window. Any overlap with its body on the ground (the 4-unit circle) counts as a flamethrower hit (board, 2026-10-14; minions keep the centre rule). Its health, and each change to it, can be read for the HUD (no HUD shows it yet).
- **Death:** at 0 health it dies and disappears. Its 10 coins are added to the run's coins at once, without a pickup, and then the run ends as a win, so the coins count in the coins saved.
- **Pause and new runs:** the kaiju stands still while the game is paused, and is gone when a new run starts; it arrives again at the new run's boss time.
- **Draw order:** like the minions, in the buildings' depth order: behind a building that covers it, in front of the rest.
- **Playtest switch:** for the board's playtest of this task, the kaiju arrives 30 seconds into the run instead of at 7 minutes, so it can be seen, fought with the weapons and killed early; it is set back to 7 minutes right before the task merges (board, 2026-10-14). Nothing else in the run moves (`game/data/playtest.json`; how to switch it: `game/docs/enemies/kaiju.md`, "The kaiju").

#### The kaiju's meteor attack (built in task T-046)

What the game does now, with the numbers in `game/data/enemies.json`, `meteor_attack` (see References). How it is built: `game/docs/enemies/kaiju.md`, "The kaiju", "The meteor attack".

- **When:** while the kaiju is on the map, its first attack starts 5 seconds after it appears, then one every 8 seconds.
- **Windup:** each attack starts with a short placeholder animation of 1 second: pale yellow rings pulse above the kaiju's head.
- **Warning:** then 3 warning circles appear on the ground at once, each where a meteor will land, and stay 2 seconds. Each lies within 10 units of the car (where the car was when they appeared), only where the map's placement check accepts a boulder (inside the map, off buildings and other boulders), never on or next to a boulder a meteor left that is still there (standing, fading or waiting for the car to move off; a free ground gap of 1.5 units, `boulder_clearance_units`, because the boulder's drawing is taller than its circle), not overlapping or next to another meteor still to land (same gap), and not on the kaiju. If no spot is free, fewer meteors fall; once a boulder is gone its spot is free again (T-147). A circle is the size of the boulder it will leave (3 units across). Placeholder look: a hazard amber disc with a thick, pulsing amber edge and an inner ring that closes in as the meteor gets near. Amber, not red, chosen while red was kept for Redgull's things and the kaiju alert signs (Visual style, Decisions); it stays amber after the rebrand; the final look comes from a separate art task.
- **Falling and impact:** in the last half second a placeholder meteor (a dark purple rock with a magenta glow and trail) falls onto the circle; when it lands, a placeholder burst of grey dust shows for half a second.
- **Hitting the car:** a meteor that lands with the car's centre within 1.5 units (the boulder's radius) takes 1 heart off the car (`impact_damage` 1, was 15) (which also cuts the combo) and knocks it back at 20 units a second, away from where it landed. One landing anywhere else does nothing to the car. A car more than 1 unit above the landing (jumping over it, or on a rooftop above it) is missed, the same rule as contact damage (T-418).
- **Hitting minions:** a meteor that lands damages every minion at the landing's level whose body reaches within 1.5 units (`impact_radius_units`) of it, for `minion_damage` (2 health points, a proposed number for the playtest; a minion has 4) (T-418).
- **New boulders:** each landed meteor leaves a plain boulder where it landed, the same size, look and collision as the map's own, so the car bounces off it and enemies walk round it. No challenge or arrow comes with it. If the car or the kaiju is on the spot as the meteor lands, the boulder appears as soon as they have moved off it (the car is knocked away at once on a hit), so nothing is trapped inside a boulder. Coins and health pickups on a boulder's spot, when it appears, are moved just outside it (a tenth of a unit clear, to the nearest side that is free ground), still collectable (T-418).
- **Pause and new runs:** the attack, the warning circles and the falling meteors stop while the game is paused, nothing lands once the run is over, and a new run clears them all.
- **Playtest switch:** for the board's playtest of this task the kaiju arrives 30 seconds into the run (the T-045 switch, above), so its first attack comes 35 seconds in; it is set back to 7 minutes right before the task merges.

#### Enemies on the rooftops and ramps (built in task T-207)

What the game does on a map with rooftops and ramps (the elevation map, Level design), following the decision "Enemies follow the car up the ramps". On the MVP map nothing here applies and the enemies walk as described above. Points marked "proposal" go beyond the decision and wait for the board's playtest. How it is built: `game/docs/enemies/ledges-and-rooftops.md`, "Enemies on the rooftops and ramps".

- **Standing on the ground:** every enemy stands on the ground under it: on the street, on a rooftop, or part way up a ramp, and is drawn lifted by that height, in the depth order at that height (over the rooftop it stands on, under a higher rooftop or a building in front of it).
- **Edges are walls:** a rooftop's edge stops an enemy like a wall from below, so an enemy climbs only along a ramp. From above it stops an enemy too, except where the enemy's way to the car drops off it (since T-226: "Enemies drop off ledges" below). It keeps its whole body off an edge, and slides along it. The sides of a ramp are walls too, except near its foot, where the ramp is still low (proposal). A weapon's knockback cannot push a minion over an edge either.
- **Finding the way:** on the car's own surface (the street, one rooftop, one ramp) an enemy walks straight at the car as before. Otherwise it follows a path to the car over the streets, ramps and rooftops, round buildings and boulders, going up each ramp along its middle (and down by a ramp only where that is shorter than dropping off an edge, T-226); the path is renewed about once a second, and at once when the car changes surface. **Minions (since T-380):** a minion walks straight at the car only while nothing stands between them (no building, boulder, rooftop edge or high ramp side on the line to the car, on any surface; a ramp's low foot and the climb along a ramp do not count), and otherwise follows a path round, so it no longer walks into a wall it cannot pass. Why they got stuck before: on the car's surface a minion walked straight at the car even with a wall in the way, so it stood against a ramp's high side, in the corner where a ramp's side meets its rooftop, or against a building just short of its corner; and at a ramp's bottom end it went back and forth between the street (straight at the car, onto the ramp's foot) and the ramp (another surface, so a path back down to the foot). It also turns for the next point of its path only half a unit from it, so its bigger body (T-379) does not cut a building's corner. The kaiju keeps the surface rule. Since the short buildings became platforms (T-405), whose edges lie between the grid's lines, a minion also checks the true ground near those edges before walking straight, and its path keeps a body's reach off them, so it no longer stands at such a platform's corner. A minion far off screen is kept for its walk round only when it is on another surface than the car (a rooftop or ramp), as before T-380.
- **Spawning:** minions come in from the screen's edges on the street only, never on a rooftop or a ramp. The kaiju arrives on the street too (proposal).
- **Staying round the car:** a minion on its way to a ramp is not removed for being far off screen, as long as it is within 120 units of the car (half the map; others are removed a screen beyond the visible one, as before), so minions walking round to a far ramp still arrive (proposal).
- **Contact damage at the car's level:** a minion or the kaiju only hits the car when the car's height (in the air too) is within 1 unit of the ground the enemy stands on: a car on a rooftop is safe from the minions on the street below its edge, and a car that jumps higher than 1 unit over a minion is not hit (proposal for the 1 unit).
- **Pushing apart:** minions push apart only from minions at their own level (proposal).
- **The kaiju (proposal):** the same rules as the minions: it climbs the ramps (its 4-unit body fits the 10-unit ramps), edges stop it, it is drawn at its height and only hits the car at its level, although it is taller than the highest rooftop.
- **The kaiju's way is planned for its size (built in task T-419):** following the decision "The kaiju only takes paths it fits through", the kaiju's way to the car is planned for its own 2-unit body, the minions' for theirs: every point of its way stays at least 2 units off buildings, props and boulders, a gap narrower than its 4-unit body is never on it (minions still go through), and it keeps 2 units off rooftops' and ramps' edges and the map's edge. Where its way drops off a rooftop it walks to a point 3 units back from the edge and drops from there, and it keeps to that way until it has dropped. Where a prop stands at a ramp's end, its way goes over the ramp cell by cell instead of along the ramp's middle. How: `game/docs/enemies/ledges-and-rooftops.md`.
- **Coins:** a coin is drawn at the height where its minion died, and stays on that level. Picking one up is unchanged: driving over it, at any height (proposal).
- **Weapons:** since T-326 (board, 2026-10-28) a weapon hits only enemies on its own height level (Weapons, Decisions, "Weapons hit only enemies on the car's own level"); at the time of this task they hit enemies at any height.

#### Enemies drop off ledges (built in task T-226)

What the game does on the elevation map, following the decision "Enemies jump down off ledges". Points marked "proposal" go beyond the decision and wait for the board's playtest. How it is built, and the hook for the falling art: `game/docs/enemies/ledges-and-rooftops.md`, "Enemies drop off ledges".

- **Dropping off:** an enemy on a rooftop whose way to the car is lower down takes the shortest way, which is usually straight off the nearest edge rather than round to a ramp. It walks out over the edge and falls. It never drops off a ramp's sides, never drops by accident (pushing apart or a weapon's knockback never takes it over an edge), and still never climbs an edge or ends up inside a building.
- **The fall (proposal):** it falls like the car does, from rest under the car's own gravity: about 0.7 s from a height-3 rooftop and 1 s from height 6, walking on at its usual speed meanwhile, so it lands a few units out from the wall (it cannot pass through a building or a higher rooftop while falling). It is drawn at its height in the air, in the depth order at that height, all the way down.
- **How the drop looks (proposal, placeholder):** from the moment it leaves the edge until it lands, a falling animation made by script from its walk frames: the legs flail (the walk cycle three times as fast for a minion, 2.5 times for the kaiju) and the body tips from side to side (and a minion is stretched a little); on landing a short squash (0.18 s for a minion, 0.25 s for the kaiju). The kaiju's ground shadow is not drawn while it is in the air. None of Greenbull's colours. Final falling frames come from a separate art task (T-227) and replace the placeholder per direction as soon as they are in the project.
- **Hurting the car while falling (proposal):** yes, with the same rule as on the ground, by its height in the air: a falling enemy hits the car only when the car's height is within 1 unit of the enemy's height, so one landing on the car hits it, and one still high above it does not.
- **The kaiju (proposal):** it drops off edges too, with the same rules and the same fall.
- **Numbers (proposal):** the gravity (the car's), the animation's speeds, tilt and squash are in the code, not balancing data.

#### Rusty Overcoat: the car damages what it touches (built in task T-463)

Following Drifting, Decisions, "Driving power-ups". Numbers: `game/data/power_ups.json`, `rusty_overcoat` (all proposals for the board's playtest). How it is built: `game/docs/enemies/minions.md`, "Rusty Overcoat".

- **The rule:** with Rusty Overcoat owned, a minion whose body touches the car's takes the owned tier's `contact_damage` (2 / 3 / 4 / 5; a minion has 4 health), with the usual red hit flash, and dies and drops coins as from any damage. The same level rule as the minion's own contact damage applies (the car within 1 unit of the minion's height). The minion still hits the car as before. The overcoat never stops an enemy's hit on the car, not even when its damage kills the enemy in that same step (T-477). Without the power-up, contact deals the minion no damage.
- **Repeat (proposal, open question for the board):** each enemy can be hit again only after the tier's `repeat_cooldown_seconds` (0.5 / 0.5 / 0.4 / 0.3 s), counted per enemy, so driving through a crowd hits each minion once per cooldown and a minion stuck to the car does not melt in one frame. The car's invulnerability after a hit does not stop it (that only protects the car).
- **The kaiju (proposal, open question for the board):** hit only when the tier's `hits_kaiju` is true, which is tier 4 only; it then takes the tier's damage on the same repeat cooldown.

### References

- Enemy numbers (the minion, how many minions are kept around over the run, coin drops, the kaiju and its meteor attack): [../game/data/enemies.json](../game/data/enemies.json), read through `game/scripts/data/enemy_data.gd`; the reasons for each number are in task T-039's result notes.


## 5. Weapons

*Source: [weapons.md](weapons.md). Which weapons exist and their progression trees.*

The car's weapons fire on their own, so the player only drives. The MVP has five: a simple gun the player starts every run with, which automatically shoots at enemies in range, a flamethrower out of the exhaust that fires only while drifting, a neon underglow that hurts enemies around the car, molotovs that leave fire on the ground, and a windshield wiper that sweeps enemies away.

### Decisions

- The MVP has 2 weapons: the starting gun and the exhaust flamethrower (below); since 2026-10-18, 5 (the three new weapons, below). Each level-up offers a choice between them (the level-up flow below).
- The final release has around 8 to 12 weapons, and each level-up offers 3 to choose from.
- **Size upgrades grow on screen** (board, 2026-10-24, after playing the game build): when a picked upgrade makes a weapon bigger (the wiper, the underglow, the flame), the weapon grows to its new size with a short animation instead of jumping to it. The damage area follows what is drawn. The timing is the Weapon Behavior Agent's proposal (T-286).
- The Game Data Agent works out how weapon upgrades scale from level to level, starting from the Unity prototype's upgrade values (below).
- **Starting gun:** the player starts every run with it. It has no visible weapon on the car, only the bullets it fires. It fires only when an enemy is within range, aims automatically, and fires at set intervals.
- **Exhaust flamethrower:** fires flames out of the car's exhaust, only while the car is drifting.
- Both MVP weapons copy the behaviour of the matching weapons in the board's Unity prototype (its starting gun and its Flame Exhaust): targeting, firing, the flame's shape and what turns it on. A report on how they work there is task T-022.
- Their upgrades also copy the Unity prototype's: the same upgrade tiers and what each tier changes.
- **Level-up flow in the MVP:** each level-up offers 2 choices and the player takes 1. The player starts every run with the gun, so the first level-up offers "get the flamethrower" or "upgrade the gun"; once the player has both, each level-up offers "upgrade the gun" or "upgrade the flamethrower".
- A weapon at its last upgrade tier is no longer offered: the level-up offers the other weapon's next tier instead, and if both are at their last tier, the level-up is skipped and the run goes on.
- Where the Unity prototype's weapons behave in unexpected ways (Unity weapons report, section 7), the MVP copies them, with three fixes:
  - **Copied:** the flame uses the gun's damage (2), not its own (1); the bullet's hit circle stays 2 units across, larger than it is drawn; the gun looks for a target only once per firing interval; the weapons never push enemies back; the flame's steering tier makes the car steer 20% faster, compounding; the flame's tier 5 only makes the burn flash last longer; reversing while steering counts as drifting, so the flame comes on.
  - **Fixed:** damage is not rounded to whole numbers, so the flame's "hotter flame" tier always adds damage; the flame's area is the same size whichever way the car faces; a bullet that misses is removed once it has flown past the gun's range.
- The exhaust flamethrower does not switch off the drift smoke (unlike the Unity prototype): smoke and flames both show. (Since 2026-10-22 any enemy is hit when any part of it touches the drawn flame; see "A smaller exhaust flame that burns what it touches" below.) The kaiju is hit when any part of its body overlaps the flames. The starting gun's bullet size and its wait before the first shot stay as built (the Unity values).
- **The flamethrower at height** (board, 2026-10-21): on a rooftop or in the air, the exhaust flames come out of the car's exhaust where the car is drawn, at its height, not somewhere else on the map; they burn what they touch at that spot. (T-206)
- **The underglow and the wiper at height** (board, 2026-10-21): the neon ring is drawn under the car at the car's height, so on a rooftop, a ramp or in the air it rises with the car instead of staying on the street; the windshield wiper's arm is lifted the same way. Their damage areas are unchanged. The molotov fire stays on the ground where the bottle landed, so it is not lifted. In the air the ring stays under the car (a proposal for the playtest). (T-225)
- **Three new weapons** (board, 2026-10-18), gained at a level-up like the flamethrower:
  - **Neon underglow:** neon lights under the car that make a circular area around it. Enemies inside take damage every second, and an enemy takes damage as soon as it enters the area.
  - **Molotovs:** thrown from the car at random, each one makes a circular area on fire where it lands. Enemies in a fire area burn and take damage.
  - **Windshield wiper:** one wiper in front of the car that sweeps in a semicircle, like a windshield wiper. Enemies it hits take damage and are knocked back. It is the only weapon that pushes enemies (the "never push enemies back" rule above is about the gun and the flamethrower).
  - They join the MVP, which then has 5 weapons (6 with Bricks, below). Each has 8 tiers like the gun and the flamethrower: getting it is tier 1, then 7 upgrades. Their numbers and what each tier changes are proposals by the agents, judged in the board's playtest.
  - Answers to the goal runner's questions (board, 2026-10-18): an enemy burns only while it is inside a molotov's fire area, not after it leaves. The windshield wiper sweeps all the time; it damages the kaiju but pushes only minions. The garage's damage bonus multiplies the damage of every weapon, the three new ones included. The starting gun's level-up card shows a small pixel-art gun.
- **A smaller exhaust flame that burns what it touches** (board, 2026-10-22, after playtests; replaces "a minion is in the flames when its centre is" of 2026-10-14): when the flamethrower is first picked up (tier 1) its flame is drawn 4 to 5 times smaller than today (a proposal of about a quarter of today's length and width), growing with its size tiers as before; it is drawn behind the car and behind the enemies, never over them; and its damage area is the flame as drawn, so a minion takes damage as soon as any part of it touches the visible flame (the kaiju as before, any overlap). (T-267)
- **A stronger wiper push** (board, 2026-10-22, after playtests): the windshield wiper's first level (tier 1, when it is picked up) pushes a minion back about twice the car's size; read as twice the car's length, 6 units (the car is 1 unit wide and 3 long), against 1.5 today. The later tiers keep their multipliers, so they grow from the new base. (T-266)
  - **Level-up offers with five weapons:** each level-up still offers 2 choices, now two different ones drawn at random from every choice available (getting a weapon the car doesn't have, or the next tier of one it has).
- **The first gift pack can hold any weapon** (board, 2026-10-28; replaces "The first level-up still offers 'get the flamethrower' or 'upgrade the gun'" above): the first level-up draws its two choices at random from every choice available, like every later level-up, not only the gun and the flamethrower. (T-321)
- **Bricks** (board, 2026-10-28): a new weapon. The car carries a load of bricks; each time the car lands on the ground after being in the air, from any height, a powerful impact wave goes out around it and damages the enemies it reaches. In the first build the wave is the same whatever the height of the fall. Its card makes it sound useless, so the player is tempted to try a jump and find out: the board's direction for the description is "Bricks - A bunch of bricks. No real use, other than making the car heavier." with a hint to jump. Text: T-322; numbers: T-323; the weapon: T-324; art: T-325.
- **Weapons hit only enemies on the car's own level** (board, 2026-10-28; replaces "Their damage areas are unchanged" in "The underglow and the wiper at height" above, for damage): on a map with rooftops and ramps, a weapon damages only the enemies on the same height level as the weapon's hit: the car's level for the gun, the flamethrower, the underglow, the wiper and Bricks, and the fire's level for a molotov. An enemy on the street is not hit from a rooftop above it, and the other way round. How a ramp's in-between heights and the kaiju count are the agents' proposals for the playtest. (T-326)
- **The gun one-shots minions and grows in bullets, speed and targets** (board, 2026-10-30; replaces the gun's tier plan in "The starting gun" below and answers the open question on upgrading how often it fires): from tier 1 one bullet kills a minion. Its upgrades go to how many bullets it fires and how fast, in this order: **+1 bullet** twice, **faster attack** twice, then at the halfway upgrade it **targets up to 3 enemies at once** (it has 3 bullets by then); then **+1 bullet** twice and **faster attack** twice, and at its last upgrade it **targets up to 5 enemies at once**. That makes 10 upgrades (tiers 2 to 11) against today's 7; the range and pass-through tiers go. What "targets up to N" means against today's closest-first spread, and the speeds, are the agents' proposals for the playtest. (T-408)
- **The neon underglow kills a minion in 2 ticks and pushes from tier 1** (board, 2026-10-30): each tick deals half a minion's maximum health at tier 1, so 2 ticks kill it, and from tier 1 it knocks enemies back a little (today it never pushes). How far, and whether the push grows with the tiers, are proposals. (T-409)
- **Weapons during the wreck** (board, 2026-10-30, audit): while the car is wrecked (Game loop architecture, Decisions, "The wreck decides the loss at its end"), damage already on the map keeps going (molotov fires, burning enemies) and the neon underglow keeps ticking; the bricks still go off if the wrecked car lands from the air. Nothing new is fired: no gun, no molotov throws, no wiper, no exhaust flamethrower. Built in T-414. Proposals for the playtest (T-414, not the board's yet): a bullet or a molotov bottle already in the air carries on and lands; a gun volley still queued is dropped; the flamethrower's burn tints already on enemies run out; and the weapons stop at once when the run ends, even in the middle of a step (a kaiju kill ends the run, and nothing later in that step damages anything).
- **Molotovs land where enemies can be** (board, 2026-10-30, audit): a molotov whose landing spot is inside a building or off the map picks another spot. Built in T-414. Proposals for the playtest: a short building counts as ground (a platform the car can drive onto), so a bottle may land on it; a bottle tries up to 30 spots and, if none fits, lands at the car.
- **The underglow barely pushes the kaiju** (board, 2026-10-30, audit; answers T-409's open point): the kaiju is pushed very little, just a slight stop at each damage tick. Minions are pushed as T-409 says.

### Content

#### Garage damage bonus

The garage's damage bonus upgrade (Garage design) is applied at the start of every run: its percentage multiplies the damage of the gun and the flamethrower, on top of each weapon's own tier (the two multiply). Level 0 changes nothing. Built in T-062.

#### Unity prototype weapons

Facts from the Unity prototype weapons report (sections 1 to 5). No new decisions.

- The prototype's starting gun is its "Simple Gun" (`SimpleGunWeapon`, data asset `Weapon_MachineGun`): the only weapon on the car when a run starts.
- The gun checks for living enemies within 12 units of the car's centre every 1.26 seconds and fires one bullet at the closest. Bullets fly straight from the car's centre at 15 units per second, deal 2 damage, and are removed on their first hit. Bullets that miss are never removed.
- The Flame Exhaust is on while the car is drifting (W or S held with A or D) at 0.85 units per second or more, and for 0.2 seconds after. It damages enemies inside a rectangle behind the car that starts each drift at half size and reaches full size (about 2.6 wide and 3.25 deep) after 1 second of drifting.
- An enemy entering the flame takes 2 damage at once, and every enemy inside takes 2 more every 0.2 seconds. The flame takes this damage from the gun's stats; its own asset's damage (1) is not used.
- Each weapon has 8 tiers: getting it is tier 1, and each later pick applies the next of 7 upgrades. The gun gets more bullets, faster fire, a wider range and, last, bullets that pierce the first enemy. The flame gets a bigger area, more damage, a longer burn flash, faster car steering and, last, an always-on flame.
- The prototype's level-up offers 3 choices drawn at random from power-ups, new weapons and the next tiers of owned weapons. A weapon at tier 8 is no longer offered, and when nothing is left the only choice is 4 coins.
- The report lists every value with its source, the differences from Solid Carbide's level-up flow, notes on porting to Godot, and open questions for the board: [weapons/unity-weapons-report.md](weapons/unity-weapons-report.md).

#### The starting gun (built in task T-041)

What the built gun does in the game. It follows Decisions and the Unity prototype weapons report, with the board's T-408 rework (Decisions, "The gun one-shots minions and grows in bullets, speed and targets"); the numbers are T-040's and T-408's ([../game/data/weapons.json](../game/data/weapons.json)). How the code is put together: `game/docs/weapons/shared.md` and `game/docs/weapons/starting-gun.md`.

- Every run starts with the gun at tier 1 and no other weapon; a new run puts it back to tier 1 and removes any bullets in flight. Nothing is drawn on the car, only the bullets.
- Every 1.26 seconds (at tier 1) the gun looks for living enemies whose centre is within 12 units of the car's centre. With none, it does nothing until the next check; with some, it fires a volley. It checks only at those moments, so an enemy that comes into range just after a check is shot at the next one.
- **Targeting rule** (T-408, a proposal for the playtest): the enemies in range are sorted closest first, and the tier says how many of them a volley aims at: 1 below tier 6, up to 3 from tier 6, up to 5 at tier 11.
  - **Below tier 6 (one target):** the volley's bullets leave 0.05 seconds apart, each at the closest enemy in range that is alive and not already doomed: an enemy counts as doomed when the gun's bullets in flight at it carry at least its health. So against minions (one bullet each) bullet 1 goes to the closest, bullet 2 to the next closest and so on, and each +1 bullet upgrade kills one more minion a volley; a tough enemy (the kaiju) takes the whole volley. When every enemy in range is doomed, the bullet goes at its first target anyway.
  - **From tier 6 (up to 3, at tier 11 up to 5):** the volley aims at that many of the closest enemies; bullet 1 goes to the closest, bullet 2 to the second closest and so on, going round them again from the closest when there are more bullets than targets. The whole volley leaves at the same moment, a fan of bullets.
  - Each bullet leaves the car's centre aimed at its target's centre at that moment, with no leading, and flies straight on.
- Bullets fly at 15 units per second and hit an enemy whose body comes within 1 unit of the bullet's centre, dealing 4 damage through the enemy's damage function (a minion's health, so one bullet kills a minion from tier 1; the garage's damage bonus only adds to it). A bullet is gone after its first hit, or once it has flown as far as the gun's range without hitting anything. Bullets never push enemies and pass through walls and boulders.
- The gun targets every damageable enemy, not only minions, so the kaiju will be shot as soon as it exists.
- The upgrade tiers (2 to 11, T-408; the gun's own last tier in the data, while the other weapons stop at 8) change the gun in the board's order: +1 bullet at tiers 2 and 3 (2, then 3 bullets a volley), 20% faster at tiers 4 and 5 (1.26 s at tier 1, then 1.06 and 0.893 s), up to 3 targets at tier 6, +1 bullet at tiers 7 and 8 (4, then 5), 20% faster at tiers 9 and 10 (0.754 and 0.639 s), and up to 5 targets at tier 11. The range stays 12 units and bullets never pass through an enemy. "20% faster" multiplies the fire rate by 1.2, as the level-up cards say; the interval is 1.2 s divided by the rate, plus the prototype's 0.06 s. The level-ups offer the gun's upgrades until tier 11 (the level-up offers, below).
- **The kaiju** takes the same 4 damage a bullet. With the gun alone that roughly halves its fight against T-039's numbers: about 158 s at tier 1 (was 315), 22 s at tier 8 (was 38) and 16 s at tier 11 (the kaiju's 500 health; flame and garage bonus shorten it further). A proposal for the playtest; Enemies' kaiju numbers are unchanged.
- The gun stops while the run is paused and once the run has ended.
- The bullets are a small cyan neon ball with a white-hot core, pulsing in 2 frames, drawn about half a unit above the ground (art: T-071, drawn by script, `game/art/effects/bullet.png`).

#### The exhaust flamethrower (built in task T-042)

What the built flamethrower does in the game. It follows Decisions (the prototype's Flame Exhaust with the board's fixes) and takes every number from [../game/data/weapons.json](../game/data/weapons.json). How the code is put together: `game/docs/weapons/flamethrower.md`, "The exhaust flamethrower".

- **Owning it:** a run starts without it. It is one of the car's weapons next to the gun, gained at a level-up (the level-up offers, below), which also applies its upgrade tiers. A playtest switch (`game/data/playtest.json`, `flamethrower_at_start`) gives it to the car at the start of every run.
- **On and off:** on while the car is drifting (W, or S, held with A or D: the car's own drift state) at 0.85 units per second or more, and for 0.2 seconds after the drift ends. Driving straight, steering while standing still, or drifting slower than that never lights it. From tier 8 it is always on. It stops while the run is paused.
- **Area (T-267):** the flame as it is drawn, at every moment: the outline of the pixels of the flame art's current picture (its direction and flicker frame), at the drawn size, from the exhaust, pointing back. There is no separate rectangle any more. At tier 1 the flame is a quarter of its old size (size factor 0.625, was 2.5): about 30 screen pixels long at full size, 15 at the start of a drift. Each drift starts it at half size; it grows to full size over 1 second of drifting (always full size at tier 8). It is the same size on the screen whichever way the car faces.
- **Why the area and the art differed before (T-267):** the area was a rectangle from numbers in the data (3.25 units deep, 2.6 wide at full size, lined up with the car in the flat world), while the drawing was the 95-pixel plume scaled by the same size factor, but with no link to the rectangle: the plume was about twice as long as the rectangle's depth on the screen, the rectangle started 0.175 units behind the car's centre and the drawing 0.42, and a rectangle is not a teardrop. A minion counted only by its centre, so the flame could cover most of its body without burning it.
- **Where it starts (T-267, a proposal for the playtest):** the car's rear bumper, 1.2 units behind its centre (it was 0.42, under the car's body). At a quarter of the size the whole flame would otherwise sit under the car and not show.
- **Who is hit (T-267):** an enemy is hit when any part of its body touches the flame: its body circle (the minions' 0.5 units, the kaiju's own size) against the flame's outline. It replaces "a minion is inside when its centre is" (board, 2026-10-14; Decisions, 2026-10-22).
- **Damage:** an enemy entering the flame takes 2 at once and flashes orange for 0.38 seconds; every 0.2 seconds while the flame is on, every enemy inside takes 2 more. No limit on how many it hits, no push. It burns every enemy, through their damage function.
- **Tiers:** tiers 2, 4 and 6 make the flame, drawn and hit area, bigger (x1.2, x1.2, x1.3: size factor 0.75, 0.9, 1.17); tier 3 multiplies the damage by 1.2 (2.4 per hit, not rounded); tier 5 makes the flash 0.5 seconds longer; tier 7 makes the car turn 20% faster; tier 8 keeps it always on at full size.
- **Look:** a pixel-art flame plume (orange, yellow and a pale core) out of the exhaust in 32 directions, flickering between 2 frames, drawn behind the car and behind every enemy (one depth step under the car's, so also under enemies standing at the same depth; over the ground, rooftops and buildings), on the street, on rooftops and in the air, at the car's height. The drift smoke still shows with the flames (board, 2026-10-14). Enemies it burns show small flames on them (`burning_flames.png`). Art: T-071, from a PixelLab sample the board approved (`game/art/effects/exhaust_flame_sheet.png`).

#### Numbers for the three new weapons (proposal, task T-166)

Proposals by the Game Data Agent for the board's playtest; the board judges and asks for changes. Numbers: [../game/data/weapons.json](../game/data/weapons.json). Each has 8 tiers (tier 1 is getting it; tiers 2 to 8 are 7 upgrades). Units and seconds as in the file. The garage damage bonus multiplies all of them.

- **Neon underglow:** circle of radius 2.5 around the car; 2 damage (half a minion's health, T-409) when an enemy enters and every 1 second inside, and each hit pushes a minion 0.5 units away from the car (the kaiju 0.1). Tiers: 2 radius x1.2; 3 damage x1.5 (3); 4 tick interval x0.75; 5 radius x1.25; 6 damage x1.5 (4.5); 7 tick interval x0.67; 8 radius x1.3 (final: radius about 5.85, damage 4.5 every 0.5 seconds).
- **Molotovs:** one thrown every 3 seconds at a random spot 3 to 8 units from the car; fire area radius 1.5 lasting 3 seconds; enemies take 2 on entering and every 0.5 seconds while inside. Tiers: 2 radius x1.2; 3 throw interval x0.8; 4 damage x1.5; 5 one more molotov per throw; 6 fire lasts 1.5 seconds longer; 7 radius x1.3; 8 one more molotov per throw (final: 3 per throw every 2.4 seconds, radius 2.34, 4.5 seconds, 3 damage).
- **Windshield wiper:** one arm 2.5 units long sweeping a 180 degree semicircle in front of the car at 240 degrees per second; 3 damage per hit, the same enemy can be hit again after 0.5 seconds; minions are pushed back 6 units (twice the car's length), the kaiju is damaged but not pushed. Tiers: 2 length x1.2; 3 damage x1.4; 4 sweep speed x1.25; 5 knockback x1.5; 6 length x1.3; 7 damage x1.4; 8 sweep speed x1.3 (final: length 3.9, damage 5.9, knockback 9).

#### Bricks

What the built weapon does in the game (built in task T-324). It follows Decisions ("Bricks", 2026-10-28), takes every number from [../game/data/weapons.json](../game/data/weapons.json) (the numbers below) and shows the card texts below. How the code is put together: `game/docs/weapons/bricks.md`, "Bricks".

- **Owning it:** a run starts without it. It is one of the car's weapons, offered on level-up cards like the other five, gained and upgraded through the same call (`upgrade("bricks")`); since T-321 it can be on the very first gift pack. A playtest switch (`game/data/playtest.json`, `bricks_at_start`, off) gives it at the start of every run.
- **The landing:** each step the weapon reads whether the car is in the air (the car's height model, the same airborne state the airtime trick uses) and counts the seconds; the step the car is back on the ground is the landing. A landing after at least the minimum time in the air (0.3 seconds) sends one impact wave; a shorter hop (a curb, a bump, a low step down) sends none. Any way of being in the air counts: a ramp's top, a rooftop's edge, any drop. Nothing is counted while the run is paused or after it ends.
- **The wave:** one wave at the landing spot, the same whatever the height of the fall (the impact speed is not read). Every enemy whose body is within the radius (4 units at tier 1) takes the damage once (6 at tier 1, times the garage damage bonus), the kaiju too: a minion counts when its body's edge is inside, an enemy that reports its body size (the kaiju) when any part of its body is. Nothing outside the radius is touched, and the steps after the landing send nothing more. Only the enemies on the level where the car lands are hit and pushed (since T-326, "Weapons hit only their own level" below). Minions that survive are pushed straight away from the landing spot by the knockback (4 units at tier 1), through the same call as the wiper's push; the kaiju is never pushed; a minion the wave kills is not pushed.
- **Two landings close together** (the cooldown, 0.5 seconds): a landing less than the cooldown after the last wave sends none, so a bounce cannot stack two waves on the same enemies.
- **Tiers:** as the numbers below (radius, damage and knockback multipliers), applied from code; the drawn ring follows the radius.
- **The car:** its handling is not changed; "making the car heavier" is only the card's joke.
- **Look:** T-325's art (Visual style, Decisions, "Bricks' art"): at the landing spot (on a rooftop, on the roof) an impact ring on the ground, the circle as seen in the isometric view, growing in stepped frames from the car's size out to exactly the damage radius in about a third of a second and showing for 0.6 seconds, with dust clouds and brick chips thrown up, then crumbling away; one script-drawn sheet per tier radius. The level-up card (and the HUD icon) shows T-325's PixelLab picture of a stack of bricks. T-324's code-drawn placeholder stays as the fallback for a radius with no sheet. No sound yet (the SFX bus has no fitting sound; a separate task can add one).

**Numbers** (proposed in task T-323): proposals by the Game Data Agent for the board's playtest, for the board's decision in Decisions ("Bricks", 2026-10-28). Numbers: `bricks` in [../game/data/weapons.json](../game/data/weapons.json), read through `WeaponData.bricks_at(tier)`. The weapon itself is T-324, which turned it on at level-ups (`offered_in_level_ups` true, `bricks` in `WEAPON_ORDER` and the choice ids in `level_up_offers.gd`). Same 8 tiers as the other weapons (tier 1 is getting it, tiers 2 to 8 are 7 upgrades; the card texts, T-322, are written for that count). The garage damage bonus multiplies its damage.

- **Damage 6**, once per enemy per landing. A minion has 4 health, so the first tier already kills a minion outright, as the board's "powerful impact wave" asks. A landing is rare (see below), so one hit has to be worth far more than the wiper's 3 per 0.5 seconds.
- **Radius 4** units around the car, a disc about 50 square units against the wiper's half disc of radius 2.5 (about 10). It is wide because the wave is the point of the weapon, and a player lands rarely.
- **Knockback 4** units, minions only, never the kaiju (the wiper's rule). Smaller than the wiper's 6: the wave is meant to clear space around the car and kill, and a minion that survives (kaiju excluded) is not thrown out of reach.
- **Minimum time in the air 0.3 seconds**, the same as the airtime trick's `min_seconds` (`combo.json`, Drifting, Content, "Airtime trick"): a curb or a bump stays under it, a ramp hop (about 0.7 seconds) and a rooftop fall (about 1 second) are well over it. One number for "a real jump" keeps the two features agreeing.
- **Cooldown 0.5 seconds** between waves, so a bounce or two quick landings cannot stack waves on the same enemies. It is rarely felt: a jump takes over 0.3 seconds in the air plus time on the ground.
- **Same wave whatever the height** (first build); the height does not scale any number.
- **Tiers:** 2 radius x1.2; 3 damage x1.5; 4 knockback x1.5; 5 radius x1.25; 6 damage x1.5; 7 knockback x1.5; 8 radius x1.3 (final: radius 7.8, damage 13.5, knockback 9). Radius and damage alternate so the weapon reads as a bigger, harder wave; the knockback steps are the wiper's tier 5 step.
- **How it compares:** the wiper at tier 1 does about 6 damage per second to an enemy it keeps hitting; the underglow 2 per second. Landings on the elevation map come from ramps and rooftop edges only, perhaps one every 10 to 20 seconds of a run that uses them, so Bricks' average damage per second to one enemy is about 0.3 to 0.6 at tier 1, but it hits everything within 4 units at once and kills a minion, so against a crowd it matches the wiper and fires only when the player jumps. If the board finds it too weak or too strong in playtest, damage and radius are the first numbers to move.

**Card texts** (task T-322; the board's line, kept word for word, with a hint to jump; scored 8 or more in the style loop). They are in [../game/scripts/ui/level_up_texts.gd](../game/scripts/ui/level_up_texts.gd). The upgrade texts follow T-323's 7 tiers (2 to 8: wider wave, harder hit, stronger knockback, wider wave, harder hit, stronger knockback, widest wave) and carry no numbers.

- `get_bricks.title`: Bricks
- `get_bricks.desc`: A bunch of bricks. No real use, other than making the car heavier. Maybe try a jump?
- `upgrade_bricks.tier2.title`: Wider Wave
- `upgrade_bricks.tier2.desc`: Each landing's impact wave reaches further. Greenbull calls it ground-breaking content.
- `upgrade_bricks.tier3.title`: Harder Landing
- `upgrade_bricks.tier3.desc`: Your landing wave hits harder. Greenbull calls it a high-impact brand activation.
- `upgrade_bricks.tier4.title`: Shove Factor
- `upgrade_bricks.tier4.desc`: Impact waves knock minions back harder. Never the kaiju; it doesn't take feedback.
- `upgrade_bricks.tier5.title`: Wider Wave II
- `upgrade_bricks.tier5.desc`: Each landing's wave spreads wider again. Greenbull calls it expanding the brand footprint.
- `upgrade_bricks.tier6.title`: Harder Landing II
- `upgrade_bricks.tier6.desc`: Your landing wave hits harder again. Greenbull is trademarking the thud.
- `upgrade_bricks.tier7.title`: Shove Factor II
- `upgrade_bricks.tier7.desc`: Landing waves shove minions even further, never the kaiju. Greenbull calls it outreach.
- `upgrade_bricks.tier8.title`: Widest Wave
- `upgrade_bricks.tier8.desc`: Your landing wave reaches its widest yet. Greenbull calls it a city-wide rollout.

#### The neon underglow (built in task T-168)

What the built underglow does in the game. It follows Decisions ("Three new weapons") and takes every number from [../game/data/weapons.json](../game/data/weapons.json) (the proposal above). How the code is put together: `game/docs/weapons/neon-underglow.md`, "The neon underglow".

- **Owning it:** a run starts without it. It is one of the car's weapons, gained and upgraded through the same call as the flamethrower (`upgrade("underglow")`), offered at a level-up (the level-up offers, below). A playtest switch (`game/data/playtest.json`, `underglow_at_start`, off) gives it at the start of every run.
- **Area:** a circle around the car's centre (radius 2.5 at tier 1), the same in every direction, moving with the car. A minion is inside when its centre is; an enemy that reports its body size, such as the kaiju, when any part of its body overlaps the circle (the flamethrower's rule).
- **Damage:** an enemy is hit on the step it enters, then every tick interval (1 second at tier 1) while it stays inside; each hit is the tier's damage times the garage damage bonus, through the enemy's damage function. No limit on how many it hits. Tier 1's hit is 2, half a minion's health (4), so a minion dies on its second tick; tiers 3 and 6 make it 3 and 4.5 (T-409). Each hit also pushes a surviving minion 0.5 units straight away from the car, at every tier (a proposal for the playtest; `knockback_distance` in `weapons.json`); the kaiju is damaged and only nudged 0.1 units away per tick (`kaiju_nudge_distance`, the board's "slight stop", 2026-10-30). It stops while the run is paused and once the run has ended.
- **Leaving and coming back** (the Weapon Behavior Agent's proposal, for the board's playtest): each enemy has its own clock. An enemy that leaves and comes back before a tick interval has passed since its last hit is not hit again on entering; it is hit once its interval is over, if it is still inside. One that was out for longer is hit as it enters.
- **Tiers:** as the proposal above (radius, damage and tick interval multipliers), applied from code.
- **Look:** a placeholder neon ring drawn in code under the car, the circle as seen in the isometric view: opaque cyan with a darker inner line and a dark outline, never in Greenbull's colours, sized with the radius tiers. The final art replaces it.

#### The molotovs (built in task T-169)

What the built molotovs do in the game. They follow Decisions ("Three new weapons" and the board's answer that an enemy burns only while inside) and take every number from [../game/data/weapons.json](../game/data/weapons.json) (the proposal above). How the code is put together: `game/docs/weapons/molotovs.md`, "The molotovs".

- **Owning them:** a run starts without them. They are one of the car's weapons, gained and upgraded through the same call as the others (`upgrade("molotov")`), offered at a level-up (the level-up offers, below). A playtest switch (`game/data/playtest.json`, `molotov_at_start`, off) gives them at the start of every run.
- **Throwing** (the Weapon Behavior Agent's proposal, for the board's playtest): a clock starts when the car gets them; each time it reaches the throw interval (3 seconds at tier 1), that tier's number of bottles leave the car's centre at once. Each lands at its own random spot: any direction around the car, at a distance picked evenly between 3 and 8 units. Where enemies are plays no part. A bottle takes half a second to land, along a small arc; this flight time is in the code, not the data.
- **Fire areas:** a circle on the ground where the bottle landed (radius 1.5 at tier 1), burning for the fire duration (3 seconds at tier 1), then gone. It does not move. Fire areas can overlap.
- **Damage:** an enemy inside a fire area is hit on the step it enters, then every tick interval (0.5 seconds) while it stays inside; each hit is the tier's damage times the garage damage bonus, through the enemy's damage function. An enemy that leaves takes nothing more (board, 2026-10-18). A minion is inside when its centre is; an enemy that reports its body size, such as the kaiju, when any part of its body overlaps the circle. Each fire area counts on its own, so an enemy inside two is hit by both (proposal). No push.
- **Pause and new run:** bottles in flight and fire areas stop while the run is paused or over, and a new run removes them all.
- **Tiers:** as the proposal above, applied from code. A fire area keeps the values of the tier it landed at.
- **Look:** placeholders drawn in code. The bottle is a small green bottle with a pale rag and a yellow flame, spinning as it flies. The fire is a flat circle on the ground, drawn under the buildings, enemies and car: orange with a yellow middle and a pale core, a dark rim and small yellow flickers. Never in Greenbull's colours. The final art replaces them.

#### The windshield wiper (built in task T-170)

What the built wiper does in the game. It follows Decisions ("Three new weapons" and the board's answers: it sweeps all the time, damages the kaiju, pushes only minions) and takes every number from [../game/data/weapons.json](../game/data/weapons.json) (the proposal above). How the code is put together: `game/docs/weapons/windshield-wiper.md`, "The windshield wiper".

- **Owning it:** a run starts without it. It is one of the car's weapons, gained and upgraded through the same call as the others (`upgrade("wiper")`), offered at a level-up (the level-up offers, below). A playtest switch (`game/data/playtest.json`, `wiper_at_start`, off) gives it at the start of every run.
- **The arm** (the Weapon Behavior Agent's proposal, for the board's playtest): one arm turning round a point on the nose of the car's body (half a unit ahead of its centre), 2.5 units long at tier 1. It sweeps from one side of the car to the other and back across the semicircle in front of the car (180 degrees) at 240 degrees per second, all the time, turning back at each end. The semicircle is fixed to the car, so it turns when the car turns.
- **Hits:** an enemy is hit when the arm touches its body as it sweeps. Each hit is the tier's damage times the garage damage bonus, through the enemy's damage function. **How often** (proposal): one enemy is hit at most once per pass (one sweep from one side to the other), and never twice within 0.5 seconds (the data's hit cooldown). So an enemy that stays in front of the car is hit about once per pass, about every 0.75 seconds at tier 1.
- **Knockback:** a hit minion is pushed 6 units (tier 1; 9 at the last tier) straight away from the car's centre, through the minion's knockback call (obstacles stop it). The kaiju is damaged but never pushed. The gun's bullets and the flamethrower still never push (tested).
- **Pause and new run:** the arm and its hits stop while the run is paused or over; a new run removes the wiper and puts the arm back to its start.
- **Tiers:** as the proposal above (length, damage, sweep speed and knockback multipliers), applied from code.
- **Look:** a placeholder wiper drawn in code: a dark steel arm with a pale grey rubber blade and a dark outline, from the car's nose out to the arm's tip, drawn over the car while it points down the screen and under it while it points up. Never in Greenbull's colours. The final art replaces it.

#### Weapons hit only their own level (built in task T-326)

What the game does on a map with rooftops and ramps (the elevation map, and levels from the level creator). It follows Decisions ("Weapons hit only enemies on the car's own level", 2026-10-28). Points marked "proposal" go beyond the decision and wait for the board's playtest. How it is built: `game/docs/weapons/shared.md`, "Weapons", "Levels".

- **Whose level:** the car's level for the starting gun, the exhaust flamethrower, the neon underglow, the windshield wiper (its push too) and Bricks (its damage and its push; the wave is on the level of the ground where the car lands). A molotov's fire burns on its own level, the ground's height where the bottle landed, wherever the car is by then. An enemy on another level inside a weapon's reach is not damaged and not pushed.
- **The starting gun:** it aims only at enemies on the car's level, so it does not fire (and wastes no volley) when the only enemies in range are on another level. Each bullet hits only enemies on the level it was fired on and flies past the rest.
- **The car's level:** the height of the ground under the car's centre: the street, the rooftop or the point of the ramp it stands on.
- **In the air (proposal):** the level under the car, the ground right below its centre. A car jumping across a rooftop still hits the enemies on that rooftop; once it is over the street, the ones on the street. Chosen over "nothing until it lands" so the weapons do not stop at every jump, and over the car's own height in the air so a high jump does not switch every weapon off.
- **A ramp's in-between heights (proposal): a tolerance of 1.5 units.** An enemy counts as on the level when its height is within 1.5 units of it. On a ramp (3 units of rise over 12) that is 6 units along the slope either way, so an enemy part way up a ramp next to the car is hit, while a rooftop is always at least 3 units from the street and the next rooftop, so nothing on another rooftop or the street below ever is. A falling enemy counts at its height in the air. The enemies' contact damage uses 1 unit (Enemies, Content, "Contact damage at the car's level"); the weapons' wider 1.5 lets a ramp's slope count a little more generously.
- **The kaiju (proposal): yes, on every level.** It is taller than the highest rooftop, so every weapon hits it from the street, a rooftop or a ramp, as before. Its push rules are unchanged (the wiper and Bricks never push it).
- **The MVP map:** a map without heights has no levels, so every weapon hits every enemy in reach exactly as before. An enemy that reports no height of its own also counts on every level.

#### Size upgrades grow on screen (built in task T-286)

What the built grow does. It follows Decisions ("Size upgrades grow on screen"). The numbers and reasons are the Weapon Behavior Agent's proposal for the board's playtest; the code is in `game/docs/weapons/shared.md`, "Weapons", "Size upgrades grow".

- **Which tiers grow:** the ones whose effect in `weapons.json` is a size. The windshield wiper's tiers 2 and 6 (arm length x1.2 and x1.3), the neon underglow's tiers 2, 5 and 8 (radius x1.2, x1.25, x1.3) and the exhaust flamethrower's tiers 2, 4 and 6 (flame size x1.2, x1.2, x1.3). Every other tier, and getting a weapon, plays no grow. The molotovs' tiers 2 and 7 (fire radius) play none either: each fire area is made when a bottle lands and keeps its size, so the next bottle just makes a bigger one and there is no standing weapon to grow (the board can ask for the fires on the ground to grow too).
- **When:** when the card or gift pack that raises the size is picked. The run is paused for the pick, so the grow starts as the game resumes and stands still while it is paused.
- **The curve (one place, `game/scripts/weapons/size_grow.gd`):** the size goes from the old size to the new one in **0.4 seconds** with a small overshoot (an ease-out-back, strength 3.0, about 20% of the step: a step is 20 to 30% of the size, so the size passes the new one by about 5% and settles) and ends exactly on the data's size. 0.4 seconds is long enough to read as growing and short enough that nobody waits for it; the overshoot is a small pop and not a wobble. The likes bar's spring (0.25 s, T-273) is the model; a weapon is bigger and further from the eye, so it gets a little longer.
- **Damage follows the drawing:** the wiper's reach, the underglow's circle and the flame's outline are all read from the size being drawn at each step, so nothing is hit outside what is drawn (and the overshoot is hit as drawn). Damage, timing and everything else are unchanged.
- **The wiper's art now follows its length (T-286):** the wiper's sheet was drawn for the first tier's 2.5 units and was never stretched, so the drawn blade stayed the same size at every tier while only the hit area grew. The art is now stretched by the arm's length over 2.5, so the drawing grows with the tiers and the hit area is the drawing. The underglow's ring and the flame already scaled with their size.

#### The level-up offers (built in tasks T-043 and T-172)

What the built level-up offers do. It follows Decisions ("Level-up flow in the MVP" and "Level-up offers with five weapons"). The screen that shows them is a separate UI task; how the code is put together: `game/docs/weapons/shared.md`, "Weapons", "The level-up offers".

- When a level-up's weapon choice starts (the run is paused for it, Game loop architecture), the car's weapons decide the choices. Each of the weapons (six since T-324 added Bricks) gives at most one available choice: "get" it while the car does not have it, or "upgrade" it (its next tier) once it does, until its last tier (8; the gun's 11 since T-408, each weapon's own last tier in the data). The gun is always owned, so it only has "upgrade the gun". That makes 11 possible choices: upgrade the gun, and get or upgrade the flamethrower, the neon underglow, the molotovs, the windshield wiper and Bricks.
- Each level-up offers 2 different choices drawn at random, all equally likely, from every choice available at that moment. They are shown in a fixed order (gun, flamethrower, underglow, molotovs, wiper, Bricks), not in the order drawn.
- The first level-up is drawn like every other one (Decisions, "The first gift pack can hold any weapon", T-321): two different choices at random from every choice available, so it can offer any weapon the car doesn't have (five besides the gun, with Bricks), or the gun's upgrade. A run that already starts with the flamethrower (its playtest switch) draws the same way, and the flamethrower's upgrades are among the choices.
- Taking a choice applies it at once (the weapon at tier 1, or its next tier) and the run resumes. If several levels were reached at once, their choices follow one after another, each drawn on its own.
- A weapon at its last tier is not offered. If only one choice is left, the level-up offers just that one (the docs say nothing here; the simplest case was taken). If none is left, the choice is skipped and the run goes on, as Decisions says.
- **Playtest switch** `all_weapons_at_start` (`game/data/playtest.json`, false, never visible to players): true gives the car every weapon (all six) at tier 1 at the start of every run, for the integration check and the board's playtest; the level-ups then offer only upgrades.

Titles and lines for the gun's tiers 2 to 11 (replacing today's tiers 2 to 8) and the changed neon underglow lines, keyed as in `game/scripts/ui/level_up_texts.gd`; T-408 and T-409 copy them. Numbers are the Project Lead's, for the playtest. Style loop scores in brackets.
