The gift pack's arrows keep clear of the pieces at their new places. **Where it is saved:** on this computer, in the same settings file as the other settings (`user://settings.cfg`, section `hud_layout`, one entry per moved piece), written once when Done is pressed (T-427's save-once rule), and used in every run from then on; Reset followed by Done removes the section. How it is built: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/hud.md`, "The HUD layout", and `pause-screen.md`.

#### The MVP pass: the screen gallery and the text list (T-479)

For the board's pass through every menu and text before the MVP (Decisions, "The board passes through every menu and text before the MVP"). Two scripts build the material, so it is rebuilt after every change. Run both from the repo root:

- **Screen gallery:** `python game/tools/screen_gallery.py` (add `--out <folder>` to change where it goes; `--no-text` skips the text list). It opens the game in a real window (not headless; about half a minute), walks through every screen and saves one 1280 x 720 PNG of each, with `manifest.json` (each screen's name, file, and how it was reached; a `not_reached` list with the reason for any it could not open). The game's own saves are never touched: settings, progress and the runs list point at throwaway files. The screens: main menu (splash), tutorial slides 1 to 3, garage, the run's HUD at the start, the HUD with the mission notebook page part done, a trick popup, the combo broken popup, the level-up gift pack screen, the driving power-up overlay, the pause screen, its trick list, its HUD layout editor, the time's up screen, the wreck, and the recap for a win, a time's up and a wreck. The runs list (Past streams) is not in the game yet, so it is listed under `not_reached`. A new screen is added to `game/tools/screen_gallery.gd`.
- **Scaling scan (T-493):** `python game/tools/screen_gallery.py --sizes --out art-archive/<task>` runs the same walk five times, with the root window resized to 1280 x 720, 1920 x 1080, 2560 x 1440, 3840 x 2160 and 3440 x 1440 (about a minute and a half; a window bigger than the monitor is clamped, so 3840 x 2160 comes out 3840 x 2130 on a 2560 x 1440 monitor and the maths uses the real size). For each screen it records the visible content Controls' pixel rectangles, compares the screen's coverage of the window (bounding box and summed leaf-content area) with 1280 x 720, and writes `scaling_report.md` and `.json` (screens worst first, then the pieces that shrink) plus a side-by-side `contact_sheets/<screen>.png`. A screen is flagged under 0.85 of its 1280 x 720 coverage, a piece under 0.70 of its area share. The maths is in `game/tools/scaling_report.py`.
- **Text list:** `python game/tools/text_inventory.py` (the gallery script runs it too), into `text_inventory.json` and `text_inventory.csv` (open the CSV in a spreadsheet). `text_files` lists every string of the text files (`game/data/*_text.json`, `screen_texts.json`, and the level-up cards' table `level_up_texts.gd`) with its source file, key, text, the screen it appears on and the file's own note when it has one. `code` lists, separately, the strings found in scripts: constants named as text (`TEXT_*`, `TITLE`, `NAMES`, `DESCRIPTIONS`, ...) and labels, buttons and tooltips set from a literal, with file and line. The scan goes by pattern, so a string built another way can be missed; developer tools (the level creator, tuning panel, test rooms) are skipped and named under `not_scanned`. The screen of each string comes from two tables at the top of `text_inventory.py`; a string whose screen is missing there says "(unlisted)" and a test fails until it gets a line.
- **Where it goes:** `screenshots/mvp-gallery/` at the repo root (git-ignored, outside `game/`).

#### Main menu

A plain screen (task T-054). The title "SOLID CARBIDE" is in big cyan letters in the free pixel-art font Press Start 2P (SIL OFL; licence and record in `game/fonts/press_start_2p/`) with a near-black outline; the "(work in progress)" line under it is unchanged word for word, in the same font, small and pale, with the same outline (T-432, proposals for the playtest). Behind everything is the **splash cover slot**: when `game/art/menu/splash.png` exists it fills the screen, cropped not stretched (aspect kept) with hard pixel edges (nearest filtering), under a 35% dark veil so the buttons stay readable; when it doesn't, a plain dark navy placeholder shows. The splash art itself comes from a later Asset Generation ticket. Below are three buttons in a column: Start, Garage and Exit (text approved in T-053). The menu only shows the screen: pressing a button sends the signal `start_pressed`, `garage_pressed` or `exit_pressed`, and what happens next is the screen flow (T-055). Keyboard (T-492): focus starts on Start; Up and Down (or W and S) move the selection through Start, Garage and Exit and wrap round (Left and Right, or A and D, keep it where it is), Enter or Space presses the selected one, and the selection shows with the shared button's focus plate; the neighbours are set explicitly in `KeyNav` (`game/scripts/ui/key_nav.gd`), not guessed by Godot, and only a fresh press counts, so a key held when the menu opens does nothing (W, A, S and D ignore key repeat, and are handled by `KeyNav.handle_wasd`). The scene is `game/scenes/menu/main_menu.tscn`; how to open it is in `game/docs/hud-and-menus/main-menu.md`, "Main menu".

#### The HUD

The first piece of the HUD (task T-090) is the run timer. It shows the time left in minutes and seconds (M:SS), counting down from 8:00 to 0:00, since T-335 as a digital clock in a dark panel at the bottom left of the screen (see "Timer clock" below); until then it was big cyan digits at the top centre. It only shows what the run reports (the run owns the time) and stops moving while the game is paused. It needs no text. It is shown in every run, whether the run scene is opened on its own or started from the main menu. The rest of the HUD (task T-049, a first layout the board adjusts in playtest) is in the same scene, `game/scenes/hud/hud.tscn`, which the run scene places on screen; how to open it is in `game/docs/game-loop/the-run.md`, "The run". It only shows what the run reports, and the texts are from T-048:

- **Top left (task T-338, the livestream HUD; Decisions, "The HUD looks like a livestream"):** the upright health bar and its heart are gone. A **row of hearts** (T-339's art, 18 x 16 pixels at 2x) sits at x36 y24 on the board's layout page (220 x 40 at 1152 x 648, each heart in a 44 x 40 cell): one heart per heart the car can have (5, plus the garage's), **full** for the hearts left and **empty** for the hearts lost, no half hearts. A heart lost flashes white and shakes for 0.4 seconds as it turns empty; a heart healed pops back in for 0.3 seconds (a proposal for the playtest). Past 10 hearts a second row starts under the first (a proposal). Under the row, the **weapon icons** column at x12 y88 (the layout page): one per weapon the car has, the starting gun included (proposal), in the order taken, each 48 x 48 pixels (since T-429 the HUD's own 24 x 24 icon, `art/hud/weapon_icons.png`, at 2x, nearest filtering; before, the level-up card picture squeezed to 48) with 8 pixels between rows. A weapon above tier 1 shows "x2" ... "x8" (its tier) to the right of its icon, in Bangers size 32, white with a black outline (proposal for the playtest). It updates the moment a weapon is taken or upgraded and empties back to the gun in a new run. How it is built: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/hud.md`, "The hearts row".
- **Sub goal (task T-337, the livestream HUD; Decisions, "The HUD looks like a livestream" and "\"Hype Lv\" is gone"):** the likes bar, its "Likes ... Hype Lv" row and the heart in that row are gone; in their place is the **sub goal**, on the right edge about two thirds down: 128 x 180 pixels with its top left at x988 y340 on the board's layout page (saved at 1152 x 648), anchored to the right edge, so it keeps its 36 pixel margin from it and the same share of the height at other window sizes. It is a 128 x 128 **square** (T-339's frame art at 2x: a dark outline, a white ring, a black inside with rounded corners) that **fills green from the bottom** with the subs gained toward the current goal (the XP within the level, as the likes bar did), in whole art pixels (2 screen pixels), following the inside's rounded corners, with a lighter top line; the green is the HUD's health green, not Greenbull's light green. The fill keeps the likes bar's spring (T-273): when subs come in it shoots to its new level in 0.25 seconds with a small overshoot and settles, never below the old level and never drawn past full; the drain empties it slowly, without a spring; it stands still while the game is paused. **The gift pack** (`art/gift_pack/package.png`, cropped to its box) is centred inside it and fills 80% of the square (a 10% margin on each side), kept to its shape, with hard pixel edges; it is **greyed out and dimmed** (grey at 60% brightness, a proposal) while the goal isn't reached, and shows in **full colour** from the moment the goal is reached. **Under the square**, centred: the subs icon (T-339, at 2x) and "{subs} / {goal} SUBS" (T-331's text, Bangers 20, white with a dark outline), for example "42 / 156 SUBS"; the row is a little wider than the square. **When the goal is reached** the level-up happens at that moment, as before (the helicopter brings the gift pack; the run pauses at the pickup): the square springs to full, the gift lights up and bounces (it grows to 1.2 times, dips under its size and settles), and a pixel glow ring (white, pale mint and green, two art pixels wide, just outside the frame) flickers round the square, for one second in twelve pixel-art frames a second, playing whether the run is paused or not (proposals for the playtest). The label reads "{goal} / {goal} SUBS" while it is full. Then the square starts again from empty, the gift greys, and the label shows the next goal, the fill springing to the subs left over. Levels coming one after another restart the celebration; a new run starts it empty. At the top level it stays full with the gift lit. There is no level number or "Hype Lv" text anywhere: the level shows only through the sub goal. The flames of the combo's top heat step (below) burn along the square's top edge. The combo counter stays at the bottom centre where it was (its bottom edge 116 pixels above the screen's bottom), until the live viewers counter takes its place (T-336). How it is built: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/hud.md`, "The sub goal".
- **Combo heat (task T-131, decision of 2026-10-14):** the combo counter heats up in steps as the multiplier climbs, chosen from the multiplier the counter shows (two decimals): **base** (above x1.0, below x2.00) is the pink counter above; **step 1** (from x2.00) is bigger and yellow, with a light pulse (it pops a little on each beat and eases back); **step 2** (from x3.00) is bigger again and orange, with a yellow glow ring round its dark outline and a stronger, faster pulse; **step 3** (from x4.00 up to the cap, x6 today) is the biggest, white-hot, with a glow ring that flickers between oranges and yellows and the strongest pulse, and the **likes bar is on fire** (since T-337 the flames burn along the sub goal square's top edge, full height along all of it, since the bar and its texts are gone): pixel flames (white-hot at the base, then yellow, then orange at the tips, with a few sparks) flicker along the top of the bar. They rise tallest over the filled part of the bar and in the gap between "Likes" and "Hype Lv", stay low over the empty part, only lick the bottom of the texts (drawn on top of them), and reach only the top few pixels of the bar, so the fill and the texts stay readable; they never reach the counter. When the combo drops (drain or a collision cut) the look drops to the step of the new multiplier, and at x1.0 the counter hides as before. The pulse grows the counter upward and to both sides from its bottom centre, so it never moves into the row below. The thresholds (2, 3, 4) are kept in one place in the code. Everything is drawn in code (no generated art), in oranges, yellows and whites, never in Greenbull's colours. The effects stop moving while the game is paused. No sound. A screenshot fixture shows the four steps in a run (`game/docs/hud-and-menus/hud.md`, the HUD).
- **Level-up animation (task T-139, replaced in T-337):** the likes bar's level-up animation (a white-hot sweep across the bar, sparks, and "Hype Lv" popping bigger) went with the bar and the "Hype Lv" text; the sub goal square's celebration (above) takes its place.
- **Bottom left, above the clock:** "Coins" followed by the number collected this run, in yellow. Moved there from the top right (board, 2026-10-28; T-341). Saved layout at 1152 x 648: x16, y496, 108 x 36 (28 pixels above the clock), anchored to the bottom-left corner so it keeps its margins at other window sizes.
- **Timer clock (task T-335, the livestream HUD):** the timer is at the bottom left, 200 x 72 pixels with its corner 16 pixels from the left and bottom edges (the board's layout page, saved at 1152 x 648: x16 y560), anchored to that corner so it keeps its margins at other window sizes; the coins counter sits above it (T-341). Dark panel, digits as "M:SS", glowing. The digits are **green** above 3:00, **yellow** to 1:30, **orange** to 0:30 and **red** below (proposals; numbers and colours in `game/data/hud.json`, `timer_clock`). Since T-429 it shows T-339's clock art: the panel and the seven-segment digits, both at 2x (the HUD's style in code, above). Nothing at the top centre any more.
- **Live viewers counter (task T-336, the livestream HUD; Decisions, "The HUD looks like a livestream" and "Tricks bring viewers, shown in one colour"):** the combo counter ("Combo x2.00" above the likes bar) is gone; the combo shows as the stream's live viewers at the bottom right, 240 x 72 pixels with its corner 16 pixels from the right and bottom edges (the board's layout page at 1152 x 648: x896 y560), anchored to that corner. It is T-339's dark viewers panel with the red LIVE badge and the viewers' eye on its left, and on its right the number over "WATCHING" (T-331's texts, Livestream HUD texts below), in the comic font. It always shows, even with no combo (2,500 viewers at x1). The number counts toward the viewers for the current multiplier (T-332's curve, speeds and short format, Game loop architecture, ViewersData): up after tricks, down when the combo drains or a crash cuts it, and it wobbles a little all the time, so it never sits still while the run goes; everything stands still while the game is paused. **One viewers colour:** cyan (#33e1ff, T-339's panel rim and eye; a proposal), used for nothing else in the HUD: the number at the base look, "WATCHING", the eye and the trick popups' amounts. **Heat:** the look changes on T-332's steps (20,000, 84,736 and 236,026 viewers, the same moments as the old x2, x3 and x4): at each step the number grows (28, 30, 32 and 34 pixels) and takes the old combo counter's heat colour, glow and pulse (yellow, then orange with a yellow glow, then white-hot with a flickering glow); from 1,000,000 viewers the panel is **on fire** (T-339's 12 fire frames, a one second loop round the panel). The step follows the number the counter is counting toward, so it heats up when a trick's viewers land. **Tricks bring viewers:** each trick popup shows its name and "+{viewers}" (the viewers the trick brought, T-332's `trick_gain`, for example "ALT DRIFT! +5,938" or "+12.0K") with the eye after it, in the viewers colour with a black outline, at every heat step (the popups' rings and flames are unchanged). 0.3 seconds after the popup shows, its amount leaves it (the bubble stays, with the name only) and flies across the screen on an arc into the counter's number in 0.55 seconds, speeding up as it goes; the trick's viewers count in when it lands, and the counter **bumps** (a quick pop of the number and a cyan flash of the panel). A popup pushed out by the three-popup limit before its amount left lets its viewers in at once. **Crashes:** when a crash cuts the combo (the COMBO BROKEN! popup, as before), the counter **flashes red** (the combo broken popup's warning red-orange, number included, 0.45 seconds) and "-{viewers lost}" (T-332's `crash_loss`, for example "-226K") in that red drops away from it, falling and fading over 0.9 seconds, while the number falls. The combo draining away is not a crash: no flash, no drop. The timings and sizes are proposals for the playtest, in `game/data/hud.json` (`viewers_counter`). The likes bar's fire at x4 and the drift marks keep today's combo heat (T-337 replaces the likes bar). How it is built: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/hud.md`, "Live viewers counter (HUD)".
- **Reaction icons (task T-351, the livestream HUD; Decisions, "Reactions like a livestream"):** little pixel hearts and thumbs up (placeholders drawn in code, in pink, orange, violet and white; the art is T-352), 90 percent opaque, 4 screen pixels per art pixel, 60 on screen at most, under every other HUD piece. **A burst:** when the sub goal is reached (once per goal), 10 icons pop out of the sub goal square at once, fan up and out, slow down and fade within about two seconds. **Floating up like a real stream's live reactions (quick tuning, board, 2026-10-28):** from random spots **on the right side, over the live viewers counter's width** (the side where the view count is; the board, 2026-10-28), icons rise up the right side of the screen, a flow of 1 or 2 at a time at uneven gaps (the mean gap times a random 0.4 to 1.8), each popping in from half size, swaying a little and fading out as they near the top. None at the base step (below 20K viewers); from the first heat step a lively flow, busier at each: 2, 3.5 and 5 groups per second at the three heat steps and 7.5 at the fire step (from 1M). The board's choice replaces the first idea of the left and right thirds and the second, anywhere along the bottom: they stay on the viewers counter's side and never drift into the middle where the car is. Pause freezes them; a new run clears them. All the numbers are proposals for the playtest, in `game/data/hud.json` (`reactions`). Where the code is: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/hud.md`, "Reaction icons". **Bad reactions when the combo breaks (task T-356; Decisions, "Bad reactions when the combo breaks"):** at the same moment as the COMBO BROKEN! popup and the viewers counter's red flash (a crash that cuts the combo, once per crash; the combo draining away starts none), 10 bad reactions start one after another over about 1.5 seconds from the viewers counter's height, at random spots in the same right-side lane, and rise faster than the floaters (260 to 420 pixels per second, living 1.4 to 2 seconds). A mix of six placeholder icons drawn by script (T-357 swaps in the art): a crying-laughing face, a thumbs down, a face peeking between its hands, a broken heart, a skull and a screaming face; same size and opacity as the good ones, none in Greenbull's colours. They count toward the 60 cap, freeze on pause and clear on a new run. Numbers (proposals): `game/data/hud.json`, `reactions` (`bad_*`).

**During the wreck (task T-360; Game loop architecture, Content, "Wrecked"):** when the last heart is gone the HUD stays on screen for the wreck's 3 seconds, as it was at that moment, so the stream still feels live (a proposal for the playtest): the hearts row all empty, the clock stopped at the time survived, the coins and the sub goal unchanged, the live viewers counter around its last number. Nothing on the HUD reacts to the wreck itself, and nothing new appears (no text). Pause works as always and freezes the wreck. Then the run ends as before (the main menu, later the recap).

**The mission notebook page (task T-458, goal G-009; Game loop architecture, Decisions, "Mission packs"; texts: "Mission notebook and power-up texts" below).** The current mission shows on the left of the HUD as a notebook page, between the weapon icons above and the coins counter below (176 x 180 at the 1152 x 648 layout, from x 12, y 304; it scales with the HUD like every piece). Placeholder art drawn in code: pale paper, blue ruled lines, a red margin line, dark Bangers ink; the art ticket replaces it. The header "Content quota" is at the top, then one line per goal of the current mission, each with a checkbox. A quantity goal's line holds `{done}/{total}` and changes live with each step of progress; a duration goal has no count. A done goal has a ticked box and its line crossed off. When the mission completes the next one replaces the page's lines; after the last one the page hides. Proposals for the playtest: its place and size, and that the page is fixed (the movable HUD, T-453, was not on the branch). How it is built: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/hud.md`, "Mission notebook page (T-458)". Screenshots: `art-archive/T-458/screenshots/`.

**The kaiju's health bar (task T-050, decision of 2026-10-15 below):** a bar on top of the kaiju in the world, following it. It is hidden until the kaiju appears, shows its health (it follows the run's kaiju health signal) and disappears when the kaiju dies or a new run starts. It is as wide as the kaiju's drawing (the width comes from the kaiju's sprite, so the final art keeps it fitting) and sits just above its head. It is a neon purple fill on a white background with a black outline (stepped pixel corners, as in the combo popups) and thin black dividers at every 10% of its health; hard pixel edges, drawn in code, no text and no red. It always draws above every building, as the trick popups do. How it is built is in `game/docs/enemies/kaiju.md`, "The kaiju's health bar". The arrow to the nearest challenge is not in the MVP (T-098). The HUD stays clear of the trick popups (near the car) and the pause strip (below the timer); while paused, the strip's dark band runs across the whole width over the lower part of the health bar.

#### Livestream HUD texts

Task T-331 (Extended narrative, Decisions, "Subs"; each line scored 8 or more in the style loop). In capitals in the HUD's comic style (Bangers). They are in `game/scripts/hud/hud.gd` and `trick_popups.gd`. "Hype Lv" and the hype level are gone for good (board, 2026-10-28): no text names them; T-337 removed the old row from the code (HUD, "Sub goal"), and the older HUD paragraphs that still mention it describe the old HUD.

- **Sub goal label**, under the square: `{subs} / {goal} SUBS`, with the subs icon beside it (T-339: the proposal instead of the star), not part of the text (`TEXT_SUB_GOAL`). Example: "42 / 156 SUBS".
- **Live badge** on the live viewers counter: `LIVE` (`TEXT_LIVE_BADGE`). T-339's badge art carries the word in its pixels; the counter uses the art (T-336).
- **Viewers unit** after the counter's number: `WATCHING` (`TEXT_VIEWERS_UNIT`), for example "20,000 WATCHING". On the counter it sits under the number (T-336, a proposal).
- **A trick's viewers** on its popup: `+{amount}` (T-082's text, `ADDED_TEXT`), {amount} being the viewers it brought in T-332's short format (T-336). **The viewers a crash lost**, dropping from the counter: `-{amount}` (`LOST_TEXT`, the board's "-{viewers lost}", T-336).
- **Subs word** (`TEXT_LIKES`, value renamed): `Subs`, replaced "Likes" in the likes row; the row went in T-337, so the HUD no longer shows the word on its own (the sub goal label ends in SUBS).
- **Reward popup:** `TRENDING! +{subs} SUBS!`, replaces "Trending! +{likes} Likes".
- **Molotov tier 6 card aside:** "Linger for subs." replaces "Linger for likes."

#### Trick popups

Task T-091. When the car sends a `trick` signal (Game loop architecture; the ids are in `game/docs/driving/tricks.md`, "Tricks"), a comic-style text pops out just above the car with the trick's name, grows quickly to full size, rises a little (about 20 pixels, easing out) and fades, in one second: LONG DRIFT! (extended drift), FULL 360! and ALT DRIFT! (text approved in T-082). The two aerial tricks (T-218; Drifting, Decisions, "Aerial tricks") have their own popups: **AIR 180!** and **AIR 360!** (left and right turns read the same), for T-219 to use word for word; the word AIR keeps an air 360 apart from the drift's FULL 360!, and like the others each is followed by its "+{amount}" when the combo adds one. The airtime trick (T-241; Drifting, Decisions, "Airtime trick") pops **HANG TIME!** on every landing after the car was in the air, followed by "+{amount}", for T-242 to use word for word. It does not show the airtime itself (no seconds in the popup): the live airtime counter already shows the number while the car is up, and the line stays short and the same size as the others (a proposal for the playtest). HANG TIME! is different from AIR 180! and AIR 360!, which name a turn: it names the time in the air, and it can pop together with them on the same landing. The thread the needle trick (T-271; Level design, Decisions, "Thread the needle"), driving between two obstacles the board marked as a pair, pops **THREAD THE NEEDLE!** followed by "+{amount}", for T-272 to use word for word: the board's name for the trick, in capitals with an exclamation mark like the others. Extended-drift popups are smaller, since they come every second. The look (task T-084, reworked after the board's playtest of 2026-10-13) is a comic-book popup: a white rounded rectangle (stepped pixel corners, not a jagged burst, board 2026-10-14) fitted to the text with a small padding, with a black border, every letter black (trick names and amounts alike) in the Bangers comic font on one straight baseline, with hard pixel edges (no smoothing) and no other colour. Black on white reads over both the dark asphalt and the dusty gravel. One popup pixel is two art pixels. Bangers has capitals only, so "Trending! +{likes} Likes" shows in capitals. It sits near the car, clear of the run timer at the top centre. Since task T-125 it follows the car for its whole life (Decisions, 2026-10-13): it is placed relative to the car's drawn position (the position the camera follows, set in the physics step so it never shakes), still pops above the car, grows, rises relative to the car and fades. Popups shown close together (a long drift every second plus a 360, or several tricks on one step) are stacked: a new popup that would overlap one already showing is moved up in steps of 4 pixels until it is clear, with a 4 pixel gap, and it stays at that place relative to the car. Since the board's playtest of 2026-10-14 popups are smaller and never go higher than half way from the car to the top of the screen: the highest popup's top edge stays at or below a quarter of the screen height from the top, at any window size and camera zoom (measured on screen). At most three popups show at once (a fourth makes the oldest go away), and they are small enough that three stack under that limit at the default zoom (14.4) and window (1152x648): the popup starts about 30 pixels above the car and rises about 20, and it rises fast at first and slows towards the end, where it fades (a cubic ease-out over the same one second). The challenge popup and the drift prototype follow the car the same way. It works in the run, including runs started from the main menu, and in the drift prototype. The challenge popup (task T-092) reuses it: when a challenge is completed, the run state's `score` signal shows "Trending! +{likes} Likes" (text approved in T-048, `hud.score_flash`) from the car in the same look and size as the normal trick popups, with the likes the challenge gave. Since task T-083 each trick popup also shows what the trick added to the combo, after its name, in the approved "+{amount}" text (T-082): "LONG DRIFT! +0.05", "FULL 360! +0.25", "ALT DRIFT! +0.5". At the combo cap the trick adds nothing and only the name shows. In the run the popups follow the run state's combo signal; the drift prototype has no combo and shows the name only. How it is built is in `game/docs/hud-and-menus/popups.md`, "Trick popups". The popups are always drawn above every building, sign, boulder and the car (task T-132, board 2026-10-14): a popup has its own absolute depth at the top of the game's drawing range, not tied to the map's depth numbers, so a skyscraper or a short building never hides one, however tall the map grows. They still draw under the HUD and the pause and level-up screens. The popups heat up with the combo (task T-133, Decisions, board 2026-10-14), on the same steps as the HUD's combo counter (same thresholds, one place): a trick popup takes the step of the multiplier the trick brought the combo to, and the challenge popup the combo's multiplier when it shows. Below x2 the popup is the plain black and white one above, with no colour. From x2 (step 1) the black border becomes a thin black outline round a yellow ring (the counter is yellow at this step). From x3 (step 2) the ring is wider, orange with a yellow inner ring, and the "+amount" is orange with a thin black outline. From x4 up (step 3) the popup also has a flaming edge: pixel flames in the burning likes bar's style and colours (white-hot next to the popup, then yellow, orange-yellow and orange at the tips, the odd spark), tall over the top edge, short at the sides and below, flickering in pixel-art frames (twelve a second). At every step the fill stays white and the trick names black; oranges and yellows only, never in Greenbull's colours; hard pixel edges. The hotter rings and flames reach a little past the plain popup, but stacking, the height limit and the three-popup limit use the plain popup's size, so they work as before. The drift prototype has no combo and keeps the plain popup. **Built ahead of drawing (T-480, an audit fix, no change to the look):** a popup's pictures are made before it is first drawn, never while drawing: a trick's name at every heat step and flame frame, and the combo broken card, are baked on worker threads when a run starts and kept for the run; a popup's own picture (its amount is new each time) is made when it is shown, and its other pictures (flame frames, the look without the amount) are asked for from worker threads at the same moment. The cache of such pictures is bounded.

#### Combo broken popup

Task T-244 (decision: Decisions, "Combo broken popup", 2026-10-21). When a crash cuts the combo, the popup pops from the car like the trick popups, in red and broken-looking, with this exact text, for T-245 to use word for word: **COMBO BROKEN!**. It is one short line in the trick popups' voice (capitals, exclamation mark, like LONG DRIFT! and AIR 360!) and reads as a loss. Proposal for the playtest: it shows no amount lost (no "-{amount}"), only the line; the combo counter dropping to nothing already shows the size of the loss, and a bare line stays readable at a glance mid-crash.

Task T-245 builds it (proposals for the playtest, the board decides the look): it appears only when a collision or any damage actually takes a combo down (the run state's `combo_broken`), never with no combo to cut and never when the combo drains away. It is the trick popups' card (same size, same place above the car, follows the car, stacks with the trick popups, same one second and fade) but a warning red-orange card (255, 80, 16, clear of the heart's red) with a black border and white lettering with a black outline, cracked in two along a jagged line through the text. It shakes for the first 0.3 seconds, and from 0.08 seconds the right half falls away (down and a little right) while it fades. Hard pixel edges, no semi-transparent pixels. How it is built: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/popups.md`, "Trick popups".

#### Time's up screen

Task T-316 (decision: Decisions, "Time's up screen", 2026-10-28). When the timer runs out with the kaiju alive, the 3-second failure screen shows this exact headline, for T-317 to use word for word: **STREAM OVER, KAIJU STILL TRENDING!**. It is in the trick popups' voice (capitals, ending in "!"), reads at a glance, and has no second line: the headline says the time is up and that the kaiju is still standing, in the stream's own language, a little out of touch about the disaster, and never makes fun of the city's people. The style loop scored it 9/10 in one round. It is stored in `game/data/screen_texts.json`, key `time_up.headline`.

Task T-317 builds it (proposals for the playtest, the board decides the look and the motion). At 0:00 the run is lost and frozen: the clock stays at 0:00, the car, enemies and pickups stand still, and nothing counts (no damage, likes, coins or kills). The screen plays for 3 seconds (`game/data/run.json`, `time_up.seconds`), then the run ends exactly as before. It can't be skipped, and Escape doesn't open the pause screen over it (a skip key would be cheap if the board wants one). Look, a placeholder drawn in code: the headline on the COMBO BROKEN! popup's cracked warning red-orange card (black border, white Bangers letters with a black outline, hard pixel edges), at twice its pixel size on the default window, over the run dimmed to about half (the HUD too). The crack runs through the space between "OVER," and "KAIJU", so every letter stays whole. Motion: the run dims in a quarter second while the headline slams in from more than twice its size; it shakes on impact for about half a second; at about 1 second the crack opens, the halves part, the right one drops and tilts; it holds, cracked, until the 3 seconds are up. Health losses have their own wreck instead (T-360). How it is built: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/time-up-screen.md`. Screenshot and GIF: `art-archive/T-317/screenshots/`.

#### Mission notebook and power-up texts

Task T-456 (goal G-009; Game loop architecture, Decisions, "Mission packs"; Drifting, Decisions, "Driving power-ups"). All in `game/data/screen_texts.json`, under `missions` and `power_ups`, each with a `_comment` line saying where it appears. Every text scored 8 or more in the style loop (T-456's Style review). `{...}` are slots the UI fills; goal lines are labels in sentence case, so the count comes after the words. Proposals for the playtest.

- **Notebook page header** (`missions.header`), top of the small notebook page on the left of the HUD: "Content quota".
- **Goal lines** (`missions.goals.<trick id>`), one per trick type in `game/data/missions.json`, fixed missions and generator rules. Quantity goals hold `{done}/{total}`: alternate_drift "Alt drifts {done}/{total}" (the board's example "2/4 Alt drifts", reworded to pass the label rule); three_sixty "Full 360s {done}/{total}"; air_one_eighty "Air 180s {done}/{total}"; air_three_sixty "Air 360s {done}/{total}"; thread_the_needle "Needles threaded {done}/{total}". Duration goals have no count: extended_drift "Hold one drift for {seconds} seconds"; airtime "Rack up {seconds} seconds of airtime".
- **Power-up overlay header** (`power_ups.overlay_header`), opened when a mission completes: "Mission done: soup up the car". It talks about the car and a mission, not Greenbull or a gift pack, so it reads differently from the weapons gift screen.
- **Take button** (`power_ups.take_button`): "Take power-up". Not shown since T-475 (the cards have no button); the text stays in the data.
- **Power-up names** (`power_ups.names.<id>`), on each card, the board's names unchanged (the style loop scored them 9): Rev Charge, Jump, Bouncy Bumpers, Rusty Overcoat.
- **Power-up descriptions** (`power_ups.descriptions.<id>`), one template per power-up that names the offered tier's number, filled from `game/data/power_ups.json`: Rev Charge "Hold W+S {charge_seconds}s, let go of S: {boost_seconds}s boost. Brakes, now monetized."; Jump "Press Space to hop. Next hop in {cooldown_seconds} s. Airtime clips better than braking." (`cooldown_seconds`); Bouncy Bumpers "Bounce {bounce_multiplier}x farther off walls and obstacles. Crashes are content too." (`bounce_distance_multiplier`); Rusty Overcoat "The car deals {contact_damage} damage to minions it touches. Rust: now a feature.". None uses "Greenbull says ...".

#### Power-up overlay

Task T-459 (goal G-009; Game loop architecture, Decisions, "Mission packs"; texts above, "Mission notebook and power-up texts"). Proposals for the playtest unless the board's.

- **When:** a completed mission pauses the run (the clock, the car and everything else stop) and the overlay opens over the dimmed run, with the HUD under it.
- **What it offers:** exactly 2 cards, two different power-ups drawn at random from those the car doesn't own (offered at tier 1) and those it owns below their last tier (offered at their next tier); a power-up at its last tier is never offered. Cards show in the data's order (Rev Charge, Jump, Bouncy Bumpers, Rusty Overcoat). **With only one choice left, one card shows (proposal).** **With none left, the gift is skipped: no overlay and no pause** (power_ups.json's `offer_when_exhausted`, "skip_gift", Drifting, Content, "Driving power-ups: the tiers").
- **Choosing,** as on the level-up screen: A/D or the arrow keys move the highlight, Enter or Space takes the highlighted card, clicking a card's button takes that card. A key already held when the overlay opens takes nothing until let go, and nothing counts during its short build-up (about a third of a second: the dim fades in, the header drops in, the cards slide up one after the other, in stepped frames). Taking a card gives that power-up (tier 1, or the next tier) and the run resumes. Escape does not open the pause screen over it, and the window losing focus does nothing, as on the level-up screen.
- **Never at once with the level-up screen (proposal):** if the gift pack is picked up while the overlay is open, the weapon choice waits and shows as soon as a power-up is taken (the run stays paused between the two); if a mission is completed while the weapon choice is open, the overlay waits and opens as soon as a weapon is taken, before the run moves on. Two missions completed together open one overlay after the other. A new run closes it and drops any waiting gift.
- **Look (placeholder drawn in code, its own look so it reads as tuning the car, not Greenbull's weapons gift; no ribbon, sunburst, emblem or green):** a workshop look in amber and dark steel. The header is a bar with amber and near-black hazard stripes at both ends and a dark steel plate in the middle holding "Mission done: soup up the car" in white Bangers with a dark outline. The cards are dark steel with a 6-pixel amber frame (the weapons cards are cream with Greenbull's green frame); the highlighted card has a thick white frame round it. Each card, top to bottom: the power-up's icon (its file from power_ups.json once the art exists; until then an amber square with the name's initial in near-black), its name in amber, a row of tier pips without text (one per tier: those owned amber, the tier offered white, the rest dark grey), the description for the tier offered in white (the tier's numbers filled in, whole numbers without decimals, for example "Next hop in 2 s"). No button: the whole card is clicked to take it (Decisions, "Gift menu cards are clicked directly"; T-475, the shared `GiftCardClick`), a hover brightens its frame, and the keyboard works as on the level-up screen. Hard pixel edges. How it is built: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/level-up-screen.md`, "Power-up overlay (T-459)". Screenshots, side by side with the weapons gift screen: `art-archive/T-459/screenshots/`.

#### Pause screen

Tasks T-015, T-093, T-095 and T-124. Escape pauses the whole game and shows the pause screen; Escape again resumes from exactly where the car was. The screen is a compact, nearly opaque black strip across the whole width, starting just below the HUD timer and only as tall as its content, over a light dim of the rest of the screen, so as much of the map as possible stays visible. It works in the run (including runs started from the main menu) and in the drift prototype. From top to bottom, centred in the strip:

- **Title:** "Paused", in large white letters.
- **Hint:** "Press Escape to get back to the stream." (texts from T-047).
- **Zoom slider:** "Camera zoom level" (T-093), a slider from 6 to 20 (default 14.4) with its value as a number at the right end. Moving it zooms the view behind the strip at once while the game stays paused, and the value is saved.
- **SFX volume slider, hidden for the MVP** (T-389, board 2026-10-29, 'No sound effects in the MVP'): with every sound effect off (the switch `sfx_enabled` in `game/data/sfx.json`, T-388), the pause screen does not show this row, and the rows below it (music volume, checkboxes, buttons) move up so no gap is left. The slider's code stays, hidden, and the row comes back when the switch is turned on. The music volume slider still shows and works. What follows describes the row when it shows.
- **SFX volume slider** (T-077): "SFX volume" (the board's name), a slider from 0 to 100 with its value as a number at the right end, on its own row directly under the zoom slider, laid out exactly like it (label, slider of the same width, value at the right end). It starts at 0, which is silent, so sound effects are silent until the player turns it up. Moving it changes the volume of every sound effect at once (the sounds' own volumes are in `game/data/sfx.json`; at 100 they play at those volumes, at 0 nothing is heard), and the value is saved between sessions like the zoom.
- **Music volume slider** (T-208): "Music volume", one short plain settings line at the left of the slider, the sibling of "SFX volume" and "Camera zoom level". T-210 uses this text word for word. The slider sits on its own row directly under the SFX volume slider, laid out like it. Built in T-210: it starts from the saved music setting (T-209, starting value 40, a proposal for the playtest), changes the music at once while the music keeps playing under the pause, and is saved between sessions. The strip is one row taller (it ends about 290 pixels from the top at 1152x648, about 325 with the dynamic-camera buttons), still below the HUD timer.
- **HUD size slider** (T-426; Decisions, 'The HUD scales with the window, and a HUD size slider'): "HUD size", one short plain settings line at the left of the slider, the sibling of "Camera zoom level" and "Music volume" (short noun phrase, sentence case, no end punctuation; scored 9 in the style loop). Its value reads as a bare number at the right end like the other sliders, so no value text exists. The text is in `game/data/pause_text.json` (key `hud_size_label`), which the pause screen reads (T-431). Built in T-431: its own row directly under the music volume slider, laid out like it, from 50 to 125 (default 100), resizing the HUD at once while paused (Content, "The HUD scales with the window").
- **HUD layout editor texts** (T-452; Decisions, 'The player can move the HUD's pieces'): four texts in `game/data/pause_text.json`, all scored 8 or more in the style loop: `hud_layout_button` "Edit HUD layout" (the pause screen button that opens the editor; the one capital, HUD, is an acronym), `hud_layout_hint` "Drag a piece to move it." (the one-line hint while editing), `hud_layout_reset` "Reset layout" (puts the default layout back) and `hud_layout_done` "Done" (finishes editing and returns to the pause screen). Plain settings voice, no Greenbull line.
- **Camera checkboxes** (T-124): "Camera smoothing" and "Dynamic camera" side by side, the board's own names (what they do: Drifting, Content, "Camera options"). Each starts from the saved setting, applies at once when switched and is saved. Placeholder look: a light square frame on a dark fill, with a light square inside when checked, so both states show over any ground.
- **Tuning buttons** (T-124), shown only while "Dynamic camera" is on: "Set min zoom" and "Set max zoom", each followed by the stored value as a number (for example 11.0 and 17.0, the proposed starting values). Pressing one stores the zoom slider's current value as the dynamic camera's zoom at a standstill (min) or at top forward speed (max), saves it, and updates the number. The board can move the slider, press a button and resume to try it. They are a temporary tuning tool for the board, plain labels rather than game text, and are removed once the board has settled the values. Placeholder look: a light frame round a dark fill.
- **Restart and Exit** (T-327; Decisions, "Restart and Exit on the pause screen"): two buttons, **"Restart"** and **"Exit"** (the board's own names, word for word), in a row centred at the bottom of the strip under the camera controls, in the strip's placeholder button look. The proposals for the playtest: **no "are you sure?" prompt** (keep it quick; a prompt would need a Narrative Theme ticket for its text, so none is built); ~~**the coins collected so far are kept**, as on any loss (banked into the saved total before the run goes)~~ the run is cancelled: its coins are lost and nothing is saved (board, 2026-10-30; Game loop architecture, Decisions, "Restart, Exit or closing cancels the run", T-416); **no time's up screen and no recap** (T-317 and T-320 are not built yet: Restart and Exit never end the run through `run_ended`, so a screen listening for it never sees them; when the recap is built it must be skipped the same way, by the pause screen's own `restart_pressed` and `exit_pressed` signals doing the leaving, and no run is recorded in the runs list); **keyboard:** the focus starts on Restart when the screen opens, the arrow keys or Tab move between the two and Enter or Space presses (Escape still resumes). In a run started from the level creator (T-239): Restart replays the same level and Exit returns to the creator's level list (both cancel the run: its coins are lost). How it is built: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/pause-screen.md`.
- **Trick list button and panel** (T-386; Decisions, 'A trick list in the pause screen'): a **"Trick list"** button at the left of the Restart and Exit row, its text from `game/data/tutorial_text.json` (`button.trick_list`). Pressing it replaces the strip with a sub-panel in the strip's look, holding the trick list scene and a **"Back"** control. **The trick list (T-491):** on the left the seven tricks as a list (illustration and name; the mouse selects by clicking, the keyboard by moving the focus with the arrow keys); on the right the selected trick shown large: its name, its rule (`trick_rule.<id>`), its **clip with the live key pad** and its **keycap recipe**. The recipe draws each step's keys as keycaps joined with +, the steps joined with an arrow, the tiny note under each step (`trick_recipe.<id>.stepN_note`) and, for a step with no keys, a badge word in capitals (`stepN_badge`); a key where either turn key works carries a small /D tag. Six tricks have a recipe; THREAD THE NEEDLE! shows its clip and rule only. The recipe's structure (the keys per step, the /D marks, which clip each trick shows) is in `game/data/trick_recipes.json`; every word comes from `tutorial_text.json`. Only the selected trick's clip is loaded, and only while the panel is on screen (freed when hidden, T-485's web memory rule). **The live key pad (T-491):** a small W A S D pad in the bottom-right corner of a clip; each key is lit (blush colour, pressed down a little) while the clip's key timeline (`keys_per_frame` in the clip's sheet JSON, T-490) says it is held, in step with the clip's frame. It is one reusable piece (`game/scripts/menu/key_pad.gd`), on the trick list's clip and on slide 2's three clips (slide 1's clip has none). The panel still starts at the strip's top line and fits at 1152 x 648, clear of the HUD timer (`button.back`, same file). The panel is centred, starts at the strip's top line (below the HUD timer and clear of the clock and the viewers panel) and fits at 1152 x 648. The run stays paused throughout. Back returns to the pause screen with its sliders, checkboxes and buttons exactly as they were. **Escape while the panel is open goes back to the pause screen instead of resuming** (a proposal for the playtest; a second Escape then resumes as usual). Keyboard: opening puts the focus on Back, Enter or Space presses it, and going back returns the focus to the Trick list button. How it is built: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/pause-screen.md`.

- **Sliders save on release and on close** (T-427): the zoom, SFX volume and music volume sliders apply their value live while dragged (the view zooms, the bus volume changes at once), but write the settings file only when the drag ends, and once more when the pause screen closes (Escape, Restart, Exit), so a keyboard or click change is not lost. A drag of 20 values makes one write, not 20. The HUD size slider follows the same rule. How it is built: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/pause-screen.md`.

The checkboxes and buttons work with the mouse and the keyboard (Tab to move, Space to switch or press). The strip's dark band runs over the lower part of the car's health bar while paused. How it is built is in `game/docs/hud-and-menus/pause-screen.md`, "Pause screen".

#### Runs list

Text task T-362 (the board's decision: Game loop architecture, Decisions, "The runs list"); the screen is T-364 and reads the text from `game/data/runs_list_text.json` (keys in the file's `_comment`). Every new line scored 8 or more in the style loop. The columns are the recap's stats; the first run's rows read left to right.

| Where | Key | Text |
|---|---|---|
| Main menu button (with Start, Garage, Exit) | `menu_button` | Past streams |
| Screen title | `title` | Past livestreams |
| Column: the day | `column.date` | Stream date |
| Column: how it ended | `column.result` | Result |
| Column: survived | `column.time` | Time survived |
| Column: highest combo | `column.combo` | Peak engagement (reused: recap `heading.combo`) |
| Column: enemies | `column.enemies` | Takedowns (reused: recap `heading.enemies`) |
| Result, win | `result.win` | Kaiju clipped |
| Result, time's up | `result.time_up` | Out of airtime |
| Result, wreck | `result.wreck` | Peak content |
| No saved runs | `empty` | No runs yet, so go drift: the content won't make itself |
| Back to the main menu | `button.back` | Back to menu |
| The X's accessible label | `button.close` | Close (reused: recap `button.close`) |

Proposals for the board to judge: "Peak content" for a wreck is the weakest line (it risks reading like the "Peak engagement" column); "Past livestreams" and "Past streams" could be one word. The empty line is long for a label.

#### Level-up screen

Task T-052 (decisions: Decisions, 2026-10-15). When the player levels up the run pauses and this screen shows over it: a white rounded banner at the top with "Greenbull sent a gift pack!" (rewritten for the rebrand in T-301/T-302: Extended narrative, Decisions, "The rebrand"), and under it the 2 choices the weapons give (Weapons, Content, "The level-up offers") as plain cards side by side, each with a title, a description and its weapon image, and no button: the whole card is clicked (all text approved in T-051). The run behind it is dimmed. An upgrade card shows the text of the tier it would give (the weapon's tier now plus 1); "get the flamethrower" has one text. With only one choice left, one card shows. The look is the comic look of the trick popups and the combo counter: white rounded cards with black borders, black Bangers text with hard pixel edges, none of Greenbull's colours. The highlighted card has a thicker border in the combo counter's yellow with a black outline round it; the first card starts highlighted. A/D or the left and right arrow keys move the highlight, Enter or Space takes the highlighted card, and clicking anywhere on a card takes it (T-474: the cards have no Take it button; a hover brightens the card's frame and a click presses it down by the shared button's 2 pixels, hovering still does not move the highlight; the click area is `GiftCardClick`, `game/scripts/ui/gift_card_click.gd`, reused by the driving power-up overlay in T-475). Only a fresh key press counts: a key held down from driving when the screen opens (or its key-repeat) does nothing until it is let go. Taking a card applies it and resumes the run; when several level-ups are waiting the next one's cards show straight after. Escape does not resume the run or open the pause screen while the choice is open. Hovering a card with the mouse does not move the highlight. (T-141) The screen wears T-140's red and gold art (Visual style, Decisions): cream cards in a gold and red 9-slice frame, the highlighted card in a bright gold frame instead of the yellow ring, the red ribbon with the title lettered between its two gull medallions, the gift box emblem at the ribbon's left end, and a red and gold sunburst behind the cards that turns slowly in steps. The card text wraps at word boundaries on the cream. The screen builds up in 0.54 seconds (0.64 with three cards) in whole-pixel frames of 0.04 seconds, with no smoothing, and it runs while the run is paused: the dim fades in over four frames, the sunburst grows from small with a small overshoot, the ribbon drops in from above with a bounce, the emblem drops just after it, and the cards slide up and settle one after the other, left first. Nothing can be taken or moved while it builds up: keys do nothing (a key pressed then and still held when it ends takes nothing until it is let go, as for a key held at the start), and the cards ignore the mouse. Keyboard and mouse then work as above. The screen opens at the package pickup, so the likes bar's level-up animation normally is over; if both overlap, they play on their own, the screen above the HUD. The numbers are proposals for the board's playtest. (T-173) Every card shows an image of its weapon (Decisions, 2026-10-18) in a 64 x 64 pixel slot centred above the title: the gun (a small gun), the exhaust flamethrower, the neon underglow, the molotovs or the windshield wiper; an upgrade card shows the same weapon's image as its "get" card. The cards grew from 360 x 300 to 360 x 374 pixels so the image does not take the texts' room, and the highlight frame grows with them. Until the art task (T-174) adds the final images, each weapon has a placeholder drawn in code (16 x 16 pixels at 4 screen pixels each, hard-edged, none of Greenbull's colours). The three new weapons' cards use T-171's text. How it is built is in `game/docs/hud-and-menus/level-up-screen.md`, "Level-up screen".

#### Recap screen

Task T-318 (decision: Game loop architecture, Decisions, "Recap screen in the MVP" and "The recap always closes a run"). Every run ends on the recap: a win, the time's up screen's loss and a wreck (the car's last heart). T-320 builds the screen and reads every label from `game/data/recap_text.json` (no text in code); the player leaves it with Continue or the X at the top right, both to the main menu. Each new line scored 8 or more in the style loop (rounds in T-318's Style review). Labels follow Extended narrative, Text rules, kind "label" (sentence case); the board reads them in the morning.

- **Title**, by how the run ended (`title.win`, `title.time_up`, `title.wreck`): "Kaiju sunsetted, record engagement!" (a win), "Time's up, kaiju still trending" (time ran out), "Car wrecked, great content" (a wreck).
- **Section headings** (`heading.*`): "Takedowns" (enemies slain), "Tricks landed" (tricks completed), "Peak engagement" (highest combo), "Weapons used".
- **Buttons** (`button.continue`, `button.close`): "Continue" (the board's word; the loop's own pick was "End stream", 9/10, not used) and "Close" (the X's accessible label).
- **Weapon tier** (`tier`): "Tier {tier}", {tier} being 1 to 8.
- **Enemy names** (`enemy.*`): "Kaiju minion" (new), "The kaiju" (new).
- **Weapon names** (`weapon.*`): "Promo pistol" (new, the gun has no card title), and reused from the level-up cards' titles: "Hot Take Exhaust" (flamethrower), "Neon Underglow", "Hot Drop" (molotov), "Wiper Blade", "Bricks".
- **Trick names** (`trick.*`), all reused word for word from the trick popups: LONG DRIFT!, FULL 360!, ALT DRIFT!, AIR 180!, AIR 360!, HANG TIME!, THREAD THE NEEDLE!.

**The screen (task T-320).** Right after a run ends (after the wreck's 3 seconds on a health loss) the run makes way for the recap, full screen over the main menu's dark background, in the game's comic look: white rounded panels with black borders, black Bangers lettering with hard pixel edges, no generated art. From the top: the **title** for how the run ended in its own panel, with the **X** (a black pixel X on a white rounded square) at the top right; then **Takedowns** (each enemy type killed, its sprite, the first frame of its south-facing sheet, its name and "x{count}", e.g. "x47") beside **Peak engagement** (the board's quick tuning, 2026-10-29: "peak engagement needs to be the max current views number, not a multiplier": the run's peak live viewers, written as the live viewers counter writes it, e.g. "236K" or "1.02M", with the viewers' eye before it, in the counter's look for that number: the viewers colour at the base, then the heat colours, glow and pulse; Live viewers counter, above); then **Tricks landed** (each trick as its plain trick popup, followed by "x{count}", wrapping onto a second row when needed); then **Weapons used** (each weapon the car ended with, its level-up card image, its name and "Tier {tier}"); and **Continue** at the bottom centre. "x{n}" is the HUD's own count form (the weapon icons'). A trick or an enemy with a count of 0 is left out. Proposals for the playtest: a section with nothing to show (no kills, no tricks) is left out; peak engagement always shows (2,500 viewers, the base, with no tricks); a run saved before the peak viewers were kept shows the viewers for its highest combo on the same curve; enemies and tricks are in the text file's order, weapons in the order taken; the panels pop in one after another (the title first) in stepped frames, about 0.7 seconds in all, while Continue and the X work at once; Enter also continues, and the buttons take no keyboard focus, so a key held from driving presses nothing. The screen can show any run's summary, also one read back from the run history, so the runs list (T-364) can reopen a saved run in it. How it is built: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/recap-screen.md`.

Slide 2: the seven tricks in a grid of four columns, each a still illustration (64 x 48 pixels drawn at 3 times, nearest) with its name below, then the two loop lines; until the art tickets' PNGs are in, each shows a code-made placeholder (blue picture, pink arrow). Slide 3: the goal line, the "Don't show again" checkbox and the Start button. Pressing Start sends the checkbox state to the screen flow, which starts the run and, when it is ticked, saves `tutorial_hidden` in the settings. Keys: left/right arrow or A/D move between slides, Enter presses the focused control (proposal). The trick list is its own scene so the pause screen can reuse it. How it is built: `game/docs/hud-and-menus/tutorial-slides.md`.

Proposals for the board to judge: the Start button reads "Go live" (loop score 9) where the board's word is "Start"; swap it in `button.start` if "Start" is wanted, like the main menu. Slide 2's single line failed the loop (card_desc is 90 characters at most; best 7), so it is two lines.

#### The four redrawn slides (T-485)

Decisions, "The tutorial slides are redrawn, with clips of the real car"; the board approved the draft on 2026-11-01. Laid out on a 1280 x 720 stage that scales to the window (centred, nearest-neighbour). Every slide has its kicker (Press Start 2P, cyan, "{n} / 4 · topic" in capitals), its headline (Bangers, 82 px, in capitals, with a pink offset shadow), the left and right arrows (the right one hidden on slide 4, the left one on slide 1), four slide dots (the current one a long bar) and a **Skip** button at the top right (the shared small button) that jumps to slide 4. All the words come from `game/data/tutorial_text.json` (the retired `slide1.controls`, `slide1.drift`, `slide2.chain`, `slide2.gift` and `slide3.goal` are no longer used) and, for the power-up names and the notebook sample lines, `game/data/screen_texts.json`.

- **1, Drive:** the W, A, S, D keycaps in their WASD shape (92 px, the W blush pink), each with its small label (`slide1.key_*`); under them the drift rule `slide1.drift_rule` split on "+" and "=", the W drawn as a pink keycap; right of them the drift clip (`drift`) in a framed 546 x 364 box.
- **2, Tricks bring gift packs:** a chain of four step panels with pink chevrons between: the long drift trick illustration (`art/tutorial/tricks/`, 2x), the HUD's eye icon with a sample viewer count (3x), the HUD's subs icon in a gold sub-goal ring (drawn in code), the gift pack package with four weapon icons from `art/hud/weapon_icons.png`; each with its title and caption (`slide2.step1..4_*`). Under a dashed rule, three clips (`long_drift`, `alt_drift`, `ramp_jump`, 256 x 171 each) with their captions (`trick.extended_drift`, `trick.alternate_drift`, `slide2.clip_ramp`).
- **3, Missions:** the HUD's own notebook page (`MissionPage`, 3x) with a ticked mission line and an open one (sample lines from `screen_texts.json`), the line `slide3.missions`, and the four power-up icons (`art/power_ups/`, 3x) with their names.
- **4, Survive the stream:** the 8-minute run as a timeline bar (cyan to pink, red in the last eighth, the last minute, with a dashed red box), four gift pack icons above it, the times 8:00, 4:00 and 1:00 under it (built from numbers), the kaiju sprite standing at the last minute with its label (`slide4.kaiju`); then the **Go live** button (the shared button with the HUD's LIVE badge) and the **Don't show again** checkbox under it. No hearts, no sentence.
- **Clips:** `game/scripts/menu/clip_player.gd` (`ClipPlayer`) plays them from frame sheets, because Godot does not play GIFs. `python game/tools/gif_to_sheet.py` turns each GIF in `art/tutorial/clips/` into `<name>_sheet.png` (all frames in a grid, 1 GIF pixel = 1 sheet pixel, RGBA) and `<name>_sheet.json` (frame size, columns, and each frame's own duration in milliseconds from the GIF); the player draws the current frame with nearest filtering, loops, loads the sheet when its slide first shows and only runs while visible.
- Keys, Start and "Don't show again" behave as before (only fresh key presses count; Enter on Go live starts the run). Screenshots: `art-archive/T-485/screenshots/`.

#### Tutorial clips (T-483; recordings for the redrawn slides)

Decisions, "The tutorial slides are redrawn, with clips of the real car". Four looping GIFs of the real car (its code and art, driven by scripted inputs) on the drift prototype's plain grid, 480 x 320 pixels, one shared palette, 25 frames a second for the drift clip (camera held still) and 16.7 for the other three (every third physics step, to stay under 1.5 MB), nothing else on screen (no HUD, popups, enemies, city or test room): `game/art/tutorial/clips/drift.gif` (slide 1: zoomed out, the camera held still, the car driving straight, breaking into a drift with W + A, its tyre marks tracing the path from where the drift starts), `long_drift.gif`, `alt_drift.gif` (a forward drift W + A, then a backward one S + A, which counts as ALT DRIFT!) and `ramp_jump.gif` (slide 2: the elevation test scene's ramp, hang time and an air spin in one clip). Each has a record JSON beside it (`<name>.json`: size, frames, seconds, bytes, the tricks and the airtime the run printed). The tutorial slides play them (T-485, "The four redrawn slides"), from frame sheets made by `game/tools/gif_to_sheet.py`.

**More clips and the key timeline (T-490; Decisions, "Each trick shows the keys that make it"):** four more clips, recorded the same way (`game/art/tutorial/clips/`, 480 x 320, 16.7 frames a second, each with its record JSON and its frame sheet): `three_sixty` (FULL 360!: one W + A drift that spins a full circle), `air_three_sixty` (AIR 360!: a fast run at a steeper, taller ramp, `tests/fixtures/data/tutorial_ramp_high.json`, with W + A held in the air at a slightly eased steer, about 1.9 s of air and 370 degrees turned at the base air-turn speed), `airtime` (HANG TIME! alone: the first ramp with W only, 1.12 s in the air, no spin, so no AIR 180! or AIR 360!) and `thread_the_needle` (THREAD THE NEEDLE!: the car drives straight between two paired boulders on the plain grid without touching either, the real `ThreadTheNeedle` watching the line). The recorder checks each take shows its trick (and, for `airtime`, no air spin trick) and prints a problem line otherwise. **The key timeline:** every clip's `<name>_sheet.json` has `keys_per_frame`, one string per sheet frame of the keys the script held (a subset of "WASD" in that order, for example "WA"; "" for none), written by the recorder from the scripted parts (the fixture logs the held keys on every physics step; frame i takes step 3i, or 2i for the drift clip) and copied into the sheet by `gif_to_sheet.py` (a sheet frame that is several merged identical frames takes the keys of its first). The UI's live W A S D pad reads it. The alt drift's timeline is W, W + A, S + A, W (with one frame of just A while the script lets go of W before pressing S). The four older clips' GIFs are the approved ones, unchanged; only their records and sheets gained the timeline.

**Re-recording:** from the repo root, `python game/tools/record_tutorial_clips.py` (needs a real window, not headless; Godot's movie maker, about 15 seconds a clip; `--only NAME ...` records some, `--no-archive` skips copying the take to `art-archive/T-483/takes/`). The fixture scenes are `game/tests/fixtures/tutorial_clip_<name>.tscn` (script `tutorial_clip_demo.gd`: the inputs, the zoom, the camera and the start are exported values in each scene).
